chunks.title: Ephemeral Agents
chunks.heading: Git provider + token broker (S5.1, S5.6)
chunks.body:
## Git provider + token broker (S5.1, S5.6)

Sprint 5 introduces an abstraction over git forges so workers can
clone, push, and open PRs with parent-minted, short-lived tokens
that get revoked on session end.

**Provider interface** (`internal/git/provider.go`):
```
Kind()                                            // "github" | "gitlab"
MintToken(ctx, repo, ttl)  → MintedToken          // short-lived
RevokeToken(ctx, token)                            // best-effort
OpenPR(ctx, PROptions)     → URL                  // pr/mr create
```

**Implementations**:
- `GitHub` — shells out to `gh` CLI. v1 uses the operator's existing
  PAT (`gh auth token`); fine-grained per-spawn tokens via
  `gh api …/installations/.../access_tokens` is a follow-up.
- `GitLab` — stub returning `ErrNotImplemented` until a GitLab repo
  enters the rotation. Schema-level acceptance is already in
  `ProjectProfile.Git.Provider`.

**Token broker** (`internal/auth/token_broker.go`):

```
broker := &auth.TokenBroker{Provider: git.Resolve("github"), Store: …, Audit: …}
rec, _ := broker.MintForWorker(ctx, workerID, "owner/repo", 1*time.Hour)
//  …worker uses rec.Token to clone + push…
broker.RevokeForWorker(ctx, workerID)
broker.SweepOrphans(ctx, agentMgr.ActiveIDs())   // periodic safety net
```

- TTL is capped at `MaxTTL` (default 1h)
- At most one active token per `WorkerID` — a new mint supersedes
  the prior with a best-effort revoke
- `SweepOrphans` removes records whose worker is gone OR whose
  expiry has passed; safe to call concurrently
- `RunSweeper` (S5.5) is the periodic safety net: started as a
  goroutine at daemon boot, runs one sweep immediately to clean up
  anything the previous instance leaked, then ticks every 5 min
  using `agentMgr.ActiveIDs` as the alive-worker set
- `PostSessionPRHook` (S5.4) — when a session bound to an agent
  reaches a terminal state and the project's `git.auto_pr` is
  `true`, the parent pushes the worker's working branch back to
  the project repo (token injected into URL, scrubbed after) and
  opens a PR via the configured `git.Provider`. Best-effort: any
  failure (no token, push denied, OpenPR rate-limited) is logged
  but does not block the session-end callback chain
- Audit log is JSON-per-line for `jq` inspection; every mint /
  revoke / sweep / mint-fail is recorded with worker_id, repo,
  provider, and a short note

chunks.title: Ephemeral Agents
chunks.heading: Memory federation (Sprint 6 in flight)
chunks.body:
## Memory federation (Sprint 6 in flight)

Each spawned worker can read + write the parent's episodic memory
under one of three modes (set per Project Profile):

| Mode | Worker reads | Worker writes | Notes |
|------|--------------|---------------|-------|
| `shared` | parent + own namespace | direct to parent | full bidirectional federation |
| `sync-back` | parent + own namespace | local sqlite, batched POST on session-end | conflict policy: append-only, timestamps win, KG triples merged |
| `ephemeral` | own namespace only | tmpfs/overlay, nothing syncs | useful for read-only audits / one-shots |

**S6.1 — namespace enforcement (shipped):** the SQLite + Postgres
memory tables gain a `namespace` column (default `__global__` to
preserve pre-F10 behaviour). New methods on `internal/memory.Store`:

**S6.2 + S6.4 — bootstrap memory bundle (shipped):**
`BootstrapResponse.Memory` now carries `{Mode, Namespace}` — the
worker reads it on startup and exports `DATAWATCH_MEMORY_MODE` +
`DATAWATCH_MEMORY_NAMESPACE` for the in-container memory client.
Mode `ephemeral` → worker uses local memory only, nothing syncs.
Mode `shared` / `sync-back` → worker uses parent's
`/api/memory/save|search|import` endpoints under the assigned
namespace (HTTP-backed adapter wiring queued as **BL100**).

**S6.7 — pgvector required-or-fallback (shipped):**
New `memory.fallback_sqlite` knob (configurable via every channel —
config.yaml, REST PUT /api/config, MCP `config_set`, comm
`configure memory.fallback_sqlite=true`, CLI via config edit).
Default false. When `memory.backend=postgres` and the connection
fails at startup AND `fallback_sqlite=true`, the daemon logs a
warning and falls back to the SQLite store at `memory.db_path`.
When false (default), Postgres failure disables memory entirely
— matches the existing strict-failure behaviour. Useful for slim
worker images that prefer "always have local memory" over "always
shared with the parent".

**S6.5 — cross-profile sharing (shipped):**
`ProjectProfile.Memory.SharedWith []string` lets a profile opt into
sharing its memory namespace with another. Datawatch enforces
**mutual opt-in** — A only sees B's memory when A.SharedWith
contains B AND B.SharedWith contains A. New helper:

```go
ProjectStore.EffectiveNamespacesFor(name string) []string
```

Returns the union of own + reciprocally-shared namespaces, in
caller order (own first). Defence: single-sided declarations are
silently dropped (no leak when one operator misconfigures their
profile to claim sharing the other never agreed to). Server-side
wiring of this into `/api/memory/search` (so a worker just passes
its `agent_id` and gets the federated namespace set automatically)
is queued as **BL101**.

**S6.3 — sync-back upload protocol (shipped):**
`ExportMemory` JSON now round-trips `wing/room/hall/namespace +
embedding` so a worker's local sqlite write surfaces in the parent's
federated search after upload. New methods:

```go
Store.ExportSince(w io.Writer, namespace string, since time.Time) error
Store.Import(r io.Reader) (int, error)   // honours per-row Namespace
```

Worker flow on session-end (BL100 wires this):
1. `ExportSince(buf, profile.Namespace, sessionStartedAt)`
2. POST buf to `parent.URL + /api/memory/import` with auth header
3. Parent's `Store.Import` deduplicates by content hash + tags rows
   with the worker's namespace; spatial metadata + embeddings flow
   through unchanged.



```go
SaveWithNamespace(ns, projectDir, content, summary, role, sessionID, wing, room, hall, embedding) (int64, error)
SearchInNamespaces([]string{"profile-foo", "__global__"}, queryVec, topK) ([]Memory, error)
```

Existing `Save` / `SaveWithMeta` callers are unchanged — they
default to `__global__` so non-F10 deployments work identically.

Sprint 6 follow-ups will wire the per-Project-Profile namespace
through the bootstrap response, the worker's memory client, and the
sync-back upload path.

chunks.title: Ephemeral Agents
chunks.heading: Post-quantum bootstrap tokens (S5.2)
chunks.body:
## Post-quantum bootstrap tokens (S5.2)

Sprint 3 shipped the F10 spawn flow with a 32-byte hex bootstrap
token: simple, fast, but compromised the moment an attacker reads
the parent's spawn log or sniffs the worker container env.

S5.2 replaces (additively, opt-in) that single secret with a
**structured envelope authenticated by NIST-standardised
post-quantum primitives**:

- **ML-KEM 768** for key encapsulation (Cloudflare CIRCL)
- **ML-DSA 65** for signing (same)

Wire format (delivered as the `token` field on
`POST /api/agents/bootstrap`):

```
<kem-ciphertext-b64> "." <signature-b64>
```

Verify path: parent splits + base64-decodes both halves,
KEM-decapsulates the ciphertext against the keys it retained at
spawn (yields the shared secret), verifies the signature against
the worker's signing public key over the agent_id. Both must
verify; one-without-the-other is rejected. Replay rejection is
inherent — KEM encapsulation is randomised, so each token instance
is unique even for the same (agent_id, keypair) pair.

`internal/agents/pqc_token.go` exposes:

- `GeneratePQCKeys()` — fresh KEM + signing keypairs per spawn
- `MakePQCBootstrapToken(agentID, keys)` — worker side
- `VerifyPQCBootstrapToken(envelope, agentID, keys)` — parent side

Shipped as opt-in primitives; wiring into the spawn driver +
`ConsumeBootstrap` is tracked as **BL95** so deployments adopt
incrementally and the existing UUID flow keeps working until the
operator flips `agents.pqc_bootstrap=true`.

chunks.title: Ephemeral Agents
chunks.heading: Production hardening (Sprint 8 in flight)
chunks.body:
## Production hardening (Sprint 8 in flight)

**S8.5 — Cloud Foundry driver placeholder (shipped):**
`agents.CFDriver` is a typed stub returning `ErrCFNotImplemented`
on every method. The schema-level `kind: cf` Cluster Profile
acceptance has been there since Sprint 2; this commit makes
spawning against `kind=cf` fail fast with a clear error pointing
operators at S8.5 in the F10 plan rather than a generic
"no driver registered" message. Concrete impl (shell-out to `cf`
CLI) is future work.

**S8.4 — Agent audit trail (shipped):**
- `agents.AuditEvent{At, Event, AgentID, Project, Cluster, State,
  Note, Extra}` — single shape across every emission point
- `agents.Auditor` interface (Append) — implementations:
    - `MemoryAuditor` for tests + temporary inspection (Recent/All)
    - `FileAuditor` for production (JSON-lines or CEF format)
- `Manager.Auditor` field (optional) — when set, emits on
  `spawn` / `spawn_fail` / `result` / `terminate`
- **Two output formats** per [AGENT.md → Audit Logging Rule](../AGENT.md):
    1. JSON-lines (`FormatJSONLines`) — `jq`-friendly default for in-
       house pipelines + the datawatch web UI
    2. CEF (`FormatCEF`) — ArcSight Common Event Format for SIEM
       forwarding (Splunk, QRadar, ArcSight, Sentinel, Chronicle).
       SignatureID + severity assignments inline in
       `internal/agents/audit.go`'s `cefSignature` table.
- `FormatCEFLine(ev)` produces the SIEM-ready single-line form
  with proper header (`|` + `\`) and extension (`=` + `\` + `\n` +
  `\r`) escaping per the CEF spec — escape coverage is treated as
  security-critical (bad escapes break SIEM parsing or let an
  attacker inject synthetic events)
- REST surface (GET `/api/agents/audit` + filters) wires as
  **BL107**

Sibling system: `internal/auth.TokenBroker` already has its own
JSON-lines audit (S5.1) covering token mint/revoke/sweep — same
shape, mirrored CEF support tracked as a follow-up.

**S8.1 — Secrets pluggability (shipped):**
New `internal/secrets` package with `Provider` interface (Get/Put)
+ five backends:

- `File` (default) — 0600 atomic file under `~/.datawatch/secrets/`
  (operator-overridable). Path-traversal rejected. Trims trailing
  newlines so editor-saved files Just Work.
- `EnvVar` — process env, prefix-able. Empty value = `ErrNotFound`
  (security hardening — empty secret is never valid). Slash-keys
  rejected.
- `K8sSecret`, `Vault`, `CSI` — typed stubs returning
  `ErrNotImplemented` with the operator-requested kind in the
  error so operators see exactly which backend is missing.

`secrets.Resolve(kind, baseDir)` dispatches to the matching impl;
unknown kind returns the stub-with-named-kind. Wiring into
`ClusterProfile.CredsRef` resolution + token broker storage is
queued as **BL111** so operators can back the existing
`creds_ref.provider` field with whichever backend matches their
infrastructure (Vault for prod, File for dev, EnvVar for K8s when
secrets are projected as env).

**S8.3 — Multi-cluster (shipped):**
New `ProjectProfile.DefaultClusterProfile` lets a project pin its
preferred cluster so spawn requests can omit `cluster_profile` and
fall back to the default. Explicit `cluster_profile` on the spawn
request always wins (operator override). Empty default + no
override produces a clear error pointing at the field. Operators
manage multiple clusters by creating one `ClusterProfile` per
(gcp/aws/on-prem/local); kubectl context caching is already
handled by the K8s driver's shell-out semantics.

**S8.6 — Idle-timeout enforcement (shipped):**
`ProjectProfile.IdleTimeout` (already in schema since Sprint 2)
finally has runtime teeth. New `Manager.NoteActivity(agentID)`
bumps a per-agent `LastActivityAt` timestamp; new
`Manager.ReapIdle(ctx, now)` walks active agents and `Terminate()`s
any whose profile timeout has elapsed since last activity (falls
back to `CreatedAt` floor when no activity recorded). Reap emits
an `idle_reap` audit event with the actual idle duration. Per-call
`now` parameter keeps the reaper deterministic for tests; the
production sweeper goroutine wiring is **BL108**. `IdleTimeout=0`
disables the policy entirely.

`ConsumeBootstrap` + `RecordResult` both bump `LastActivityAt` as
sure-fire activity signals. BL108 will thread the bump into the
agent reverse proxy / memory proxy / peer broker / MCP call paths
so every real worker→parent interaction counts as activity.

**S8.7 — Crash policy field (shipped):**
New `ProjectProfile.OnCrash` enum (default = empty = `fail_parent`).
Three values:

- `fail_parent` (default + safest) — surface the failure to the
  parent session, do not respawn
- `respawn_once` — single retry with the same task; further failures
  revert to fail_parent semantics
- `respawn_with_backoff` — exponential backoff (1m, 2m, 4m, …,
  capped at 30m) until manual operator intervention

Validation enforced at profile load + via every channel. Runtime
enforcement (Manager loop reacting to Failed transitions + retry
state) is queued as **BL106**.

**BL114 — Cluster-shared NFS / PVC / HostPath volumes (shipped):**
New `ClusterProfile.SharedVolumes []SharedVolume` field. Each entry
must set exactly one of `host_path | nfs | pvc`; `read_only`
defaults to false but the safety pattern is to start read-only and
flip rw only after verifying the right workers see the right share.

- Docker driver: `-v <host_path>:<mount_path>[:ro]` for HostPath
  entries only. NFS + PVC are silently skipped — the operator pre-
  mounts the NFS share on the host at any path of their choosing
  and references that path via HostPath. **No `/mnt/...` prefix is
  inferred** (per AGENT.md "no hard-coded configurations").
- K8s driver: renders `volumes` + `volumeMounts` blocks for NFS,
  PVC, and HostPath sources.

Doc lives in `docs/registry-and-secrets.md` §6 with example schemas
using IANA TEST-NET addresses.

**BL112 — Service-mode reconciler (shipped):**
S8.2 shipped the `Mode` field + idle-reaper exemption for service
workers; BL112 adds the parent-restart recovery so they survive a
control-plane restart.

- New `Driver.Discovery` capability interface + `DiscoveredInstance`
  metadata struct. Drivers without label discovery return
  `ErrDiscoveryUnsupported` and are skipped.
- Docker driver: `docker ps --filter label=…` then `docker inspect`
  for labels + IP.
- K8s driver: `kubectl --context=<ctx> -n <ns> get pods -l <selector> -o json`
  per cluster registered in the store.
- Spawn now also injects `datawatch.branch` + `datawatch.parent_agent_id`
  labels alongside the existing role/agent_id/project/cluster labels
  so the reconciler can rebuild the in-memory record verbatim.
- `Manager.ReconcileServiceMode(ctx)` runs at boot from main:
  per-cluster scan, profiles with `Mode="service"` are reattached
  with `State=Ready`, ephemerals + missing-profile rows are
  reported as orphans for operator review (operator-prune is the
  follow-up).

**BL96 — Wake-up stack L4/L5 + per-agent L0 overlay (shipped):**
The 4-layer (L0..L3) wake-up stack was designed for single-host
sessions. F10 spawned children + sibling workers need two more
layers + per-agent identity:

- `Layers.L0ForAgent(id)` — overlays `<data_dir>/agents/<id>/identity.txt`
  when present; falls back to the host `identity.txt`. Lets the
  validator agent introduce itself as "I am the validator for spawn X"
  without affecting the host's own identity.
- `Layers.L4(parentNamespace, maxChars)` — pulls the parent agent's
  recent working context via the BL101 namespace search so a spawned
  child doesn't re-derive what the parent already knows.
- `Layers.L5(selfID, parentAgentID)` — lists sibling workers via a
  new `PeerLister` interface (wired in main from `agents.Manager`).
  Self is filtered out; non-siblings are filtered out. Returns ""
  when no PeerLister is wired (back-compat).
- `Layers.WakeUpContextForAgent(self, parent, ns, projectDir)` —
  composes L0+L1+L4+L5 for a spawned child. Top-level spawns (no
  parent agent / namespace) degrade to the host wake-up.

The post-compaction recall rule in AGENT.md now references all six
layers (L0..L5) so an AI session continuing after a context
compaction knows which layers to walk.

**BL100 — Worker memory client for shared / sync-back (shipped):**
S6.2 shipped the bootstrap `BootstrapMemory` bundle (mode +
namespace) and `DATAWATCH_MEMORY_MODE` / `DATAWATCH_MEMORY_NAMESPACE`
env. BL100 ships the worker-side HTTP client that uses them:

- `memory.NewHTTPClientFromEnv()` returns nil for `ephemeral` /
  unset modes (worker keeps its own local store)
- `Remember(ctx, projectDir, content, role, sessionID)` — shared
  mode hits the parent synchronously; sync-back buffers and flushes
  via `Flush(ctx)` (re-queues unflushed entries on partial failure)
- `Search(ctx, query)` — round-trips to `/api/memory/search`; when
  `Profile` is set it auto-uses BL101's cross-profile namespace
  expansion (workers query peer-shared memory without knowing
  raw namespace strings)
- `QueuedLen()` for tests + UI badges
- Nil receiver is safe on every method so worker code can call
  through without checking

Worker images adopt this in their session-start hook:
```go
mc := memory.NewHTTPClientFromEnv()
defer func() { _, _ = mc.Flush(ctx) }()
```

**BL109 — Auto-wire MCP into every spawned LLM session (shipped):**
Until now MCP wiring only fired for claude-code (via the bespoke
`claude mcp add` shell-out). BL109 generalises so every backend that
honours the `modelcontextprotocol/spec` `.mcp.json` discovery file
gets the datawatch MCP server pre-wired:

- New `channel.WriteProjectMCPConfig(projectDir, channelJSPath, env)`
  writes (and idempotently rewrites) `<projectDir>/.mcp.json` with
  a single `datawatch` server entry; existing operator-added entries
  under other names are preserved.
- The session pre-launch hook runs the writer for every backend,
  then keeps the existing claude-code-specific registration path
  alongside it.
- `channel.NodePath` now honours `DATAWATCH_NODE_BIN` so operators
  on hosts where node isn't on the daemon's PATH (and tests) can
  point it explicitly.

Backends that don't honour `.mcp.json` (aider's `--mcp-config` flag,
others) get a per-backend writer in the BL109-followups; the writer
registry is the extension point.

**BL111 — Secrets provider wired into CredsRef (shipped):**
S8.1 shipped `secrets.Provider` (File / EnvVar concrete + K8sSecret /
Vault / CSI stubs). BL111 wires usage so a `ClusterProfile.CredsRef`
goes through the operator-configured backend rather than being
treated as a literal filesystem path:

- `agents.secrets_provider` config knob (default `file`)
- `agents.secrets_base_dir` config knob (default `<data_dir>/secrets`
  for the file provider; ignored by env/vault/k8s-secret/csi)
- `Manager.SecretsProvider` field — set in main via
  `secrets.Resolve(cfg.Agents.SecretsProvider, baseDir)`
- `Manager.ResolveCreds(ref)` helper: empty key → no-op, nil
  provider → literal-key fallback (so legacy callers like
  kubeconfig-path resolution keep working unchanged), stub
  providers bubble `secrets.ErrNotImplemented`

The token broker integration (Vault-backed mint storage) is filed
as a follow-up so the existing `tokens.json` file isn't pulled out
from under in-flight workers when an operator flips the provider.

**BL110 — MCP self-config permission gate + CLI parity (shipped):**
The `config_set` MCP tool now refuses to write unless the operator
has flipped `mcp.allow_self_config: true` in `~/.datawatch/config.yaml`
(bootstrap-protected — the gate cannot be opened via the gate
itself). When allowed, every mutation is recorded to stderr and to
`mcp.self_config_audit_path` (default
`<data_dir>/audit/config-self-modify.jsonl`) as JSON-lines so
operators can review what an AI session changed.

Closing the every-channel parity loop, two new CLI commands ship
alongside the gate:

- `datawatch config set <key> <value>` — talks to the running
  daemon's `PUT /api/config`; values are sent raw first then
  quoted-as-string on retry so booleans/numbers round-trip without
  manual JSON-escaping
- `datawatch config get <key>` — fetches `/api/config` and walks
  dotted keys (`agents.image_tag`, `mcp.allow_self_config`, …)

This unlocks the BL113 self-bootstrap path: an in-cluster AI
session can now rotate its own image tag, idle-timeout, peer-
broker cap, etc. — under operator-approved + auditable conditions.

**BL102 — Worker comm-channel proxy-send (shipped):**
S7.7 shipped the bootstrap `Comm.Channels` list + `DATAWATCH_COMM_INHERIT`
env so workers know which channels are active on the parent. BL102
wires the parent-side endpoint they POST to:

- `POST /api/proxy/comm/{channel}/send` body `{recipient?, message}`
  — recipient defaults to the parent's per-channel
  default (group ID, chat ID, room) when omitted; the parent looks
  the channel name up in the registry installed at startup and calls
  `backend.Send(recipient, message)`.

Status codes:
- 200 + `{status: "sent", channel, backend}` on success
- 404 when channel isn't active on this parent
- 503 when no comm backends were registered
- 502 when the backend's Send returns an error
- 400 on missing message / no recipient + no default

main.go now declares `commBackends := map[string]messaging.Backend{}`
populated inside `newRouter` (one entry per backend constructed) and
hands the map to the server via `SetCommBackends`. Worker-side
outbound helper (the env+retry shape) lands alongside BL100.

**BL104 — Peer broker REST proxy (shipped):**
S7.6 shipped the in-process `PeerBroker`. BL104 wires the parent-
side REST surface so workers can talk to each other without bypassing
the parent's trust boundary:

- `POST /api/agents/peer/send` body `{from, to[], topic, body}` —
  delivers to each recipient's per-agent inbox; sender authorization
  (`AllowPeerMessaging` on the sender's profile) enforced inside
  `broker.Send`. Returns `{delivered, dropped[]}`.
- `GET /api/agents/peer/inbox?id=<recipient>&peek=0|1` — returns
  the recipient's queue; `peek=0` (default) drains, `peek=1` is
  non-destructive.

The broker is wired in main with `agentMgr` + the default 100-message
inbox cap. Worker-side outbound helper lands alongside BL100 (the
HTTP memory client uses the same retry/auth shape).

**BL107 — Agent audit trail query (shipped):**
S8.4 shipped the `Auditor` interface + Manager emissions. BL107
wires the read path. Operators set `agents.audit_path` (default
`<data_dir>/audit/agents.jsonl`; `-` disables) and optional
`agents.audit_format_cef` (default false → JSON-lines so the REST
query handler can read it back). The new
`agents.ReadEvents(path, filter, limit)` parses JSON-lines; CEF
files are off-limits (operators query their SIEM instead). Surfaces
per the every-channel rule:

- REST: `GET /api/agents/audit?event=&agent_id=&project=&limit=`
- MCP: `agent_audit` tool (same params)
- comm: `agent audit [<agent-id>]` — pretty-printed last 20
- CLI follow-up: deferred (operator can curl the REST endpoint)

A Settings UI "Agents card" surface remains a UI follow-up; the
data path is in place.

**BL101 — Cross-profile memory namespace expansion (shipped):**
S6.5 shipped `ProjectStore.EffectiveNamespacesFor` returning the
mutual-opt-in namespace union for a given profile. BL101 wires it
into `GET /api/memory/search`: when the caller passes
`?profile=<name>` (or `?agent_id=<id>` — the agent's profile is
looked up via `agentMgr.Get`), the handler resolves the effective
namespace set and calls a new `MemoryAPI.SearchInNamespaces` instead
of plain `Search`. The underlying `Retriever.RecallInNamespaces`
embeds the query and uses a new optional `NamespacedBackend`
capability interface (SQLite `Store` implements; the Postgres path
returns `ErrNamespaceUnsupported` until the matching pgvector query
lands). Workers can query peer-shared memory without knowing the
peer's raw namespace string.

**BL106 — Runtime OnCrash enforcement (shipped):**
S8.7 shipped the `OnCrash` field + validation. BL106 wires the
runtime response: `Manager.HandleCrash(ctx, agent)` is called on the
spawn-failure path and dispatches to either `respawnOnce` (single
retry honoured per-(project, branch, parent) tuple) or
`respawnWithBackoff` (immediate first retry; subsequent crashes
deferred 1m → 2m → 4m → … capped at 30m). `Manager.ResetCrashRetries`
clears the per-key counter when an operator manually intervenes.
Crash detection from polled state transitions (Failed observed
outside of Spawn) is the BL112-adjacent reconciler that walks
labelled containers/Pods.

**BL95 — PQC bootstrap envelope wiring (shipped):**
S5.2 shipped the PQC primitives (ML-KEM 768 + ML-DSA 65) as opt-in
building blocks. BL95 wires them into the spawn → bootstrap path:
operators set `agents.pqc_bootstrap: true`; `Manager.Spawn` mints a
fresh keypair into `Agent.PQCKeys`; the Docker + K8s drivers inject
`DATAWATCH_PQC_MODE`/`_KEM_PRIV`/`_KEM_PUB`/`_SIGN_PRIV` env vars;
`Manager.ConsumeBootstrap` accepts a PQC envelope (`<b64-ct>.<b64-sig>`)
or the legacy UUID side-by-side, so partial rollouts (PQC-aware
parent + older worker image) keep bootstrapping. Both forms are
single-use; the keys are zeroed on consume alongside the UUID.

**BL108 — Idle-reaper sweeper goroutine (shipped):**
S8.6 shipped the `Manager.NoteActivity` + `ReapIdle` primitives.
BL108 wires the periodic loop: `Manager.RunIdleReaper(ctx, interval)`
launches a background goroutine that calls `ReapIdle` on the
configured cadence (default 60s, clamped to 10s minimum). Operators
control the cadence via `agents.idle_reaper_interval_seconds`
(default 0 = 60s; negative = disabled). The reaper short-circuits
when no Project Profile sets a non-zero `idle_timeout`, so the cost
in profiles that don't opt in is a single map walk per tick.

**BL92 / BL93 / BL94 — Orphan session reconciliation (shipped):**
Three small backlog items shipped together because they address one
problem: session directories on disk that don't appear in the
`sessions.json` registry (observed with session `cdbb`).

- **BL92 — Write-through registry**: `Store.Save` already flushed
  synchronously; added explicit `Flush()` API for external reconcilers
  + `TestStore_Save_WriteThrough` regression test pinning the contract.
- **BL93 — Startup reconciler**: new `Manager.ReconcileSessions(autoImport)`
  walks `<data_dir>/sessions/<id>/session.json` and reports orphans.
  Main daemon runs it on boot, gated by new `session.reconcile_on_startup`
  config knob (default false → dry-run + log; opt-in for auto-import).
- **BL94 — Manual import**: `Manager.ImportSessionDir(dir)` is the
  single-dir entry point.

Per the every-channel rule, both BL93 and BL94 are exposed via REST
(`POST /api/sessions/reconcile`, `POST /api/sessions/import`), MCP
(`session_reconcile`, `session_import`), CLI (`datawatch session
reconcile [--apply]`, `datawatch session import <dir-or-id>`), and
comm channels (`session reconcile [apply]`, `session import <dir|id>`).

**S8.2 — Service-mode workers (shipped):**
New `ProjectProfile.Mode` enum: `ephemeral` (default) or `service`.
Ephemeral workers terminate when their session ends or after the
S8.6 idle window. Service workers are long-lived: the idle reaper
in `Manager.ReapIdle` walks every active agent and short-circuits
when `project.Mode == "service"`, leaving them running until an
operator issues an explicit terminate. Validation is case-sensitive
and enforced at profile load + via every channel. Reattaching
service workers after a parent restart (walking labelled containers/
Pods + reconstructing the in-memory record) is queued as **BL112**.

chunks.heading: Pointing datawatch at *your* registry / cluster / git account
chunks.body:
## Pointing datawatch at *your* registry / cluster / git account

Datawatch ships zero hard-coded production hosts — every registry,
kubectl context, and git credential is operator-configured. See
[**docs/registry-and-secrets.md**](registry-and-secrets.md) for the
full walkthrough: build-time `REGISTRY` overrides, `agents.image_prefix`
config knob (settable via REST/MCP/CLI/comm/YAML), per-cluster
`image_registry` override, Helm chart `image.registry` (no default —
must be set), kubectl context resolution (`~/.kube/config` or in-
cluster ServiceAccount), `gh auth login` for git tokens, secrets
handling (gitignored files + Helm Secret patterns + SealedSecret
recommendation), and audit recipes to verify nothing leaks.

chunks.title: Ephemeral Agents
chunks.heading: Helm chart for the parent (S4.4)
chunks.body:
## Helm chart for the parent (S4.4)

`charts/datawatch/` packages the datawatch parent for in-cluster
deploys. Quickstart:

```sh
helm install dw ./charts/datawatch -n datawatch --create-namespace \
  --set image.tag=v2.4.5 \
  --set publicURL=http://datawatch.datawatch.svc.cluster.local:8080
```

The chart provisions a Deployment (replicas pinned to 1 for v1), a
ClusterIP Service, a ConfigMap for `config.yaml`, optional Secret
for `apiToken`/`postgres.url`/TLS, optional PVC for state, and a
namespace-scoped Role + RoleBinding so the parent's K8sDriver can
create + delete worker Pods in its own namespace. See
`charts/datawatch/README.md` for the full values reference.

chunks.title: Ephemeral Agents
chunks.heading: Multi-agent orchestration (Sprint 7 in flight)
chunks.body:
## Multi-agent orchestration (Sprint 7 in flight)

Sprint 7 turns spawned workers from "one-shot helpers" into a
coordinated orchestration layer. Stories shipped so far:

**S7.3 — workspace lock (shipped):** `Manager.Spawn` rejects a
request that would put two active workers on the same
`(project_profile, branch)` tuple. Concurrent workers on the same
workspace would race each other's git pushes — clean refusal at
spawn time is the cheapest fix. Branch defaults to the profile's
`git.branch` when not supplied; pass `branch` on the spawn
request for distinct workspaces. Lock auto-releases on Terminate
(Stopped/Failed agents are excluded from the lock check).

**S7.1 — orchestrator core (shipped):**
`agents.Orchestrator.Run(ctx, plan)` walks an `OrchestratorPlan` of
`OrchestratorNode{ID, ProjectProfile, ClusterProfile, Task,
Branch, DependsOn[]}`. Nodes spawn when every upstream node reaches
`NodeDone`; downstream cascades to `NodeSkipped` on failure.
Concurrency capped at `MaxConcurrent` (default 4) on top of the
existing per-cluster workspace lock + per-parent recursion budget.
Cycle detection runs up-front via DFS; missing deps + duplicate
IDs + missing required fields all rejected before any spawn fires.
Returns a `PlanRun{Nodes: map[id]*NodeRun{State, AgentID, Result,
Error, StartedAt, FinishedAt}, StartedAt, FinishedAt}` for caller
inspection. F15 `pipelines.Executor` wiring is **BL105**.

**S7.2 — fan-in result aggregation (shipped):**
New endpoint `POST /api/agents/{id}/result` accepts a structured
`AgentResult{Status, Summary, Artifacts}`. Stored on the Agent
record; visible via `GET /api/agents/{id}` JSON. The orchestrator
reads `Result.Status == "ok"` to advance the DAG; non-ok / no
report after agent terminate cascades downstream as `NodeFailed`.

**S7.6 — peer-to-peer messaging (shipped):**
New `ProjectProfile.AllowPeerMessaging bool` (default false; opt-in
per profile via every channel). New `agents.PeerBroker` provides
in-process per-recipient inboxes with capacity caps + sender-profile
authorisation:

```go
broker := NewPeerBroker(agentMgr, 100)         // maxInbox=100
delivered, dropped, err := broker.Send(senderID, []string{recipID}, "topic", "body")
inbox := broker.Drain(recipID)                  // pulls + clears
snap  := broker.Peek(recipID)                   // pulls without clearing
```

Workers don't talk to each other directly — every message routes
through the parent's broker, which:
- enforces sender's `AllowPeerMessaging` (rejects when false)
- skips recipients whose agent is unknown or in
  Stopped/Failed state (returned in `dropped` list for partial-
  fanout handling)
- bounds each recipient's queue at `maxInbox` (overflow drops with
  the rest)
- snapshots sender's profile at spawn time — operator can't yank
  P2P out from under a running worker

The HTTP/WS surface (`POST /api/agents/{from}/peer/send` +
`GET /api/proxy/agent/{id}/peer/inbox`) + worker-side outbound
helper are queued as **BL104**. The broker is also the foundation
for Sprint 7's orchestrator (S7.1) — the orchestrator agent uses
this same routing layer to address its workers.

**S7.5 — validation orchestrator trigger (shipped):**
New `ProjectProfile.AutoValidate bool` (default false) +
`ValidateProfile string` (default "validator"). When a worker
session reaches a terminal state and AutoValidate is true, the
parent spawns a small read-only validator agent against the named
profile, on the same Cluster Profile as the worker. Branch is
auto-derived (`validate-{agent[:8]}-{unix}`) so it never collides
with the worker's branch under the workspace lock. The validator's
actual image + check logic (PR diff sanity, declared-task vs
observed work, memory writes) is queued as **BL103** — this commit
ships only the trigger.

**S7.7 — comm-channel inheritance (shipped):**
New `ProjectProfile.CommInheritance []string` lists parent
messaging-backend names the worker should route alerts through
(e.g. `["signal", "telegram"]`). The bootstrap response carries the
list under `BootstrapResponse.Comm.Channels`; `ApplyBootstrapEnv`
exports it as `DATAWATCH_COMM_INHERIT` (CSV) for the worker
daemon's outbound alert path. Empty list = no inheritance (worker's
alerts stay local). The actual proxy-send endpoint
(`/api/proxy/comm/{channel}/send`) + worker outbound wiring is
queued as **BL102** so credentials never leave the parent.

**S7.4 — recursion gates (shipped):** when `SpawnRequest.ParentAgentID`
is set (recursive child spawn from a worker), the Manager enforces
the parent agent's profile budgets:

- `allow_spawn_children` must be `true` (default false — explicit
  opt-in)
- `spawn_budget_total` caps lifetime children per parent (0 = no cap)
- `spawn_budget_per_minute` caps recent children per parent (0 = no cap)

All three fields live on the existing `ProjectProfile` (S2 schema)
and are configurable via every channel. Top-level operator-initiated
spawns (no `ParentAgentID`) bypass the recursion gates entirely —
gates apply only to recursive children.

chunks.heading: End-to-end smoke
chunks.body:
## End-to-end smoke

Two parallel scripts exercise the Docker and K8s drivers against a
running parent daemon. Both walk the same REST chain: profile
create → agent spawn → agent get → bootstrap token validation →
agent terminate → profile cleanup. Default image is
`busybox:latest` (placeholder — the container/Pod just needs to
exist for Terminate to reap). Set `RUN_BOOTSTRAP=1` with a real
worker image to also assert `state=ready` after bootstrap.

```
tests/integration/spawn_docker.sh [BASE_URL]   # kind=docker
tests/integration/spawn_k8s.sh    [BASE_URL]   # kind=k8s — honours
                                                 KUBE_CONTEXT + NAMESPACE
```

chunks.title: Ephemeral Agents
chunks.heading: Security notes
chunks.body:
## Security notes

* **Bootstrap token** — 32-byte hex, minted at spawn, never logged,
  never emitted in JSON snapshots (json:"-" + `cloneAgent` zeros it),
  burned on first consume. Sprint 5 wraps it in post-quantum
  signature/encryption.
* **Container labels** — every spawned container gets
  `datawatch.role=agent-worker` + `datawatch.agent_id=<id>` so the
  Sprint 7 reconciler can find our workers even if in-memory state
  is lost (e.g. parent daemon restart).
* **Image prefix / pull secret** — per-cluster override on
  `ClusterProfile.image_registry` + `image_pull_secret` lets the same
  Project Profile pull from harbor in prod and localhost:5000 in dev.
* **TLS pin (S4.3)** — when the parent has TLS enabled, it computes
  the SHA-256 fingerprint of its leaf cert at startup and injects it
  into every spawned container as `DATAWATCH_PARENT_CERT_FINGERPRINT`.
  The worker's bootstrap client pins to that fingerprint and refuses
  any other cert (no fallback to a system trust store, no TOFU). The
  parent's cert is also served at `GET /api/agents/ca.pem` for
  operator setup and `ClusterProfile.trusted_cas[]` ConfigMap
  projection. When the parent has no TLS cert configured, workers
  fall back to `InsecureSkipVerify` — explicit dev/legacy mode,
  logged as a warning.

Feature-access table: [api/autonomous.md](api/autonomous.md#shared-tag-registry) |

| `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_tags` | `autonomous_prd_set_tags` | Complete | body `{tag_ids[], primary_tag_id?}`, MCP args `tag_ids_json` and `primary_tag_id`; replaces the list (empty clears), and `primary_tag_id` alone keeps the tags |
| `GET /api/autonomous/attention` | `autonomous_attention_list` | Complete | the attention group `{statuses, items}`: Automata in the attention statuses (blocked, needs_review, paused) plus those with a task held for review; read-only |
| `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_llm` | `autonomous_prd_set_llm` | Complete | Set the PRD's worker LLM fields; OMITTED fields stay unchanged, an empty value clears that field (falls back to global) |
| `GET /api/autonomous/lane-fill` | `autonomous_lane_fill_status` | Complete | the lane fill status: `mode`, `last_poll_at`, `lanes[]`, `queued_eligible`, `evidence`, `decisions[]` (newest first) and `alerts[]`; query `limit` (1 to 1000, default 50; 400 outside that range); needs the autonomous read capability; CLI `datawatch autonomous lane-fill [--limit N] [--json]`, comm `autonomous lane-fill [limit]` |
| `GET /api/autonomous/triage` | `autonomous_triage` | Complete | the triage records: `records[]` newest first + `alert_minutes`; query `automation_id`, `prd_id`, `status` (`failed`, `blocked`; case-sensitive, 400 otherwise); 403 without the autonomous read capability, 503 with the manager down; an empty match is `records: []`, not an error. CLI `datawatch autonomous triage [--automation <id>] [--prd <id>] [--status failed\|blocked] [--json]`, comm `autonomous triage [automation-id]` (one optional positional argument, the automation id) |
| `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_lane_preference` | `autonomous_prd_set_lane_preference` | Complete | body `{lane_preference}`: `gpu`, `claude` or `any` (empty = any); 400 on an unknown value, 404 on an unknown id; CLI `datawatch autonomous prd-set-lane-preference <id> <gpu\|claude\|any>`, comm `autonomous set-lane-preference <prd-id> <gpu\|claude\|any>` |
| `GET /api/autonomous/progress` | `autonomous_progress` | Complete | the progress metrics object; query `automation_id`, `tag_id`, `since`, `until` (dates, `YYYY-MM-DD`; `until` includes the whole day); a missing backlog file gives `backlog_available: false`; 400 on a bad date or `until` before `since`; needs the autonomous read capability |
| `GET /api/autonomous/progress/trend` | `autonomous_progress_trend` | Complete | `{days, points[], direction}` from the saved daily snapshots; query `days` (1 to 365, default 30; 400 outside that range); empty `points` and `direction: unknown` without snapshots; needs the autonomous read capability |
| `GET /api/capacity` | `capacity_status` | Complete | admission ledger: pools, leases, wait queue; each `llm:*` pool carries `effective_max_inflight` (cap admitted against) + `inflight_source` (`explicit` | `plan_tier` | `kind`); response also carries `patterns_version`, `patterns_stale` and usage-backoff `claude_cli_version`; it also carries a `budgets` array (see Per-LLM dollar budget); a `tasks` object lists `waiting` (task, `cause`, plain `reason`, `since`, optional `resets_at`, `holder`) and `running` (task, `pools`, `node`, `session_id`, `note`) tasks, both always arrays, narrowed by `?prd_id=`; each `backoff` entry carries `reset_known` (false when no reset time was named and `until` is the maximum back-off). CLI `datawatch capacity` and comm `capacity` print the queued reasons and holdings; each `node:*` pool may carry a `usage` object (model probe `state` — `ok` | `unreachable` | `pending` | `no_data`, `checked_at`, optional `error`, `models_supported`, `models[]` with loaded model name/size/expiry, `gpu[]` with utilisation and memory) and those surfaces print one line per loaded model and GPU, or a state line such as `checking...` / `unreachable: <reason>` |
| `GET /api/capacity/admission` | `capacity_admission` | Complete | read-only admission query: `backend` (or `llm`), `node`, `model`, `role` (`worker`, `verifier`, `planner`, `interactive`), `priority`, `prd_id`; resolves the same host, `llm:*` and `node:*` pools a real start uses and returns `kind` (`admit` \| `queued` \| `alternate_available`), `queue_position`, `reason`, `resets_at`, `alternates`; takes no lease and changes no state; same auth as `GET /api/capacity`. CLI `datawatch capacity admission --backend X [--node N --model M --role R --priority P] [--json]`; comm `capacity admission <backend> [node] [model]` |
| `PUT /api/compute/nodes/{name}` (`max_concurrent_sessions`) | `compute_node_update` / `compute_node_add` | Complete | per-node cap on autonomous sessions |
| `PUT /api/compute/nodes/{name}` (`session_slots`), `GET /api/compute/nodes/{name}/detail` (`derived_slots`) | `compute_node_update` / `compute_node_add`; `compute_node_detail` | Complete | per-node worker count (0 = derive from observer GPU data); the detail carries the count in effect |
| `PUT /api/llms/{name}` (`max_inflight`, `plan_tier`) | `llm_update` / `llm_add` | Complete | per-LLM cap on autonomous sessions; `plan_tier` (`pro`/`max_5x`/`max_20x`/`api`) admits against that tier's `plan_tier_max_inflight` value unless an explicit `max_inflight > 0` overrides it; `GET /api/llms` responses carry both `effective_max_inflight` and `inflight_source`; also carries the optional `budget` object (see Per-LLM dollar budget) |
| `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/run` | `autonomous_prd_run` | Complete | `?view=compact` (absent or `view=full` = full; MCP sends `view=compact`) |
| `GET /api/autonomous/learnings` | `autonomous_learnings` | Complete | |
| `GET /api/autonomous/subscriptions` | `autonomous_subscriptions` | Complete | list the operator's persisted lifecycle event subscriptions (optional `?owner=` filter) |
| `POST /api/autonomous/subscriptions` | `autonomous_subscribe` | Complete | body `{filter:{kinds[], level?, prd_id?, task_id?, story_id?, owner?}, sink:{type, target}, action:{type, text}?, coalesce?, one_shot?, expires_at?}`; 400 with the validation message on bad input; sinks `comm`/`session`/`topic`/`alert`/`mcp_queue`/`webhook`/`peer` (the queue name is the sink target; `webhook` takes the https URL as target and `sink.secret_ref` = one `${secret:name}` reference, never a literal; `peer` takes the registered federation peer name as target). `webhook` and `peer` are refused with a 400 while their delivery is disabled, while the URL is off the allow-list, or while the peer is not a federated peer with `autonomous:write`; the answer never echoes the secret. Listings return `secret_ref` as the reference text only. MCP `expires_in_seconds` maps to `expires_at`; MCP `secret_ref` maps to `sink.secret_ref` |
| `DELETE /api/autonomous/subscriptions/{id}` | `autonomous_unsubscribe` | Complete | 404 for unknown ids (also accepted as `DELETE ?id={id}`); one-shot subscriptions are also auto-deleted after first delivery; changes take effect live (engine re-attaches), no restart needed |
| `PUT /api/autonomous/subscriptions/{id}` | `autonomous_subscription_update` | Complete | full replace of the mutable fields (filter, sink, action, coalesce, one_shot, expires_at; owner kept unless supplied); id and created_at are kept; 200 + the record, 400 validation message, 404 unknown id; auth `autonomous:write`; live re-attach, no restart |
| `POST /api/autonomous/subscriptions/{id}/test` | `autonomous_subscription_test` | Complete | delivers a synthetic `[test] ` prd.updated event to just that subscription's sink (never the action text, never consuming a one-shot); for `webhook` and `peer` it goes through the same sender as a real event; 200 `{ok, sink, error, status?, attempts?}` (`status` is the last HTTP status, `attempts` the POST count, both set for `webhook` and `peer` only), 404 unknown id; auth `autonomous:write` |
| `GET /api/autonomous/events` | `autonomous_events_pending` | Complete | `?queue=` (required), `?since=` cursor (default 0), `?limit=` (default 50, capped at 200); returns `{events, next_cursor, dropped}` with `events` always an array; 400 for a missing queue or non-numeric since/limit, 503 when no queue is wired; reads the queue behind an `mcp_queue` subscription sink. CLI `datawatch autonomous events`; comm `autonomous events` |
| `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_failure_escalation` (body `{task_id, policy\|null, actor}`) | `autonomous_prd_set_failure_escalation` | Complete | `policy` is the object `{enabled, max_failures, steps}`; `clear=true` sends a null policy. Task override when `task_id` is set — [howto](howto/failure-escalation.md) |
| `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/resolve_task_review` (body `{task_id, action, spec, backend, model, effort, files, note, actor}`) | `autonomous_prd_resolve_task_review` | Complete | `action` is `retry` or `cancel`; a 409 when the task is not held for review — [howto](howto/failure-escalation.md) |
| `GET /api/config` and `PUT /api/config` keys `autonomous.failure_escalation.enabled`, `.max_failures`, `.steps` | `config_set` / `get_config` | Complete | `steps` takes a JSON array or the text `backend:model[@attempts],...` — [howto](howto/failure-escalation.md) |

chunks.title: API ↔ MCP Tool Mapping
chunks.heading: Operator questions
chunks.body:
### Operator questions

| API Endpoint | MCP Tool | Status | Notes |
|-------------|----------|--------|-------|
| `POST /api/questions` | — | Deferred | Raise an operator question; needs the autonomous write capability. Body caps 64 KiB; the required shape is `text`, 2 to 20 options with unique ids, a `default` (an option or `hold`) and a `context` (`none`, `prd`, `task`, `proposal`, `registry_row`) with its matching link. Step 1 fields: `priority` (`normal` default / `high` — gates the alert announce, nothing else) and `return_path` (bool, opt-in `DATAWATCH_ANSWER:` line; needs `session_id`). MCP, CLI and comm rows are deferred pending the question channel's MCP and surface coverage |
| `GET /api/questions` | — | Deferred | List, newest first: `?state=`, `?context=`, `?asker=` (exact on `asked_by`), `?text=` (case-insensitive substring over question text, option labels/tradeoffs, answer quotes), `?limit=` (default 100, capped 1000). Needs the autonomous read capability |
| `GET /api/questions/{id}` | — | Deferred | One question (including `priority` and `return_path` on the record) + `answer_count` + `current_answer_id` + the standing answer's summary (`answer`, or `null` while it has no answer) in the same read — the polled return path for an asker |
| `POST /api/questions/{id}/answer` | — | Deferred | Record an answer: `chosen_option_id` and/or a non-blank `quote`; `supersedes` for a changed mind (the old answer is immutable, kept in the log); `surface` (`pwa`, `android`, `ios`, `cli`, `rest`, `mcp` or `comm:<channel>`), `source_message_id`, `actor`. A secret-looking answer is 422-refused — the body carries the fixed phrase `matched: secret pattern`, the two safe routes, and `reason: secret_detected`, but no part of the submitted text and no rule name (the matched rule's name lands on the `question_answer_refused` audit entry) |
| `POST /api/questions/{id}/withdraw` | — | Deferred | Withdraw an open question; 409 when it has already moved on |
| `GET /api/questions/{id}/answers` | — | Deferred | The full answer log, oldest first, each answer with its derived superseded flags, plus `current_answer_id` |

All rows are gated on `autonomous.questions.enabled` (off by default; `503` naming the switch while off). The rows are deferred because the MCP tools do not exist yet — the REST endpoints are implemented and live, and the switch itself is already reachable from MCP and comm (`config_set` / `configure autonomous.questions.enabled`). The three notification toggles (`notify_messaging`, `notify_alert`, `return_path`) are likewise reachable from every surface through the generic config keys (`config_set` / `datawatch config set` / `configure` / PWA Settings → General). The lifecycle subscription machinery already covers the new event kinds: `autonomous_subscribe` (MCP), `POST /api/autonomous/subscriptions` (REST), `datawatch autonomous subscribe --on question.answered,question.withdrawn` (CLI) and `autonomous subscribe --on …` (comm) accept both in `filter.kinds` — exactly-once, restart-durable delivery over every sink type. See [api/autonomous](api/autonomous.md#operator-question-channel) and [operations](operations.md#operator-questions).

chunks.heading: Automation records
chunks.body:
### Automation records

| API Endpoint | MCP Tool | Status | Notes |
|-------------|----------|--------|-------|
| `GET /api/automations` | `automation_list` | Complete | Data records only — no automatic advance yet; each record carries the computed `budget` view (see the Automation spending limit rows below) |
| `POST /api/automations` | `automation_create` | Complete | body `{name, description, entry_member_id, members[], budget_policy, project_dir, backend, model, effort, verification_*}` |
| `GET /api/automations/{id}` | `automation_get` | Complete | the record plus a computed `budget` view (absent when the Automation has no budget policy in play): `scope`, `ceiling_type`, `ceiling_usd`, `spent_usd`, `remaining_usd`, `window`, `window_start`, `window_end`, `pacing`, `pacing_allowed_usd`, `on_breach`, `ceiling_reached`, `hold` / `hold_reason`, `reset_at` / `reset_known` / `reset_source`, `state` (the current breach), `allocation_estimate` (always estimated), `peers[]` with `peer_spend_usd`, `peer_basis` and `peer_note`. Computed on every read, never stored |
| `PUT /api/automations/{id}` | `automation_update` | Complete | optional `expected_version` — optimistic concurrency, `409` if the record moved since |
| `DELETE /api/automations/{id}` | `automation_delete` | Complete | member Automatons are unaffected — the back-reference is cleared |
| `POST /api/automations/import-graph/{graph_id}` | `automation_import_graph` | Complete | CLI `datawatch automation import-graph <graph-id> [--dry-run]`; comm `automation import-graph <graph-id> [dry-run]`. Body `{dry_run}`; `404` unknown graph, `409` member already owned, `422` not representable |
| `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_budget` | `automation_set_budget` | Complete | Automation spending limit. Body `{member_id?, ceiling_type, ceiling_value, window, pacing?, on_breach?, backend?, allocation_estimate?, peer_window?, reset_time?, reset_weekday?, reset_day?, reset_zone?, estimated_cost_usd?, clear?, expected_version, actor, reason}`. The policy fields replace the whole policy of the Automation, or of one member when `member_id` is given; `clear` removes it and cannot be combined with them; `estimated_cost_usd` (member only) declares the member's expected cost. Does not change the Automation's status. `400` invalid policy, `404` unknown Automation or member, `409` stale `expected_version`, a finished member or a finished Automation. Audit action `automation_set_budget`. CLI `datawatch automation set-budget <id>`; comm `automation set-budget <id> key=value...` |
| `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_decision_assistant` | `automation_set_decision_assistant` | Complete | Optional local-model decision assistant (default off). Body `{member_id?, backend, model, mode?, hooks?, thresholds?, clear?, expected_version, actor, reason}`. The fields replace the whole setting of the Automation, or of one member when `member_id` is given; `clear` or an empty `backend` turns it off. `mode` is `shadow` (default) or `live`; `hooks` are `empty_edge`, `skip_member`, `insert_member`, `budget_breach`; `thresholds` map a hook to a number in (0,1]. `400` invalid setting, `404` unknown Automation or member, `409` stale `expected_version`. Audit action `automation_set_decision_assistant`. CLI `datawatch automation set-decision-assistant <id>`; comm `automation set-decision-assistant <id> key=value...` |
| `GET /api/autonomous/status` (`automations[].budget`) | `autonomous_status` | Complete | each Automation row carries the same `budget` view plus `spent_usd` and `ceiling_display` (for example `$12.40 of $40.00 (week)`); a block caused by the limit also shows as the row's blocked reason, and a pause or block is recorded in `budget.state` (`action`, `reason`, `resume_at`). CLI `datawatch autonomous status`; comm `automation status <id>` prints the budget lines |

| `GET /api/usage/readings` | `usage_readings` | Complete | The shared readings series (percent and/or spend, when, session percent, lanes, source), the bought extra credit, and the per-policy remaining-work figure; shared across federated daemons through a keeper, stale reads carry `stale`/`stale_reason`/`copied_at` |

Daemon-local, never part of the shared series |
| `PUT /api/config` key `usage.calculator.variant` (and `usage.calculator.policy`) | `config_set` | Complete | the calculator's stored variant/policy are ordinary daemon configuration, set through the general config tool: `{ "usage.calculator.variant": "pace-gauge" }`, with the same validation as REST |

| `GET /api/federation/fingerprints` | — | Complete | Peer-facing responder: the **peer daemon** calls it (not the operator), so no MCP tool. Requires the `federation:fingerprint` capability **and** per-peer `fingerprint_sync` opt-in on both sides; a peer token without the capability gets no read access at all. Returns per-pair hashes only — node identities and billing-group labels, never raw values |
| `GET /api/federation/fingerprint-matches[?state=pending\|confirmed\|rejected]` | `federation_fingerprint_matches` | Complete | Operator-facing match records; `state` maps to the REST parameter (omit for all states); each record has `id`, `peer`, `kind`, both resource names, state, and `shared_with` (confirmed peers only) |
| `POST /api/federation/fingerprint-matches/{id}/confirm` | `federation_fingerprint_confirm` | Complete | Operator decision: the two resources become one shared pool — a confirmed shared compute node makes the peer's admitted hold count against local capacity; re-confirming is safe; echoes back the updated record |
| `POST /api/federation/fingerprint-matches/{id}/reject` | `federation_fingerprint_reject` | Complete | Operator decision: the resources stay separate (undoes a prior confirm); the record stays rejected on later re-observation; unknown id is a 404 |

Opt-in rides on the peer record (`federation_peer_add` / `federation_peer_update`
`fingerprint_sync`, CLI `federation peer add|update --fingerprint-sync[=false]`),
and the billing-group label on LLM entries (`llm_add` / `llm_update`
`billing_group`). Decisions are audit-logged (`fingerprint_match_decision`).

chunks.title: `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask
chunks.body:
# `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask

**Shipped in v3.5.0 (BL34).** Sends a single-shot prompt to a chat
backend and returns the answer inline. No tmux session, no persistent
state — fast path for quick questions.

---

chunks.title: `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask
chunks.heading: When to use
chunks.body:
## When to use

- An operator wants a one-off answer ("what's the syntax for X?") without
  burning a session.
- An AI agent needs to consult an alternative model for a quick check.
- A messaging-channel listener wants to surface a cheap answer back to
  the user without spawning a worker.

If you need state across turns, threading, or tool use — start a session
instead (`POST /api/sessions`).

---

chunks.title: `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask
chunks.heading: Endpoint
chunks.body:
## Endpoint

```
POST /api/ask
Content-Type: application/json
```

chunks.title: `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask
chunks.heading: Request body
chunks.body:
### Request body

```json
{
  "question": "<required, non-empty>",
  "backend":  "ollama" | "openwebui",      // optional, default "ollama"
  "model":    "<optional model override>"  // optional
}
```

When `model` is omitted, the configured default is used:
- `ollama.model` for Ollama
- `openwebui.model` for OpenWebUI

chunks.title: `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask
chunks.heading: Response (200 OK)
chunks.body:
### Response (200 OK)

```json
{
  "backend":      "ollama",
  "model":        "llama3.2:3b",
  "answer":       "...",
  "duration_ms":  812
}
```

chunks.title: `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask
chunks.heading: Error codes
chunks.body:
### Error codes

| Code | Cause |
|------|-------|
| 400  | Empty question, unknown backend, missing model |
| 405  | Method other than POST |
| 500  | Backend returned an error or is not configured |

---

chunks.heading: Examples
chunks.body: ## Examples

chunks.title: `POST /api/ask` — read-only LLM ask

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/ask \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"question":"What does GOMAXPROCS default to?"}' | jq .
```

chunks.heading: Configuration
chunks.body:
## Configuration

`POST /api/ask` works as soon as the chosen backend is configured:

```yaml
ollama:
  enabled: true
  host:    http://localhost:11434
  model:   llama3.2:3b

openwebui:
  enabled: true
  url:     http://localhost:3000
  model:   gpt-oss:20b
  api_key: <token>
```

No new fields were added — `ask` consumes the existing backend config.

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.body:
# Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)

**Shipped in v3.10.0.** LLM-driven Product Requirements Document →
Stories → Tasks planning with independent verification. Each
Task can be spawned as a worker session under F10. Inspired by
HackingDave/nightwire's autonomous module; the design map is in
`docs/plans/2026-04-20-bl24-autonomous-decomposition.md`.

Disabled by default — opt in by setting `autonomous.enabled: true`.

---

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.heading: Surfaces (full channel parity)
chunks.body:
## Surfaces (full channel parity)

| Channel | Entry-point |
|---|---|
| YAML  | `autonomous:` block in `~/.datawatch/config.yaml` |
| REST  | `/api/autonomous/*` (bearer-authenticated) |
| MCP   | `autonomous_status`, `autonomous_config_get/set`, `autonomous_prd_*`, `autonomous_learnings`, `autonomous_lane_fill_status`, `autonomous_triage` |
| CLI   | `datawatch autonomous <subcmd>` |
| Comm  | `rest GET /api/autonomous/status` etc. via the comm `rest` passthrough (Signal/Slack/Telegram/Matrix/etc.) |

---

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.heading: REST endpoints
chunks.body:
## REST endpoints

```
GET    /api/autonomous/status              loop snapshot (running, active PRDs, queued/running)
GET    /api/autonomous/config              read current config
PUT    /api/autonomous/config              replace config (full body)

POST   /api/autonomous/prds                create PRD; body: {spec, project_dir, [backend], [effort], [kind]}
GET    /api/autonomous/prds                summary list, newest-updated first, paged; ?full=1 for whole records (see "Automata list" below)
GET    /api/autonomous/prds/{id}           one PRD with story+task tree
PATCH  /api/autonomous/prds/{id}           edit PRD title + spec (non-running only); body: {title, spec, actor}     [v5.19.0]
DELETE /api/autonomous/prds/{id}           cancel + archive (status → cancelled)
DELETE /api/autonomous/prds/{id}?hard=true permanently delete the PRD + descendants spawned via SpawnPRD             [v5.19.0]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/plan      run LLM planning phase (creates stories+tasks) [BL304 canonical]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/decompose run LLM planning phase (back-compat alias for /plan)
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/approve   review/approve gate                                                       [v5.2.0  / BL191 Q1]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/resume   resume a paused PRD, or one the boot-resume gate parked; body: {actor, note} (409-style 400 if neither)
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/reject    operator rejects the plan; body: {actor, reason}                          [v5.2.0  / BL191 Q1]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/request_revision  ask for a re-plan; body: {actor, note}                            [v5.2.0  / BL191 Q1]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/edit_task per-task spec edit on needs_review/revisions_asked; body: {task_id, …}    [v5.2.0  / BL191 Q1]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/instantiate  template instantiation; body: {vars{}, actor}                          [v5.2.0  / BL191 Q2]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_llm   PRD-level worker LLM override; body: {backend, effort, model, decomposition_profile, [guardrail_backend], [guardrail_model], actor}   [v5.4.0  / BL203]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_task_llm  per-task LLM override; body: {task_id, backend, effort, model, [guardrail_backend], [guardrail_model], actor}             [v5.4.0  / BL203]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_task_project_dir  per-task project dir override; body: {task_id, project_dir, actor} ("" clears)   [v9.1.0 / BL447]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_task_verification_llm   per-task verifier LLM; body: {task_id, [verification_backend], [verification_model], [verification_effort], actor}   [v9.0.69]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_story_verification_llm  per-story verifier LLM; body: {story_id, [verification_backend], [verification_model], [verification_effort], actor} [v9.0.69]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_verification_llm        per-Automaton verifier LLM; body: {[verification_backend], [verification_model], [verification_effort], actor}       [v9.0.69]
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_verifier_policy         per-Automaton verifier policy; body: {[mode], [backends[]], actor}
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_task_verifier_policy    per-task verifier policy; body: {task_id, [mode], [backends[]], actor}
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_failure_escalation     failure escalation override; body: {[task_id], policy|null, actor} (null clears; see "Failure escalation")
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/resolve_task_review        operator decision on a task held for review; body: {task_id, action: retry|cancel, [spec], [backend], [model], [effort], [files[]], [note], actor}
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_dirs  directory scope; body: {write_dirs[], read_dirs[]} (absolute paths)
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_tags  replace the Automaton's tags; body: {[tag_ids[]], [primary_tag_id]}; tag_ids may be omitted when primary_tag_id is sent, which keeps the current tags ([] clears; primary_tag_id must be one of the tags or empty, else 400)
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_kind  Automaton kind; body: {kind} (feature|bug|other; "" derives it again); 400 on an unknown kind, 404 on an unknown id
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_lane_preference  lane an Automaton may take; body: {lane_preference: gpu|claude|any} ("" means any); 400 on an unknown value, 404 on an unknown id
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_notify_events  set the lifecycle event kinds the Automaton notifies on; body: {notify_events[]} — absent/null/[] clears (inherit); the reply carries the computed notify_events_effective
POST   /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/run       kick the executor for this PRD
GET    /api/autonomous/prds?tag={id}[&include_sub=false]  Automata carrying a tag (and, by default, any descendant tag)

GET    /api/autonomous/tags[?include_sub=&counts=]  tag tree (parent_id) with Automata counts; counts=true adds subtree, direct and session counts and an untagged object
POST   /api/autonomous/tags                 create; body: {name, [parent_id], [color], [description]}
PATCH  /api/autonomous/tags/{id}            rename / recolor / describe / reparent; 409 if the move makes a cycle
DELETE /api/autonomous/tags/{id}            409 while the tag has child tags, 409 with {count} while Automata carry it
GET    /api/autonomous/attention           the attention group: {statuses, items}; see "Attention list" below
GET    /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/children  list child PRDs spawned via SpawnPRD                                      [v5.9.0  / BL191 Q4]
GET    /api/sessions/{id}/progress         live progress snapshot for one session (turns, tool calls, last action,
                                           tokens) — same `progress` shape prd-get carries per running task;
                                           404 for a non-pi session (never reads another session's pi log)

GET    /api/autonomous/learnings           extracted post-task learnings
GET    /api/autonomous/progress[?automation_id=&tag_id=&since=&until=]  progress metrics object (counts by kind, throughput, utilization, remaining work, completion range); since/until are YYYY-MM-DD, until is inclusive; 400 on a bad date
GET    /api/autonomous/progress/trend[?days=]  saved daily snapshots as {days, points[], direction}; days 1..365 (default 30), 400 outside that range
GET    /api/autonomous/lane-fill[?limit=N]  lane fill status: mode, lanes, queued eligible counts, pool evidence, newest decisions and idle alerts; limit 1..1000 (default 50), 400 outside that range

# Guardrail Library + Profiles
GET    /api/autonomous/guardrails                  list guardrail library (built-ins + skill-contributed)
GET    /api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles          list profiles
POST   /api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles          create profile; body: {name, description?, guardrails[], block_on_file_drift?, notify_events?}
GET    /api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles/{id}     get one profile
PUT    /api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles/{id}     update profile (a key left out stays as-is; an explicit empty notify_events clears it)
DELETE /api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles/{id}     delete profile
PUT    /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/guardrails        set per-Automaton override; body: {guardrail_profile?, per_task_guardrails[], per_story_guardrails[]}

# Automations — orchestration records (see the Automations section below)
GET    /api/automations              list Automations (each carries a computed tags array: the member Automata's tag IDs)
POST   /api/automations              create (returns draft, version 1); body: {name, entry_member_id?, members[], budget_policy?, project_dir?, actor, reason}
GET    /api/automations/{id}         get one
PUT    /api/automations/{id}         update; body: create fields + expected_version (required)
DELETE /api/automations/{id}         delete (draft/completed/cancelled only); body: {actor?, reason?}
POST   /api/automations/{id}/set_llm               set the execution and planning defaults; body: {backend?, model?, effort?, planning_backend?, planning_model?, expected_version?, actor?, reason?}
POST   /api/automations/{id}/set_verification_llm  set the verification default; body: {backend?, model?, effort?, expected_version?, actor?, reason?}
POST   /api/automations/{id}/set_budget   set, replace or clear the spending limit of an Automation or one member (see "Spending limit" below); body: {member_id?, ceiling_type, ceiling_value, window, pacing?, on_breach?, backend?, allocation_estimate?, peer_window?, reset_time?, reset_weekday?, reset_day?, reset_zone?, estimated_cost_usd?, clear?, expected_version, actor?, reason?}

# Lifecycle event subscriptions (BL427 — PRD lifecycle events, phase 3)
GET    /api/autonomous/subscriptions        list persisted lifecycle event subscriptions (optional ?owner= lists only those created by the named owner)
POST   /api/autonomous/subscriptions        create (201 + the record); body: {filter:{kinds[], level?, prd_id?, task_id?, story_id?, owner?}, sink:{type, target}, action:{type, text}?, coalesce?, one_shot?, expires_at?}. Sink types: comm | session | topic | alert. An action is only valid with a session sink (action.type must be send_input, ≤4096 chars). 400 with the validation message on bad input
DELETE /api/autonomous/subscriptions/{id}   delete (204; 404 when unknown) — also accepted as DELETE /api/autonomous/subscriptions?id={id}. One-shot subscriptions are also auto-deleted by the engine after their first delivery. Changes take effect live — the engine re-attaches on store changes, no restart
```

`GET/POST/DELETE /api/autonomous/subscriptions` sit on the operator's
persisted lifecycle subscriptions (`<data_dir>/lifecycle_subscriptions.json`):
`filter.kinds` picks event kinds from the known set (`prd.completed`,
`task.completed`, … every PRD/task status-change kind plus
`task.session_started`, `task.session_cleared`, `scope_warning`,
`guardrail_warn`, `prd.updated`),
`filter.level` narrows to `prd` or `task` events, and the `sink` is
where matching events are delivered (`comm` = the notify pipeline, `session`
= a datawatch-managed session, `topic` = the push-topic bus, `alert` = the
in-app alerts store). With `sink.type = session`, `action` may type
`action.text` into the session each time (`send_input`), which replaces
per-event watch-and-inject scripts. `one_shot: true` consumes the
subscription after its first delivery; `expires_at` (RFC 3339, future)
expires it instead. These endpoints require the same auth as the other
`/api/autonomous` routes (federation peers need `autonomous:read` for
list, `autonomous:write` for create/delete). They are served only when the
daemon runs the subscription engine; otherwise 503.

When `autonomous.enabled` is false, every endpoint returns
`503 autonomous disabled`.

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.heading: Notify events (`set_notify_events`)
chunks.body:
### Notify events (`set_notify_events`)
The set of lifecycle event kinds (the same known set as the subscription
filter above, `prd.completed`, `task.completed`, …) that the notification
pipeline fires for this Automaton, independent of who is subscribed.
Resolution is a tiered precedence chain — **Automaton > guardrail profile
> global default**. Each level may supply the whole set, or inherit
from the level behind it. An empty or unset list on a tier falls
through to the next one; the result is always an effective list.

```
POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_notify_events
     {"notify_events":["prd.completed","task.completed"]}
     # clear → inherit from the guardrail profile / global default:
     #   {}            /  {"notify_events":null}  /  {"notify_events":[]}
```

* **Per-Automaton** (`set_notify_events`): sets, replaces, or clears
    (`notify_events` null, `[]`, or an absent key) the list for that
    Automaton. POST only — any other method is `405`. Invalid entries are
    rejected with `400` and a message that names the offending kind (or
    its index) *and* lists the valid kinds, so nothing is ever partially
    applied.
* **Per-guardrail-profile** (create/update body `notify_events`, same
    key rule): applies to every Automaton that runs under the profile and
    whose Automaton-tier list is empty.
* **Global default** (config key `autonomous.notify.default_events`,
    written through the standard config surfaces — `PUT /api/config`
    and the autonomous config endpoint): the floor of the chain. Unset
    (`nil`) falls back to the built-in five default kinds; an explicit
    empty list is preserved as "no events at all", so it is distinguishable
    from unset.

Reads surface the resolution without ambiguity. The by-id Automaton and
`set_*` replies carry both `notify_events` (the raw list set at this
tier) and `notify_events_effective` — `{events, source}` where
`source` is `automaton`, `profile` or `global`, the tier that actually
supplied the effective kinds. `GET /api/autonomous/status` reports a
`notify` block: `default_events` (the in-effect global defaults) and
`overrides`, one entry per non-terminal Automaton whose effective list
resolves from the `automaton` or `profile` tier (`id`, `source`,
`events`) — sorted by Automaton ID and capped at 100. Both arrays are
always lists: empty, never null. All of these endpoints follow the same
auth as the other
`/api/autonomous` routes: the `set_notify_events` action requires
`autonomous:write` for federation peers, `autonomous:read` for the
status/config reads.

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.heading: Live task progress + looping warning
chunks.body:
### Live task progress + looping warning

While a task is actively running — `status` `in_progress` or `verifying` —
the executor's periodic session poll also parses the worker's own pi JSONL
log and refreshes two fields that ride along in every PRD view (`prd-get`,
`tasks` and `full` detail, MCP `autonomous_prd_get`):

```json
{
  "id": "task-1234", "status": "in_progress",
  "progress": {
    "last_event_at": "2026-10-14T12:04:41Z",
    "assistant_turns": 12,
    "tool_calls": {"bash": 9, "write": 3},
    "last_tool_name": "bash",
    "last_tool_args": "{\"command\": \"go test ./...\"}",
    "last_summary": "Now running the full test suite before wrapping up.",
    "tokens": 48210
  },
  "looping_warning": "suspected looping: same call x5"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `progress.last_event_at` | Timestamp (RFC3339) of the newest event in the log — freshness is the first thing to check. |
| `progress.assistant_turns` | Assistant-role messages so far, one per LLM reply (tool-calling ones included) — a proxy for "how much work has been attempted". |
| `progress.tool_calls` | Per-tool-name call counts across the log so far. |
| `progress.last_tool_name` / `last_tool_args` | The most recent tool call, with arguments as compact JSON (truncated to 500 chars). |
| `progress.last_summary` | First 200 chars of the most recent thinking/text block — what the worker was last planning or reporting. |
| `progress.tokens` | Cumulative tokens reported by the log's usage fields. |
| `looping_warning` | **Omitted unless set.** The worker re-issued the same tool name + arguments on three consecutive periodic polls (~an hour of real time); treat it as "stuck, needs an operator" rather than "progressing slowly". |

**Presence semantics.** The store forces both fields off the moment a task
leaves the active statuses (and strips them at every save/load), so
`progress` present ⇔ the worker is running right now. A `pending` task has
neither key in JSON; a `completed` task that ran for an hour keeps none of
its progress behind — history lives in the decisions log and the session
log on disk, not on the task.

`GET /api/sessions/{id}/progress` returns the same snapshot for any pi
session whose log exists, regardless of autonomous involvement — session id,
full id, state, `log_path`, plus the fields above. The route never reads a
pi log from another session: a non-pi session gets 404 even when a stale pi
log sits in its project directory, 405 for non-GET. The PWA shows the
snapshot on the running task's card in the Status tab; the session view no
longer carries a progress strip of its own (removed in 9.31.3).

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.heading: Clean restart on `reset_task`
chunks.body:
### Clean restart on `reset_task`

`POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/reset_task` accepts a `clean_restart` boolean
(default `false`) alongside `task_id` and `force`. By default the next attempt
restores the work that `preserve_attempt_work` saved from earlier killed
attempts. Setting `clean_restart: true` starts that one attempt from the
pre-task tree instead, so the saved work is not restored for that attempt. The
flag applies to the single reset only; later attempts restore again unless they
are reset with `clean_restart` too. The MCP tool and the comm-channel command
accept the same option.

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.heading: Guardrail judge LLM override (`set_llm` / `set_task_llm`)
chunks.body:
### Guardrail judge LLM override (`set_llm` / `set_task_llm`)

Set a PRD's worker LLM with `set_llm`: Omitted fields stay unchanged; an
empty value (`""`) clears that field (falls back to global). Every `set_llm`
call is audit-logged and appended to the PRD's decision log.

Command-line usage: `autonomous set-llm <prd-id> [backend=<v>] [effort=<v>] [model=<v>] [decomposition_profile=<v>]`

`guardrail_backend` / `guardrail_model` pick the LLM that judges the
guardrail/verification step for an Automaton or a single task. They
are presence-aware, unlike the worker-LLM keys:

- **absent** — the field is left unchanged
- **`""`** — the override is cleared (falls back to the next level)
- **a value** — sets the override (`guardrail_backend` must be a configured LLM name; unknown names return 400)

A body that carries **only** guardrail keys (plus `task_id` / `actor`)
does not touch `backend` / `effort` / `model` / `decomposition_profile`.
A body that carries any worker-LLM key keeps the existing
overwrite-all behaviour for those keys.

Resolution order: task `guardrail_backend` → Automaton
`guardrail_backend` → global `autonomous.verification_backend` / `verification_model`.

```bash
# guardrail-only: leaves the worker LLM untouched
curl -sX POST http://localhost:7433/api/autonomous/prds/<id>/set_llm \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"guardrail_backend":"ollama","guardrail_model":"qwen3.8:27b"}'

# clear a task's guardrail model override only
curl -sX POST http://localhost:7433/api/autonomous/prds/<id>/set_task_llm \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task_id":"<task-id>","guardrail_model":""}'
```

chunks.title: Autonomous PRD planning (v3.10.0 — BL24 + BL25)
chunks.heading: Per-task project dir override (`set_task_project_dir`)
chunks.body:
### Per-task project dir override (`set_task_project_dir`)

Each task carries an optional `project_dir` field (JSON `project_dir`).
When set, the task runs in that directory instead of the Automaton's
`project_dir`.

- **Precedence:** task `project_dir` → Automaton `project_dir`. An empty
  value means the task inherits the Automaton's directory, and sending
  `""` clears an existing override.
- **Every per-task check follows the override:** diff capture, scope
  (write/read dirs), file drift detection, quality gates and the
  verifier all use the task's resolved directory.
- **Validation:** the path must be absolute and must not be a
  filesystem root or system directory. When the Automaton has write
  dirs, the path must be inside them. Validation errors and unknown task IDs return
  `400`. Like `set_task_llm`, it is accepted only while the Automaton is
  `needs_review`, `revisions_asked` or `cancelled`.

| Surface | How |
|---|---|
| **REST** | `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_task_project_dir`, body `{task_id, project_dir, actor}` |
| **MCP** | `autonomous_prd_set_task_project_dir` (`id`, `task_id`, `project_dir`) |
| **CLI** | `datawatch autonomous prd-set-task-project-dir <prd> <task> [dir]` (leave out `dir` to clear) |
| **Comm** | `autonomous set-task-project-dir <prd> <task> [dir]` (alias `set_task_project_dir`) |
| **PWA** | Task edit modal → **Project dir override** (empty inherits); the task card shows a `dir:` badge when it is set |

```bash
curl -sX POST http://localhost:7433/api/autonomous/prds/<id>/set_task_project_dir \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task_id":"<task-id>","project_dir":"/srv/repo/services/api"}'

# clear: inherit the Automaton's project_dir again
curl -sX POST http://localhost:7433/api/autonomous/prds/<id>/set_task_project_dir \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task_id":"<task-id>","project_dir":""}'
```
