---

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Authentication
chunks.body:
## Authentication

```
Authorization: Bearer <server.token>
```

Set the token in datawatch config:
```yaml
server:
  token: <random-string>
```

The mobile app stores the token in OS keychain / iOS Keychain; never
in plain user storage.

---

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Versioning
chunks.body:
## Versioning

The mobile app should send `User-Agent: datawatch-app/<version>` and
read the daemon version from `GET /api/info`. The daemon stays
backward-compatible within the 3.x line per the operator's versioning
rule (no 4.0 without explicit instruction).

When the mobile app needs to check whether a new endpoint exists
(e.g. `/api/cost` was added in v3.7.0), check `version >= "3.7.0"`
before calling. The daemon returns 404 for unknown paths.

For optional behavior on an existing endpoint (query parameters,
WebSocket modes, compression), prefer the `capabilities` array in
`GET /api/info` over version comparisons — see
[Low-bandwidth client flow](#low-bandwidth-client-flow).

---

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Low-bandwidth client flow
chunks.body:
## Low-bandwidth client flow

A phone that only shows a session list should not download every
session's full record and every terminal's output. The daemon offers a
lighter path for each of the heavy streams. Use each one only when
`GET /api/info` advertises it, so the same client keeps working against
an older daemon.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: 1. Check capabilities
chunks.body:
### 1. Check capabilities

```
GET /api/info
→ { "version": "...", "capabilities": ["sessions.view_summary", "alerts.paging",
     "alerts.count", "ws.alerts_read", "ws.hello", "ws.session_list_delta",
     "ws.session_list_window", "ws.session_view_summary", "ws.output_scoped",
     "ws.unsubscribe", "api.gzip"], ... }
```

Treat a missing `capabilities` array as an empty one. Capability strings
are never renamed; new features add new strings.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: 2. Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` on every request
chunks.body:
### 2. Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` on every request

With `server.api_gzip` on (the default; advertised as `api.gzip`), any
`/api/*` JSON response larger than `server.api_gzip_min_bytes` (default
1024 bytes) comes back with `Content-Encoding: gzip`. OkHttp and
URLSession add the header and decompress transparently; a hand-built
client must check `Content-Encoding` before parsing. Small responses
are never compressed.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: 3. Open the WebSocket and send `hello`
chunks.body:
### 3. Open the WebSocket and send `hello`

```json
{"type":"hello","data":{"session_list":"delta","session_view":"summary","output":"subscribed"}}
```

The daemon answers with the modes now in effect:

```json
{"type":"hello_ack","data":{"session_list":"delta","session_view":"summary","output":"subscribed","capabilities":["ws.hello","ws.session_list_delta","ws.session_view_summary","ws.output_scoped","ws.unsubscribe"]}}
```

- `session_list: delta` — no whole-list `sessions` frames. Each new or
  changed session arrives as one `session_state` `{"session": {...}}`;
  each removed session as one `session_removed` `{"session_id": "..."}`.
- `session_view: summary` — `session_state` carries the compact record
  (long text fields truncated, `truncated_fields` lists which).
- `output: subscribed` — `output`, `raw_output`, `pane_capture` and
  `chat_message` frames arrive only for sessions you `subscribe` to.

Send only the keys you want; each is independent. Frames that arrive
before `hello_ack` can be ignored.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Window form: `session_list: "window"`
chunks.body:
#### Window form: `session_list: "window"`

Capability `ws.session_list_window`. This is the bounded form and the one
a phone list should use. The daemon sends only the default view, as compact
rows, and after that only the sessions that change.

The default view is every session that is not finished, plus each finished
session (complete, failed or killed) updated within the window. The window is
the daemon's `server.recent_session_minutes` setting (a value of 0 or less
means 5). The daemon echoes it as `window_minutes` on every list frame, so read
it there and never hard-code it.

```json
{"type":"hello","data":{"session_list":"window","session_view":"summary"}}
```

The daemon answers with `hello_ack` (`session_list` is `window`), then sends
exactly one `sessions` frame:

```json
{"type":"sessions","data":{"sessions":[{"id":"...","full_id":"...","state":"running","updated_at":"..."}, ...],"version":"...","window_minutes":5,"total":4000,"more":true},"ts":"..."}
```

- `data.sessions` — summary rows, the same shape as
  `GET /api/sessions?view=summary` (with `scheduled_count` where the schedule
  store is wired). A row has no `task`; see the merge rules below.
- `data.window_minutes` — the window this list is built on.
- `data.total` — how many sessions the daemon holds, inside the window or not.
- `data.more` — `true` when the daemon holds sessions this frame leaves out
  (finished and older than the window). A field the daemon omits means `0` or
  `false`.

After that frame the socket sends no `sessions` frame at all. Each change is
one `session_state` `{"session": {...}}` for the one session that changed:
merge it by `full_id`, and add it if it is new to the window.

`session_removed` `{"session_id": "..."}` is sent only when a session is
deleted. A session that ages out of the window gets no frame; see *Aging*
below.

**Frames before `hello_ack`.** The socket is open before you can send
`hello`, so the first frame on a new connection is the legacy bounded
`sessions` frame (described below). Treat it as provisional. The rows frame
that follows `hello_ack` replaces it. Sending `hello` again gets a fresh
`hello_ack` and a fresh rows frame, which replaces your list.

**Merge rules** (the PWA follows these):

- A row without `task` keeps the `task`, `last_response`, `input_mode`,
  `channel_ready` and the other fields you already hold for that session.
- A summary key the row omits is empty now: clear it, do not keep the old
  value. The summary keys are `id`, `full_id`, `name`, `state`, `backend`,
  `llm_ref`, `project_dir`, `hostname`, `created_at`, `updated_at`,
  `last_activity`, `parent_id`, `est_cost_usd`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`,
  `status_line` and `truncated_fields`.
- A text field named in `truncated_fields` was cut. If you hold the full text
  for the same session, keep it. Otherwise show the cut text and fetch
  `GET /api/sessions/{id}` when the user opens the session.
- A full record (one that carries `task`) replaces the held record.

**Aging.** The daemon never sends a removal because a finished session left
the window. A rows frame is the whole default view, so a held session it omits
and that you did not fetch over REST has left the view: drop it. Between
frames you may also drop a finished session whose `updated_at` is older than
`window_minutes`, so your list matches the daemon's.

**History.** Finished sessions older than the window never come over the
WebSocket, to any client mode. Fetch them over REST, with cursor paging:

```
GET /api/sessions?view=summary&limit=50
GET /api/sessions?view=summary&limit=50&cursor=<next_cursor>
GET /api/sessions?view=summary&limit=50&history=1&cursor=<next_cursor>
```

Repeat with each `next_cursor` until the response has none. `history=1` adds
the archived sessions; send the same parameters on every page. A single
session's full record is `GET /api/sessions/{id}`.

**Legacy bounded frame.** A client that does not announce `window` (no
`hello`, or `session_list` `full`) still gets a `sessions` frame on connect and
on every change. It is bounded: only the default-view sessions, long text cut
to `server.session_summary_text_chars` with `truncated_fields` set, and
`more`, `total` and `window_minutes` alongside. Its `session_state` frames stay
full records, for default-view sessions only. Get the full text of a cut field
with `GET /api/sessions/{id}`, and page history over REST as above.

**Adopting the window form, step by step:**

1. Read `capabilities` from `GET /api/info`. Use the window form only when
   both `ws.hello` and `ws.session_list_window` are present.
2. Open `/ws` with the Bearer token, as today.
3. Send `hello` with `"session_list":"window"` and your `session_view`.
4. Wait for `hello_ack`. If its `session_list` is not `window`, keep the
   legacy handling.
5. On the next `sessions` frame, replace the default-view list with its rows
   using the merge rules. Read `window_minutes`, `total` and `more` from the
   frame. Do not fetch the initial list over REST.
6. Apply each `session_state` (merge by `full_id`) and each `session_removed`
   (drop by `session_id`).
7. Age finished rows out locally, as described under *Aging*.
8. Page history over REST when the user asks for it (`limit=50`, `cursor`,
   `history=1`). The socket never carries history.
9. On reconnect, send `hello` again and apply the new rows frame, which
   replaces your list.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: 4. Load the initial list over REST
chunks.body:
### 4. Load the initial list over REST

A `delta` client loads the list here. A `window` client does not: its list
comes in the rows frame (see the window form above), and it fetches history
only.

Right after `hello_ack` (`delta` clients):

```
GET /api/sessions?view=summary
```

This returns the compact list: long text fields cut to
`server.session_summary_text_chars` characters, and only the newest
`server.session_summary_terminal_limit` ended sessions (the response
header `X-Datawatch-Sessions-Omitted` says how many older ones were
left out). Add `states=active` for running/waiting sessions only, or
`since=<RFC3339|unix>` to fetch only what changed after a reconnect.
Fetch `GET /api/sessions/{id}` when the user opens a session and needs
the full record. Contract: [sessions.md](sessions.md#compact-session-list-viewsummary).

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: 5. Apply the stream
chunks.body:
### 5. Apply the stream

- `session_state` → replace (or insert) the session keyed by `full_id`.
- `sessions` (window rows frame) → replace the default-view list, using the
  merge rules in the window form above.
- `session_removed` → drop that session.
- On reconnect, send `hello` again and refetch with `since=` set to the
  last `updated_at` you saw (or refetch the whole summary list).

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: 6. Subscribe only while a terminal is open
chunks.body:
### 6. Subscribe only while a terminal is open

```json
{"type":"subscribe","data":{"session_id":"myhost-a1b2"}}
{"type":"unsubscribe","data":{"session_id":"myhost-a1b2"}}
```

Send `subscribe` when the session's terminal view opens and
`unsubscribe` when it closes. `unsubscribe` also stops the screen
capture the subscription started. Full and short session IDs both work.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: 7. Alerts without polling
chunks.body:
### 7. Alerts without polling

- Badge: `GET /api/alerts/count` → `{"unread_count": N, "total": M}`
  once at start-up.
- Updates: the `alert` WS event carries each new alert; `alerts_read`
  (`{"ids": [...], "unread_count": N}` or `{"all": true,
  "unread_count": 0}`) arrives whenever alerts are marked read on any
  client. Update the badge from these instead of polling.
- List screen: `GET /api/alerts?limit=20` (add `unread=1` for unread
  only) and page with `before=<next_before>` while `has_more` is true.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Fallback on an older daemon
chunks.body:
### Fallback on an older daemon

| Capability missing | Do this instead |
|---|---|
| `sessions.view_summary` | `GET /api/sessions` (full list; the params are ignored by older daemons, so check before relying on truncation or the omitted header). |
| `ws.hello` | Do not send `hello`; expect the full `sessions` frame on connect and on every change. |
| `ws.session_list_window` | Do not send `session_list: "window"`. Use `delta` when `ws.session_list_delta` is present (load the list over REST, step 4), otherwise keep the full handling. Where a daemon sends the bounded legacy frame, read `more`, `total` and `window_minutes` when present, and page history over REST. |
| `ws.session_list_delta` / `ws.session_view_summary` | Keep handling `sessions` frames and full `session_state` records. `hello_ack` echoes what was actually applied, so trust it over what you asked for. |
| `ws.output_scoped` | Expect output for every session; drop frames for sessions you have not opened. |
| `ws.unsubscribe` | Skip `unsubscribe`; the subscription ends when the socket closes. |
| `alerts.count` / `alerts.paging` | `GET /api/alerts` and count unread client-side. |
| `ws.alerts_read` | Refetch the badge after your own mark-read calls; changes from other clients appear on the next refresh. |
| `api.gzip` | Nothing to change — the header is harmless; responses are just uncompressed. |

Operators can tune these defaults (`server.ws_session_list_default`,
`server.ws_output_scope_default`, the summary limits and the gzip
threshold) — see [operations.md](../operations.md#payload-settings-for-low-bandwidth-clients).

---

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: OpenAPI / schema
chunks.body:
## OpenAPI / schema

The full machine-readable spec lives at `/api/openapi.yaml`. The

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Push notifications
chunks.body:
## Push notifications

Push delivery channel is configured per-device at registration time
(`platform: "fcm" | "ntfy"`). Datawatch sends push payloads via the
operator-configured FCM/ntfy backend. The mobile client receives:

- `session_state` — when a watched session changes state
- `alert` — operator-defined alerts (BL11 anomaly, BL30 cooldown, …)
- `audit` — when an audit-eligible action occurs (BL9; opt-in)

These are best-effort; the source of truth is always
`GET /api/sessions` + `GET /api/audit`.

---

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Guardrail APIs (Automata surface)
chunks.body:
## Guardrail APIs (Automata surface)

Mobile and Auto surfaces can access the guardrail library and profile
management endpoints under `/api/autonomous/guardrails*`:

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/autonomous/guardrails` | GET | List guardrail library |
| `/api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles` | GET | List profiles |
| `/api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles` | POST | Create profile |
| `/api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles/{id}` | GET | Get one profile |
| `/api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles/{id}` | PUT | Update profile |
| `/api/autonomous/guardrail_profiles/{id}` | DELETE | Delete profile |
| `/api/autonomous/prds/{id}/guardrails` | PUT | Set per-Automaton override |

Per-story approval payloads include `guardrail_verdicts` so Wear/Auto
surfaces can surface block reasons without polling full telemetry.

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Triage records (Automata surface)
chunks.body:
## Triage records (Automata surface)

The triage records of the failed and blocked Automata are read from
`GET /api/autonomous/triage` — the same contract the PWA's triage card and the CLI, MCP and comm surfaces use. It is a stable read for Android/Wear/Auto:

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/autonomous/triage` | GET | List triage records, newest first, optionally filtered |

Optional query params (combinable): `automation_id`, `prd_id`, `status` (`failed`\|`blocked` only; anything else is refused).

Response body — `records` plus the alert threshold in force (`alert_minutes`, the
`autonomous.automation.triage_alert_minutes` setting, default 30, `0` = off):

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "prd_id": "d0442737d38c",
      "prd_title": "nightly ingest",
      "automation_id": "4522f306c266",
      "automation_name": "nightly pipeline",
      "member_id": "member-2",
      "status": "failed",
      "task_id": "task-9",
      "task_title": "run integration tests",
      "error": "connection refused: testdb:5432 (truncated at 2000)",
      "blocked_reason": "waiting on operator decision",
      "session_end_reason": "runtime error: exit 2 (truncated at 2000)",
      "first_seen_at": "2026-10-27T09:12:44Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-10-27T09:44:02Z",
      "alerted_at": "2026-10-27T09:44:02Z",
      "retry_budget": {
        "infra":   { "limit": 3, "used": 1, "left": 2 },
        "content": { "limit": 4, "used": 4, "left": 0 },
        "scope":   { "limit": 2, "used": 0, "left": 2 },
        "policy":  { "limit": 1, "used": 0, "left": 1 },
        "ceiling_total": 10,
        "ceiling_left": 5
      },
      "notes": [
        { "at": "2026-10-27T09:12:44Z", "source": "triage", "text": "Automaton failed on task 'run integration tests'" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "alert_minutes": 30
}
```

Shape notes for the app team:

- A record is a **read** of the engine's state: it is filled and refreshed by the
  daemon on every coordinator tick while the Automaton stays failed or blocked, and
  removed again when it leaves that state. Polling sees new records appear and old
  ones disappear.
- `retry_budget` is informational (the engine's existing budget for the four
  categories: infra, content, scope, policy, each with `limit`, `used`, `left`;
  plus `ceiling_total` and `ceiling_left`, the overall auto-retry ceiling —
  `ceiling_total` is `0` when there is none).
- `alerted_at` is absent until the triage alert for the episode has fired.
- The strings (`error`, `session_end_reason`) are already truncated to
  2000 chars by the daemon; treat them as hostile text and render sanitized.
- The optional fields (`prd_title`, `automation_id`, `automation_name`, `member_id`,
  `task_id`, `task_title`, `error`, `blocked_reason`, `session_end_reason`,
  `alerted_at`, `notes`) are simply absent when empty — a failed record normally
  carries the task fields and not `blocked_reason`, a blocked record the reverse.
- `alert_minutes` rides the list body beside `records`, not on each record.
- The record card on a client displays, in order: the Automaton name (title, or
  id), the status chip (failed/blocked), the owning Automation name with its
  member id when one exists, the failed task title, the task error, the block
  reason, the session end reason, the first-seen time, the alert state (when it
  fired, or that it has not fired yet), one row per retry-budget category (used
  of limit, left), and the overall ceiling when one is set; values the record
  does not carry are simply not shown (this is what the PWA's triage card renders
  from the same contract).
- A read that matches nothing is `records: []` with the same HTTP 200 — not an error.
- Access follows the daemon's rules: bearer token locally, the autonomous read
  capability for federated peers. The same endpoint is listed in the full OpenAPI
  spec (`TriageList`/`TriageRecord` schemas).

chunks.title: Mobile API surface
chunks.heading: Listener auth posture (`/api/health` `listeners`, `server.acknowledge_unauthenticated`)
chunks.body:
## Listener auth posture (`/api/health` `listeners`, `server.acknowledge_unauthenticated`)

`GET /api/health` (no auth) returns, in addition to status/hostname/version/uptime_seconds, a `listeners` array with one entry per daemon listener: `rest`, `rest_tls`, `mcp_sse`, `proxy_sandbox`, `webhook`, `github_webhook`, `twilio_webhook`. Each entry is posture only:

```
{ "name": "rest", "enabled": true,
  "auth_required": false, "loopback": false,
  "acknowledged": false }
```

Fields are booleans: `enabled` (listener enabled in the active config), `auth_required` (a token/secret guards it), `loopback` (bound to `127.0.0.1`/`::1`/`localhost`), `acknowledged` (the operator set `server.acknowledge_unauthenticated`). Bind addresses and token/secret values are never included.

**Client guidance (Android and iPhone):** flag a listener when
`enabled && !auth_required && !loopback && !acknowledged` — the daemon's
"exposed" condition — the same set of listeners the daemon warns about at
start. Clear the flag when the operator sets
`server.acknowledge_unauthenticated` (then `acknowledged` is `true`).

`server.acknowledge_unauthenticated` (bool, default `false`) is read and
written with the standard config endpoints:

```
GET /api/config   → server.acknowledge_unauthenticated
PUT /api/config   { "server.acknowledge_unauthenticated": true }
```

It silences the daemon's startup warning for exposed, unauthenticated,
unacknowledged listeners and sets `acknowledged` in the health `listeners`
array (and in the `listener_*` diagnose checks). It does not change the
bind address, the token, or the warning condition itself.

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.body:
# Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor

**Shipped in v4.1.0 (Sprint S9).** Replaces the flat `/api/stats` scalars with a structured `StatsResponse v2` payload carrying a host envelope, CPU/mem/disk/GPU details, per-process tree rolled up into per-session and per-LLM-backend envelopes, sessions + backend health, and optional cluster / peer views.

Design doc: [`../plans/2026-04-22-bl171-datawatch-observer.md`](../plans/2026-04-22-bl171-datawatch-observer.md).

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Ways to read the data
chunks.body:
## Ways to read the data

- **REST** (v2): `GET /api/stats?v=2` or `GET /api/observer/stats`.
- **REST** (v1 compat): `GET /api/stats` keeps the old flat shape for v1 clients; all flat scalars are also present as top-level aliases inside the v2 response.
- **REST** (BL180 cross-host, v5.12.0): `GET /api/observer/envelopes/all-peers` — federation-aware view; collects local + every peer's last-pushed envelopes and runs `CorrelateAcrossPeers` so cross-peer caller attributions surface as `<peer>:<envelope-id>` rows on each matched server envelope. Response shape: `{by_peer: {peer-name: [Envelope, ...], ...}}`.
- **Live** (WS): `MsgStats` broadcast on the existing `/ws` channel — payload upgraded to StatsResponse v2 at 1 s cadence.
- **MCP tools**: `observer_stats`, `observer_envelopes`, `observer_envelope`, `observer_envelopes_all_peers` (v5.12.0), `observer_config_get`, `observer_config_set`, `observer_peers_list`, `observer_peer_get/register/delete`, `observer_peer_stats`, `observer_agent_list/stats`, `ollama_stats`.
- **CLI**: `datawatch observer stats|envelopes|envelopes-all-peers|envelope <id>|config-get|config-set <json>|peer list|peer register|peer delete|peer stats <name>`.
- **Comm**: via the existing `rest` passthrough (`rest GET /api/observer/envelopes`).

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Envelopes — the headline feature
chunks.body:
## Envelopes — the headline feature

Each tick, every process visible under `/proc` is classified into an **envelope**:

| Kind | ID format | What lands here |
|---|---|---|
| `session` | `session:<full_id>` | tmux-pane PID subtree for every tracked session (claude + spawned shells / helpers / agents) |
| `backend` | `backend:<name>[-docker\|-k8s]` | process subtree rooted at a known LLM backend executable (ollama, aider, goose, gemini, opencode, open-webui) — including children, and any docker / k8s container wrapping it |
| `container` | `container:<short-id>` | any other containerized process we picked up via `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` parsing |
| `system` | `system` | everything that didn't match — kernel threads, root procs, daemons |

Rolled-up metrics per envelope: `cpu_pct`, `rss_bytes`, `fds`, `threads`, `net_rx_bps` + `net_tx_bps` (Shape C eBPF or Shape A/B with CAP_BPF), `gpu_pct` + `gpu_mem_bytes` (when `nvidia-smi` reports compute apps for the subtree's PIDs).

Sorted by CPU descending — the operator sees "which session / backend is eating the box right now" as the first row.

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Deployment shapes
chunks.body:
## Deployment shapes

One wire contract, three deployment options — pick what fits the host:

- **Shape A — in-process plugin (default).** Lives in `internal/observer/`. Unprivileged `/proc` walk + `nvidia-smi` scrape. Default-on; toggle with `observer.plugin_enabled`.
- **Shape B — standalone daemon (`datawatch-stats.service`, Sprint S11).** Tiny binary on a host that isn't running the session manager. Registers with the main daemon over HMAC-auth peer protocol; payload merges into the aggregator's `/api/stats`.
- **Shape C — cluster container (Sprint S12).** Privileged (`CAP_BPF` + `CAP_PERFMON` or `--privileged` + `hostPID: true`). Adds eBPF per-process net, per-cgroup CPU/mem, DCGM GPU, k8s metrics-server scrape.

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: eBPF across all three shapes
chunks.body:
### eBPF across all three shapes

All three shapes share the same eBPF object; privilege is the only difference:

| Shape | Privilege | Enabled via |
|---|---|---|
| A | unprivileged default; CAP_BPF when granted | `datawatch setup ebpf` (adds `AmbientCapabilities=CAP_BPF CAP_PERFMON` drop-in to `datawatch.service` + flips `observer.ebpf_enabled=true`) |
| B | unprivileged default; CAP_BPF when granted | `datawatch setup ebpf` against the `datawatch-stats.service` unit |
| C | **via k8s / docker manifest only** — no runtime `setup ebpf` command | Helm values `securityContext.capabilities.add: [BPF, PERFMON]` (k8s) or `cap_add: [BPF, PERFMON]` + `pid: host` (compose) |

When eBPF is unavailable, the observer silently degrades to `/proc`-only (no `net.per_process[]`, no `envelope.net_*_bps`). Everything else still renders.

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Shape C — Kubernetes snippet
chunks.body:
### Shape C — Kubernetes snippet

```yaml

observerCluster:
  enabled: true
  image: ghcr.io/dmz006/datawatch-stats-cluster:v4.1.0
  securityContext:
    capabilities:
      add: [BPF, PERFMON, SYS_RESOURCE]
  hostPID: true
```

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Shape C — docker-compose snippet
chunks.body:
### Shape C — docker-compose snippet

```yaml
services:
  datawatch-stats-cluster:
    image: ghcr.io/dmz006/datawatch-stats-cluster:v4.1.0
    cap_add: [BPF, PERFMON, SYS_RESOURCE]
    pid: host
    environment:
      DATAWATCH_PRIMARY: https://datawatch.example:8443
      PEER_NAME: cluster-a
```

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Configuration — `observer:` YAML block
chunks.body:
## Configuration — `observer:` YAML block

```yaml
observer:
  plugin_enabled: true              # Shape A toggle
  tick_interval_ms: 1000            # 1 s cadence (minimum 500)
  process_tree_enabled: true
  top_n_broadcast: 200
  include_kthreads: false
  session_attribution: true
  backend_attribution: true
  docker_discovery: true
  gpu_attribution: true
  ebpf_enabled: auto                # auto | true | false — shared across shapes
```

Every knob is reachable from YAML + REST (`/api/observer/config`) + MCP (`observer_config_set`) + CLI (`datawatch observer config-set`) + comm (`rest PUT /api/observer/config {…}`) per the parity rule.

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Wire shape (v2)
chunks.body:
## Wire shape (v2)

See the design doc for the full JSON contract. Highlights:

- `host.shape`: `"plugin"` | `"daemon"` | `"cluster"` — tells the consumer where the data came from.
- `envelopes[]`: sorted by CPU descending, kind-tagged.
- `processes.tree`: top-N by CPU with ancestors preserved so the tree is always connected.
- `peers[]`: populated only on the aggregator (main datawatch) — lists Shape B / C peers + last-push freshness.
- Every v1 flat field (`cpu_pct`, `mem_pct`, `uptime_seconds`, `sessions_total`, `sessions_running`, `disk_pct`, `gpu_pct`) is preserved at the root so v1 clients keep working.

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Sub-process monitoring examples
chunks.body:
## Sub-process monitoring examples

**Track claude's children.** If you start a Claude session and it spawns a shell + `rg` + `grep`, the resulting `session:<full_id>` envelope counts all four processes' CPU/RSS/FD together. Drill in: `datawatch observer envelope session:<full_id>` returns the full subtree.

**Watch ollama's runners.** `ollama serve` forks `ollama-runner` children per model. The `backend:ollama` envelope sums them. If Ollama is running inside a Docker container, the envelope id becomes `backend:ollama-docker` and `envelope.container_id` + `envelope.image` are populated.

**GPU attribution.** `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory` maps compute-using PIDs to GPUs; the observer annotates matching envelopes with `gpu_pct` + `gpu_mem_bytes`.

chunks.title: Observer — unified stats + process-tree + sub-process monitor
chunks.heading: Not in v4.1.0
chunks.body:
## Not in v4.1.0

- Standalone daemon (Shape B) — arrives in Sprint S11 (v4.2.0).
- Cluster container (Shape C) — arrives in Sprint S12 (v4.2.x).
- Per-process eBPF network — library present in Shape A/B, but the kprobes ship in Sprint S12 alongside the cluster container.
- Mobile Phase 1+2 consumption (structured cards, WS live stream) — lands in datawatch-app v0.34.x.

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.body:
# PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)

**Shipped in v4.0.0.** Composes BL24 autonomous PRDs into a graph and
runs each PRD under a **guardrail sub-agent overlay** — every PRD
node is attested by one or more independent validators (rules,
security, release-readiness, docs-diagrams-architecture) before the
DAG advances.

Disabled by default — opt in with `orchestrator.enabled: true`.

Design doc: [`../plans/2026-04-20-bl117-prd-dag-orchestrator.md`](../plans/2026-04-20-bl117-prd-dag-orchestrator.md).

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: Surfaces (full parity)
chunks.body:
## Surfaces (full parity)

| Channel | Entry-point |
|---|---|
| YAML  | `orchestrator:` block |
| REST  | `/api/orchestrator/*` |
| MCP   | `orchestrator_config_get/set`, `orchestrator_graph_*`, `orchestrator_verdicts` |
| CLI   | `datawatch orchestrator <subcmd>` |
| Comm  | via the comm `rest` passthrough |

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: Configuration
chunks.body:
## Configuration

```yaml
orchestrator:
  enabled:                false
  default_guardrails: ["rules", "security", "release-readiness", "docs-diagrams-architecture"]
  guardrail_timeout_ms:   120000      # 2 min per guardrail
  guardrail_backend:      ""          # empty = inherit session.llm_backend
  max_parallel_prds:      2           # per-graph PRD parallelism
```

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: REST endpoints
chunks.body:
## REST endpoints

```
GET    /api/orchestrator/config
PUT    /api/orchestrator/config

POST   /api/orchestrator/graphs                 body: {title, project_dir, prd_ids, [deps]}
GET    /api/orchestrator/graphs                 list
GET    /api/orchestrator/graphs/{id}            one graph with node tree + verdicts
DELETE /api/orchestrator/graphs/{id}            cancel
POST   /api/orchestrator/graphs/{id}/plan       rebuild node tree
POST   /api/orchestrator/graphs/{id}/run        fire-and-forget runner

GET    /api/orchestrator/verdicts               flatten guardrail verdicts across graphs
```

When `orchestrator.enabled` is false, every endpoint returns `503`.

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: Graph model
chunks.body:
## Graph model

Each graph is a DAG of **Nodes**. Two node kinds:

| Kind        | Contents | Wrapped work |
|-------------|----------|--------------|
| `prd`       | `prd_id` | BL24 autonomous PRD execution (via `/api/autonomous/prds/{id}/run` loopback) |
| `guardrail` | `prd_id, guardrail` | One attestation per (PRD × guardrail) |

`Plan` generates one PRD node per PRD ID, then one guardrail node per
(PRD × configured guardrail). Operator-supplied `deps` (PRD → [PRDs])
become node-level dependencies so downstream PRDs wait for upstream
PRDs and their guardrails.

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: Verdicts
chunks.body:
## Verdicts

Each guardrail returns a Verdict:

```json
{"outcome": "pass | warn | block",
 "severity": "info | low | medium | high | critical",
 "summary": "…", "issues": ["…"]}
```

`block` halts the DAG — the graph status becomes `blocked` and
operator intervention is required. `warn` records the verdict without
halting. `pass` clears the node.

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: CLI
chunks.body:
## CLI

```
datawatch orchestrator config-get
datawatch orchestrator config-set '{"enabled":true}'

datawatch orchestrator graph-list
datawatch orchestrator graph-create "ship v4.0" '["prd1","prd2"]' '{"prd2":["prd1"]}'
datawatch orchestrator graph-get <id>
datawatch orchestrator graph-plan <id> '{"prd2":["prd1"]}'
datawatch orchestrator graph-run <id>
datawatch orchestrator graph-cancel <id>
datawatch orchestrator verdicts
```

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: MCP tools (AI-ready)
chunks.body:
## MCP tools (AI-ready)

Typical AI workflow:
1. `autonomous_prd_create` + `autonomous_prd_decompose` for each PRD.
2. `orchestrator_graph_create(title, prd_ids, deps)`.
3. `orchestrator_graph_run(id)`.
4. Poll `orchestrator_graph_get(id)` until `status` is `completed` or `blocked`.
5. On `blocked`, inspect the `Verdict` of the offending node, fix, re-run.

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: Guardrails — v1 stub
chunks.body:
## Guardrails — v1 stub

v4.0.0 ships with a **stub GuardrailFn** that returns `pass` with an
informational summary per guardrail name. This lets the graph
structure + DAG traversal + verdict persistence ship end-to-end while
the concrete BL103-validator-image wiring for each guardrail type
(rules checklist evaluation, security diff review, release-readiness
gate, docs integrity checker) lands as v4.0.x patches.

To author a real guardrail today, register a **plugin** (BL33) on the
`on_guardrail` hook — the orchestrator will prefer plugin verdicts
over the stub when the hook is declared. Plugin manifest:

```yaml
name: my-rules-check
entry: ./check
hooks: [on_guardrail]
```

and the plugin receives the same `GuardrailRequest` JSON as the built-in stub.

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: Storage
chunks.body:
## Storage

Graphs persist as JSON-lines under `<data_dir>/orchestrator/graphs.jsonl`.
Full rewrite on every update; small-dataset assumption.

---

chunks.title: PRD-DAG orchestrator (v4.0.0 — BL117)
chunks.heading: Non-goals
chunks.body:
## Non-goals

- Not a replacement for BL24 — composes its PRDs.
- Not a replacement for F10 — every node ultimately spawns an F10
  worker.
- Not a replacement for `pipeline.Executor` — that runs the *task*
  DAG inside a single PRD; the orchestrator runs the *PRD* DAG above it.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.body:
# Plugin framework (v3.11.0)

**Shipped in v3.11.0.** Subprocess plugin framework — external
binaries or scripts the daemon discovers under
`<data_dir>/plugins/<name>/`, invokes per-hook via line-oriented
JSON-RPC over stdio, and reaps when done.

Disabled by default — opt in by setting `plugins.enabled: true`.

Design doc: `docs/plans/2026-04-20-bl33-plugin-framework.md`.

---

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: ⚠️ Security
chunks.body:
## ⚠️ Security

Plugins run **in-process as a subprocess** — same privileges as the
daemon. They can read every file the daemon can and make network
calls. **Install only plugins you've reviewed.** No sandboxing in v1;
container-based isolation is a future v3.12.x patch.

---

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Quickstart
chunks.body:
## Quickstart

```sh
# 1. Write the plugin
mkdir -p ~/.datawatch/plugins/my-filter
cat > ~/.datawatch/plugins/my-filter/manifest.yaml <<'YAML'
name: my-filter
description: Redact API keys from session output.
version: 0.1.0
entry: ./filter
hooks:
  - post_session_output
timeout_ms: 1500
YAML
cat > ~/.datawatch/plugins/my-filter/filter <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
read line
echo "$line" | grep -qE 'sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}' \
  && echo '{"action":"replace","line":"[redacted]"}' \
  || echo '{"action":"pass"}'
SH
chmod +x ~/.datawatch/plugins/my-filter/filter

# 2. Enable plugins globally
datawatch plugins reload     # rescan after install

# 3. Verify
datawatch plugins list
datawatch plugins test my-filter post_session_output '{"line":"sk-abcd1234567890abcdef"}'
```

---

```
POST   /api/plugins/{name}/widgets/token        mint/rotate the widget push token (v9.0.40)
POST   /api/plugins/{name}/widgets/{widget_id}  push a widget value, plugin push token (v9.0.40)
GET    /api/plugins/{name}/widgets              declared widgets + latest values (v9.0.40)
GET    /api/plugins/{name}/widgets/{widget_id}  one widget + latest value (v9.0.40)
```

The widget endpoints are described under [Widgets](#widgets-v9040).

When `plugins.enabled` is false, every endpoint returns
`503 plugins disabled`.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Community registry install + browse (v8.1.0)
chunks.body:
### Community registry install + browse (v8.1.0)

Two additional endpoints for installing plugins from a registry and
browsing registry contents.

**POST /api/plugins/install**

Install a plugin from a named registry.

Request body:
```json
{"registry": "<registry-name>", "name": "<plugin-name>"}
```

Response:
```json
{"status": "ok", "installed": "<name>", "from_registry": "<registry>"}
```

The daemon downloads the plugin into `<data_dir>/plugins/<name>/`,
validates the manifest, and makes it available immediately. A
`plugins reload` is not required after install.

**GET /api/plugins/browse?registry=\<name\>**

List all plugins available in a named registry.

Response:
```json
{
  "registry": "<name>",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "...",
      "path": "...",
      "manifest": {
        "name": "...",
        "description": "...",
        "version": "...",
        "author": "...",
        "license": "...",
        "category": "...",
        "hooks": ["..."],
        "contributor_notes": "...",
        "datawatch_min_version": "..."
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The community registry is pre-seeded as the first registry by default
at `https://github.com/dmz006/datawatch-community`. Use
`datawatch plugins browse-registry community` to list it without any
additional setup.

```sh
export BASE=https://localhost:8443
export TOKEN=<your_bearer_token>

# Browse the default community registry.
curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "$BASE/api/plugins/browse?registry=community"

# Install a plugin from the community registry.
curl -sk -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"registry": "community", "name": "redact-secrets"}' \
  "$BASE/api/plugins/install"
```

---

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Plugin contract
chunks.body: ## Plugin contract

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Manifest (`manifest.yaml`)
chunks.body:
### Manifest (`manifest.yaml`)

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name`        | yes | Unique plugin name |
| `entry`       | yes (automation) | Executable path; relative paths are resolved against the plugin dir |
| `hooks`       | yes (automation) | List of hook names this plugin registers for |
| `description` | no  | Human-readable one-liner |
| `version`     | no  | Freeform version string |
| `timeout_ms`  | no  | Per-invocation timeout (overrides global `plugins.timeout_ms`) |
| `mode`        | no  | **Deprecated, ignored** (since v9.0.31). Parsed for one more release so existing manifests still load, then removed. Use `kind` instead. |
| `kind`        | no  | `automation` (default when absent — fork-per-call hook subprocess, the v2.1 behavior) or `service` (a persistent external process datawatch talks to as a client). Case-insensitive. Manifest v3, v9.0.31. |
| `connection`  | yes when `kind: service` | How datawatch reaches a service-kind plugin. See the `connection.*` rows. |
| `connection.base_url`    | yes when `kind: service` | Absolute `http://` or `https://` URL of the running service. |
| `connection.auth.type`   | no  | Auth scheme. Only `bearer` is supported; empty means `bearer`. |
| `connection.auth.token`  | yes when `connection.auth` is set | Exactly one `${secret:NAME}` reference — never a literal credential. Only the reference shape is validated; the secret is resolved at use time. |
| `connection.health_path` | no  | Path (relative to `base_url`) for health probing in either lifecycle mode. |
| `lifecycle`   | no  | Only allowed when `kind: service` (rejected on automation manifests). Absent means attach-only. See the `lifecycle.*` rows. |
| `lifecycle.supported_modes` | yes when `lifecycle` is set | Non-empty list of `attach_only` and/or `managed`, no duplicates. Author-declared: the operator's later mode choice is limited to what is listed here. |
| `lifecycle.entry`           | yes when `managed` is listed | Executable to launch for managed mode (relative to the plugin dir, or absolute). |
| `lifecycle.args`            | no  | Arguments passed to `lifecycle.entry` (managed mode only). |
| `lifecycle.restart_policy`  | no  | `on-failure`, `always` or `never`. Empty = supervisor default. |
| `lifecycle.stop_timeout_ms` | no  | Grace period before a managed process is killed on stop. Must be `>= 0`; `0` = supervisor default. |
| `widgets`     | no  | List of dashboard/session widgets, allowed on both kinds. See [Widgets](#widgets-v9040) for the per-widget fields. v9.0.40. |

Unknown keys are ignored, so a manifest written for a newer daemon
still loads on an older one. A manifest that fails validation is
skipped at discovery (logged to stderr) and rejected by
`POST /api/plugins/install`.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Service-kind plugins (manifest v3)
chunks.body:
### Service-kind plugins (manifest v3)

Added in v9.0.31. A `kind: service` plugin is a long-running process
or server that datawatch connects to as a client, instead of a
subprocess it forks per hook call. The plugin stays a standalone
program: it must work on its own, without datawatch. The `connection`
block is what datawatch needs to attach to it. The optional
`lifecycle` block says whether datawatch may also start and supervise
that same binary.

```yaml
name: mail-service
description: Mail triage service exposed to datawatch.
version: 1.4.0
kind: service
connection:
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8765
  health_path: /healthz
  auth:
    type: bearer
    token: ${secret:mail-service-token}   # secrets-store ref, never a literal
lifecycle:
  supported_modes: [attach_only, managed]
  entry: bin/mail-service                 # required because managed is listed
  args: ["--listen", "127.0.0.1:8765"]
  restart_policy: on-failure
  stop_timeout_ms: 5000
```

- **`attach_only`**: datawatch only connects to an instance that is
  already running. It never starts or stops it.
- **`managed`**: datawatch starts the same binary as a child process,
  health-checks it, restarts it per `restart_policy`, and stops it.
- The plugin author declares which modes the plugin supports. The
  operator can only choose from what the author listed.
- Service-kind plugins are **never invoked as hooks**. Any `hooks:`
  list on a service manifest is ignored, and `POST /api/plugins/{name}/test`
  returns an error for them.

**What ships when.** v9.0.31 added parsing and validation of
service-kind manifests (discovery, install,
`scripts/check-plugin-manifests.sh`, and the `kind` / `connection` /
`lifecycle` fields in `GET /api/plugins`). v9.0.32 adds the runtime
for `managed` mode, described below. `attach_only` still does nothing
at runtime: datawatch does not yet connect to or health-probe an
attach-only service.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Managed mode at runtime (v9.0.32)
chunks.body:
#### Managed mode at runtime (v9.0.32)

datawatch supervises a service plugin only when **all** of these hold:

1. `kind: service` and the author lists `managed` in
   `lifecycle.supported_modes` (the ceiling: an operator cannot force
   a mode the author did not declare);
2. the operator has opted the plugin in (see below);
3. the plugin is enabled, and `plugins.enabled` is on.

Anything else (automation plugins, attach-only plugins, plugins not
opted in) is never started, stopped or probed. Nothing is spawned
until the daemon has finished starting its plugin subsystem.

**Opting in.** Persistently, in `~/.datawatch/config.yaml`:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled: true
  managed:
    - mail-service        # names of service plugins datawatch may supervise
```

At runtime over REST (in memory, like enable/disable; add the name to
`plugins.managed` to keep it across restarts):

```bash
curl -sk -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"managed": true}' \
  "$BASE/api/plugins/mail-service/enable"
```

`{"managed": false}` opts out (and stops the service); an empty body
leaves the opt-in unchanged. The endpoint returns `400` when the
plugin does not declare `managed` support or the body is malformed,
and `404` when the plugin is unknown. Over MCP, `plugin_enable` takes
the same optional boolean: `plugin_enable(name="mail-service",
managed=true)`; the body is sent only when `managed` is given.

**Lifecycle.**

- **Start** — at daemon boot, and whenever a plugin becomes eligible
  later (enabled, opted in, or newly found by `POST /api/plugins/reload`
  or the dir watcher). `lifecycle.entry` runs with `lifecycle.args` in
  the plugin dir as a child process in its own process group. Env is
  built the same way as for hook plugins, so `${secret:NAME}` env
  values work.
- **Health** — with `connection.health_path` set, datawatch GETs
  `base_url` + `health_path` every 5s, sending the resolved
  `connection.auth` bearer token when configured. The first 2xx marks
  the service `healthy`. A health failure is either no 2xx within 30s
  of launch, or 3 consecutive failed probes after the service was
  healthy (it shows as `unhealthy` in between). On a health failure the
  child is stopped and the restart policy decides what happens next.
  Without a `health_path`, a process still running 30s after launch is
  treated as healthy.
- **Restart** — per `lifecycle.restart_policy`:

  | Policy | Non-zero exit / signal / health failure | Clean exit 0 |
  |---|---|---|
  | `on-failure` (default) | restart | stop (state `stopped`) |
  | `always` | restart | restart |
  | `never` | no restart (state `crashed`) | no restart (state `stopped`) |

  Restarts back off exponentially: 1s, 2s, 4s, … capped at 30s.
- **Give-up** — after 5 restarts in a row without a stable run (the
  6th consecutive failure), datawatch stops supervising and leaves the
  service in state `failed`. A run that stays healthy for 60s resets
  the failure count. To try again, disable and re-enable the plugin
  (or restart the daemon).
- **Stop** — disabling the plugin, opting it out, removing it from the
  plugin dir, and daemon shutdown all stop the service: SIGTERM to the
  process group, then SIGKILL if it is still running after
  `lifecycle.stop_timeout_ms` (default 10s). datawatch waits for the
  child to be reaped. On shutdown all managed services stop
  concurrently, bounded at 30s overall. A hot-reload of the plugin dir
  never orphans a running child.

**Status.** `GET /api/plugins` and `GET /api/plugins/{name}` add a
`service` object to any plugin that currently has a supervisor
(plugins without one are unchanged):

```json
"service": {
  "state": "healthy",
  "pid": 41237,
  "restarts": 1,
  "last_error": "process exited: exit status 2"
}
```

`state` is one of `stopped`, `starting`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`,
`crashed`, `restarting`, `failed`, `stopping`. `pid` and
`last_error` are omitted when empty.

**Audit events.** Every lifecycle transition is written to the audit
log with actor `daemon`, resource type `plugin` and the plugin name,
and also printed to the daemon log:

| Action | When | Details |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin_service_start` | a child process is launched (first start and each restart) | `pid`, `restarts` |
| `plugin_service_restart` | a run ended and the policy will restart it | `restarts`, `backoff_ms`, `exit_code`, `error`, `health_fail` |
| `plugin_service_health_fail` | startup deadline missed or probe-failure threshold reached | `reason` (`startup_deadline` / `probe_failures`), `error`, `url` |
| `plugin_service_stop` | requested stop, a run the policy won't restart, or give-up | `reason` (`requested` / `exited` / `max_restarts`), plus `state`, `exit_code`, `error`, `consecutive_failures` when not requested |

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Widgets (v9.0.40)
chunks.body:
### Widgets (v9.0.40)

Added in v9.0.40. A plugin of either kind can declare **widgets**:
small tiles of plugin data for the dashboard or a session view. Each
widget gets its data in one of two ways. In **pull** mode the daemon
fetches the value on an interval. In **push** mode the plugin sends
the value whenever it wants. You choose the mode per widget, so one
plugin can mix both.

**What ships when.** v9.0.40 ships the data model and transport:
manifest validation, pulling, the push endpoint, push tokens, storage
and the read endpoints below. The release after v9.0.40 adds the PWA
renderer:

- **Dashboard widgets** (`surface: dashboard`) are added one at a time
  from the dashboard's **Add Card** panel. Once added, a widget card
  can be moved, resized and removed like any other card.
- **Session widgets** (`surface: session`) appear in every session's
  detail view. A widget has one value, so it shows the same data no
  matter which session is open.
- Widgets of a **disabled** plugin show as unavailable. The read
  endpoints still return their stored value, but the PWA does not
  display it.

MCP, CLI, comm-channel and mobile-app widget surfaces come in a later
release. On those surfaces, the read endpoints are the only way to
see a widget's value.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Manifest `widgets:` fields
chunks.body:
#### Manifest `widgets:` fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id`               | yes | Unique within the manifest. Used in the push and read URLs. `token` is reserved and rejected. |
| `surface`          | yes | Where the widget will render: `dashboard` or `session`. |
| `kind`             | yes | How it will render: `stat_tile`, `table`, `list`, `sparkline`, `status_badge` or `markdown`. |
| `data_mode`        | yes | `pull` (the daemon fetches the value) or `push` (the plugin posts it). |
| `pull_path`        | pull only | Required when `data_mode: pull`, and must be empty for `push`. On `kind: service` it is a path appended to `connection.base_url` and must start with `/`. On `kind: automation` it is passed to the plugin in the `status_poll` request, so a plugin with several pull widgets can tell them apart. |
| `interval_seconds` | no  | Pull interval in seconds (pull only). `0` or unset means 30s. Negative values are rejected. |

An invalid `widgets:` block fails validation like any other manifest
error: the plugin is skipped at discovery and rejected by
`POST /api/plugins/install`.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Widget value shapes
chunks.body:
#### Widget value shapes

The daemon stores whatever JSON a plugin sends (up to 64 KiB) without
checking it against the widget's `kind`. The PWA reads the `data`
field of the value and expects this shape for each `kind`:

| `kind` | Expected `data` | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `stat_tile`    | `{value: number\|string, label?: string, unit?: string, detail?: string}` | `{"value": 42, "label": "queued jobs"}` |
| `table`        | `{columns: [string], rows: [[cell, ...]]}`. A cell is a string, number, boolean or `null`. A row can also be an object keyed by column name. | `{"columns": ["job", "state"], "rows": [["#812", "passed"], {"job": "#811", "state": "failed"}]}` |
| `list`         | `{items: [string \| {text: string, detail?: string}]}` | `{"items": ["#812 passed", {"text": "#811 failed", "detail": "lint"}]}` |
| `sparkline`    | `{points: [number], label?: string, value?: number\|string}`. Points that are not finite numbers are dropped. | `{"points": [3, 5, 4, 8], "label": "builds/hour", "value": 8}` |
| `status_badge` | `{status: "ok"\|"warn"\|"error"\|"unknown", label?: string, detail?: string}`. Any other `status` shows as `unknown`. Without a `label`, the badge shows the status name. | `{"status": "warn", "label": "disk 85%"}` |
| `markdown`     | `{text: string}`, or a bare JSON string. | `{"text": "**3** builds queued"}` |

How the PWA handles values:

- **Mismatched values render as empty.** If `data` does not match its
  kind's shape (wrong type, missing required field, nothing usable
  left), the widget shows its quiet "No data yet" state. It never
  shows an error and never breaks the dashboard. The same goes for a
  widget that has no value yet.
- **Strings are always text.** Every plugin-supplied string is
  HTML-escaped before display, so markup in `data` shows as literal
  text. Nested objects or arrays in a table cell or list field show
  as blank. The one exception is `markdown`: its text goes through
  the dashboard's existing markdown renderer, which sanitizes the
  resulting HTML.
- **Pull errors.** When the latest pull failed, the value carries an
  `error`. The widget keeps showing the previous data and adds a small
  ⚠ marker whose tooltip shows the error.
- **Size caps.** The renderer shows at most 50 table rows, 20 table
  columns, 50 list items and the most recent 500 sparkline points.
  When rows or items are cut, the widget shows a `+N` line with the
  number left out. Long strings are shortened with `…` and the full
  text is kept in a tooltip: a stat or sparkline value at 24
  characters, a unit at 16, a label at 40, a `detail` at 120, a table
  header at 28,
  a table cell at 40, and a list item's text and detail at 60 and 80.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Pull mode
chunks.body:
#### Pull mode

The daemon runs one pull worker per pull widget of each **enabled**
plugin. Workers follow plugin reloads and enable/disable changes. The
first pull happens right away, then one per interval. Each widget is
isolated: a slow or hung pull only delays that widget. A tick that
arrives while the widget's previous pull is still running is skipped,
not queued. A pull is cut off at the widget's interval at the latest.

- **`kind: automation`**: the daemon invokes the plugin's
  `status_poll` hook through the normal hook path (same subprocess,
  env, `${secret:…}` handling and `timeout_ms` budget as every other
  hook; see below).
- **`kind: service`**: the daemon sends
  `GET <connection.base_url><pull_path>` with `Accept: application/json`.
  When `connection.auth` is set, it adds
  `Authorization: Bearer <resolved secret>`. The service must answer
  `2xx` with a JSON body of at most 64 KiB. The body is stored as the
  widget value, unchanged.

A failed pull records an `error` on the widget and **keeps the previous
value**. A failure is an error response, a non-2xx status, a timeout,
invalid JSON or a body over 64 KiB.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: The `status_poll` hook
chunks.body:
#### The `status_poll` hook

`status_poll` is a oneshot hook, like the other hooks. List it under
`hooks:` in an automation plugin that has pull widgets.

Request (one line on stdin):

```json
{"hook":"status_poll","payload":{"widget_id":"queue-depth","pull_path":"/queue","surface":"dashboard","kind":"stat_tile"}}
```

Response (one line on stdout):

```json
{"fields":{"data":{"value":42,"label":"queued"}}}
```

- The widget value is `fields.data`. If there is no `data` key, the
  whole `fields` object is the value. It is stored as JSON (at most
  64 KiB).
- A non-empty `error`, a missing `fields` object, a timeout or a
  non-zero exit is a failed pull: the error is recorded and the widget
  keeps its previous value.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Push mode and push tokens
chunks.body:
#### Push mode and push tokens

A plugin pushes a value with
`POST /api/plugins/{name}/widgets/{widget_id}`. The request body **is**
the widget value: any JSON document, at most 64 KiB, stored unchanged.

Pushes use a **plugin-scoped push token**, not the operator token. Mint
it once with operator auth (config-write capability) and hand it to the
plugin process, for example via the secrets store:

```bash
# Mint (or rotate) the push token for plugin "build-feed". The token is
# returned once; only a bcrypt hash is kept, in
# <data_dir>/plugins/widget_tokens.json.
curl -sk -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "$BASE/api/plugins/build-feed/widgets/token"
# → {"token":"q3V…"}
```

Calling the endpoint again **rotates** the token: the old one stops
working immediately. A token only authenticates `POST` to that one
plugin's push route. It is not accepted by any other endpoint, by
another plugin's push route, or by the read endpoints. The operator
token is not accepted on the push route either.

Push responses:

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `200` | Stored. Body: `{"updated_at":"<RFC 3339 time>"}` |
| `400` | Body is empty or not valid JSON |
| `401` | Missing bearer token, wrong token, another plugin's token, or the operator token |
| `404` | Unknown plugin, or the plugin does not declare that widget |
| `409` | The widget is `data_mode: pull`, so pushes are refused |
| `413` | Body over 64 KiB |
| `503` | Widgets unavailable: `plugins.enabled` is off |

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Read endpoints
chunks.body:
#### Read endpoints

Both need operator auth (config-read capability).

```bash
# Every widget a plugin declares, each with its latest value.
curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$BASE/api/plugins/build-feed/widgets"

# One widget.
curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$BASE/api/plugins/build-feed/widgets/recent-builds"
```

```json
{
  "plugin": "build-feed",
  "widgets": [
    {
      "id": "recent-builds",
      "surface": "session",
      "kind": "list",
      "data_mode": "push",
      "value": {
        "plugin": "build-feed",
        "widget_id": "recent-builds",
        "data": {"items": ["#812 passed", "#811 failed"]},
        "updated_at": "2026-10-12T07:15:02Z",
        "source": "push"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The single-widget endpoint returns one entry of that `widgets` array.
`value` is `null` until data arrives. `source` is `push` or `pull`.
`error` holds the last pull error and is omitted when there is none.
Unknown plugin or undeclared widget → `404`; plugins disabled → `503`.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Storage
chunks.body:
#### Storage

The daemon keeps one latest value per (plugin, widget) in memory. It
writes them to `<data_dir>/plugins/widgets.json` every 60s if anything
changed, and once more on shutdown. Widgets keep their last value
across a daemon restart.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Example: a pull widget on an automation plugin
chunks.body:
#### Example: a pull widget on an automation plugin

`~/.datawatch/plugins/queue-stats/manifest.yaml`:

```yaml
name: queue-stats
description: Show the job queue depth on the dashboard.
version: 0.1.0
entry: ./poll.py
hooks: [status_poll]
timeout_ms: 1500
widgets:
  - id: queue-depth
    surface: dashboard
    kind: stat_tile
    data_mode: pull
    pull_path: /queue          # passed through to status_poll
    interval_seconds: 15
```

`~/.datawatch/plugins/queue-stats/poll.py` (make it executable):

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, os, sys

req = json.loads(sys.stdin.readline())
if req.get("hook") == "status_poll":
    payload = req.get("payload", {})
    if payload.get("pull_path") == "/queue":
        depth = len(os.listdir("/var/spool/jobs"))   # your data source
        print(json.dumps({"fields": {"data": {"value": depth, "label": "queued jobs"}}}))
    else:
        print(json.dumps({"error": "unknown widget " + payload.get("widget_id", "")}))
    sys.exit(0)
print(json.dumps({"action": "pass"}))
```

After `datawatch plugins reload`, the daemon calls `poll.py` every 15s.
`GET /api/plugins/queue-stats/widgets/queue-depth` returns the latest
value with `"source": "pull"`.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Example: a push widget on a service plugin
chunks.body:
#### Example: a push widget on a service plugin

`~/.datawatch/plugins/build-feed/manifest.yaml`:

```yaml
name: build-feed
description: Recent CI builds, pushed by the build-feed service.
version: 1.0.0
kind: service
connection:
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8770
  auth:
    type: bearer
    token: ${secret:build-feed-token}
widgets:
  - id: recent-builds
    surface: session
    kind: list
    data_mode: push
```

Mint the push token once (see above), give it to the service, and the
service pushes whenever its data changes:

```bash
curl -sk -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WIDGET_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":["#812 passed","#811 failed"]}' \
  "$BASE/api/plugins/build-feed/widgets/recent-builds"
# → {"updated_at":"2026-10-12T07:15:02.481Z"}
```

`connection.auth` is for calls from datawatch to the service, such as
pulls and health probes. The push token is for calls from the service
to datawatch. They are separate credentials.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Hooks (v1 set)
chunks.body:
### Hooks (v1 set)

| Hook | When | Input fields | Expected response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pre_session_start`      | Before `Session.Start` | `task, project_dir, backend, effort` | `{action:"pass"\|"block"\|"mutate", fields:{...}}` |
| `post_session_output`    | Per output chunk       | `session_id, line`                   | `{action:"pass"\|"drop"\|"replace", line:"…"}` |
| `post_session_complete`  | On session end         | `session_id, status, cost`           | `{ok:true}` — fire-and-forget |
| `on_alert`               | Before alert emission  | `severity, channel, text`            | `{ok:true}` — fire-and-forget |
| `status_poll`            | On a pull widget's interval (automation plugins, v9.0.40) | `payload: {widget_id, pull_path, surface, kind}` | `{fields:{data: <widget value>}}`. See [The status_poll hook](#the-status_poll-hook) |

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: JSON-RPC over stdio
chunks.body:
### JSON-RPC over stdio

- **Stdin**: one JSON object, newline-terminated.
- **Stdout**: one JSON object response, newline-terminated.
- **Stderr**: captured into the daemon audit log on non-zero exit.

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Failure policy
chunks.body:
### Failure policy

- **Timeout**: response treated as `{action:"pass"}`; error recorded.
- **Non-zero exit**: response treated as `{action:"pass"}`; error
  recorded; plugin's error counter increments but is not disabled.
- **Invalid JSON on stdout**: response discarded, `{action:"pass"}`
  applied.
- **Plugins never block the hot path**: `post_session_output` runs
  through a bounded per-plugin channel.

---

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Fan-out for filter hooks
chunks.body:
## Fan-out for filter hooks

When multiple plugins register for the same `post_session_output`
hook, the daemon chains them in plugin-name alphabetical order. Each
`replace` feeds into the next plugin's `line` input; the first `drop`
stops the chain. Operators who need a specific ordering should name
their plugins with a numeric prefix (e.g. `00-redact`, `10-trim`).

---

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Example plugin (Python)
chunks.body:
## Example plugin (Python)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, sys
req = json.loads(sys.stdin.readline())
if req.get("hook") == "post_session_output":
    line = req.get("line", "")
    if "PASSWORD" in line:
        print(json.dumps({"action": "replace", "line": "[redacted]"}))
        sys.exit(0)
print(json.dumps({"action": "pass"}))
```

Manifest:
```yaml
name: py-redact
entry: ./redact.py
hooks: [post_session_output]
```

---

chunks.title: Plugin framework (v3.11.0)
chunks.heading: Not in v1
chunks.body:
## Not in v1

Deferred to later patches:
- Long-lived plugins — now declared with `kind: service` (manifest v3,
  v9.0.31; see [Service-kind plugins](#service-kind-plugins-manifest-v3)).
  Manifests are parsed and validated; attaching to and supervising
  the running service is still deferred to a later release.
- Per-plugin container sandboxing.
- Hot reload via filesystem watcher (SIGHUP + `POST
  /api/plugins/reload` is enough for v1).
- Plugin signature verification / code-signing (install from registry
  shipped in v8.1.0; signing/verification remains deferred).
- Go `.so` loading — intentionally rejected; Go plugins lock to exact
  toolchain + CGO + glibc versions and rebreak on every daemon rebuild.

# `GET /api/project/summary` — project overview

**Shipped in v3.5.0 (BL35).** Returns a structured snapshot of a
project directory: git status, recent commits, sessions that have
worked on the directory, and aggregated stats. Read-only.

---

chunks.title: `GET /api/project/summary` — project overview
chunks.heading: When to use
chunks.body:
## When to use

- An AI agent landing on a new task wants situational awareness:
  what's the branch, what's been done here recently, did past
  sessions succeed?
- An operator wants a one-glance "current state" of a workspace from
  a comm channel or terminal without opening the web UI.
- A wrapper script wants per-project rollups for dashboards.

---

chunks.title: `GET /api/project/summary` — project overview
chunks.heading: Endpoint
chunks.body:
## Endpoint

```
GET /api/project/summary?dir=<absolute-path>
```

chunks.title: `GET /api/project/summary` — project overview

chunks.title: `GET /api/project/summary` — project overview

When the directory is not a git repo, `is_git_repo: false` and the

- `dir` MUST be absolute. If your runtime gives you a relative path,
  resolve it first (`os.path.abspath` etc.) before calling.

chunks.title: Routing rules — backend auto-selection (BL20)
chunks.body:
# Routing rules — backend auto-selection (BL20)

**Shipped in v3.9.0.** Pattern-driven backend dispatch on session
start. The first matching rule overrides any default; no match falls
through to the request's explicit backend or `session.llm_backend`.

---

chunks.title: Routing rules — backend auto-selection (BL20)
chunks.heading: When to use
chunks.body:
## When to use

- Route "fix the test" / "add tests" tasks to claude-code while
  letting Ollama handle quick research questions.
- Route privacy-sensitive prompts to a local backend (`ollama`,
  `openwebui`) regardless of operator default.
- A/B which backend handles which kind of work without changing
  every operator command.

---

chunks.title: Routing rules — backend auto-selection (BL20)
chunks.heading: Configuration
chunks.body:
## Configuration

```yaml
session:
  routing_rules:
    - pattern:     "(?i)(test|spec|coverage)"
      backend:     "claude-code"
      description: "Test work goes to Claude"
    - pattern:     "(?i)(quick|small|tiny)"
      backend:     "ollama"
      description: "Trivial tasks go local"
    - pattern:     "(?i)refactor"
      backend:     "opencode"
      description: "Refactors prefer opencode's wider context"
```

`pattern` is a Go regexp matched against the task text on session
start. `backend` is any registered LLM backend name. `description` is
operator-facing context.

Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins. An empty
`routing_rules` list disables auto-selection.

---

chunks.title: Secrets Manager API (BL242)
chunks.body:
# Secrets Manager API (BL242)

Centralized encrypted secrets store with scope enforcement, three storage backends, and cross-surface access (REST, MCP, CLI, comm channel, PWA). Shipped across v6.4.0–v6.4.7.

chunks.title: Secrets Manager API (BL242)
chunks.heading: REST Endpoints
chunks.body:
## REST Endpoints

All endpoints except `/api/agents/secrets/{name}` require the operator bearer token.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/secrets` | List all secrets (names/tags only; no values) |
| `POST` | `/api/secrets` | Create a secret |
| `GET` | `/api/secrets/{name}` | Get a secret with its value (audited) |
| `PUT` | `/api/secrets/{name}` | Update a secret |
| `DELETE` | `/api/secrets/{name}` | Delete a secret |
| `GET` | `/api/secrets/{name}/exists` | Check existence without revealing value |
| `GET` | `/api/agents/secrets/{name}` | Agent runtime fetch — bearer token is the per-agent SecretsToken (pre-auth, scope-enforced) |

chunks.title: Secrets Manager API (BL242)
chunks.heading: Create / Update body
chunks.body:
### Create / Update body

```json
{
  "name": "github-token",
  "value": "ghp_...",
  "tags": ["git"],
  "description": "GitHub PAT for CI worker",
  "scopes": ["agent:ci-runner", "plugin:gh-hooks"]
}
```

`scopes` — optional list of `type:name` entries that restrict access to specific callers. Empty = universally accessible. Supported types:
- `agent:<profileName>` — only agents whose project profile name matches
- `agent:*` — all agents
- `plugin:<pluginName>` — only the named plugin
- `plugin:*` — all plugins

Operators (REST/MCP/CLI with daemon token) always bypass scope checks.

chunks.title: Secrets Manager API (BL242)
chunks.heading: Agent runtime access
chunks.body:
### Agent runtime access

Workers spawned by the daemon receive `DATAWATCH_SECRETS_TOKEN` and `DATAWATCH_SECRETS_URL` in their environment (set by `ApplyBootstrapEnv`). Use the worker SDK:

```go
import "github.com/dmz006/datawatch/internal/agents"

val, err := agents.FetchSecret(ctx, "github-token")
// Returns agents.ErrSecretsUnavailable if the parent has no secrets store
// Returns an error with "access denied (scope)" if the secret is out of scope
```

Or call the endpoint directly:

```
GET /api/agents/secrets/{name}
Authorization: Bearer <DATAWATCH_SECRETS_TOKEN>
```

Tokens are revoked when the agent terminates. Each child agent mints its own token.

chunks.title: Secrets Manager API (BL242)
chunks.heading: Config Reference (`datawatch.yaml`)
chunks.body:
## Config Reference (`datawatch.yaml`)

```yaml
secrets:
  backend: builtin          # builtin | keepass | onepassword

  # KeePass backend
  keepass_db: /path/to/vault.kdbx
  keepass_binary: keepassxc-cli   # default
  keepass_group: datawatch        # optional group scope
  # keepass_password: set via DATAWATCH_KEEPASS_PASSWORD env var

  # 1Password backend
  op_vault: ""              # default vault when omitted
  # op_token: set via DATAWATCH_OP_TOKEN env var
```

chunks.title: Secrets Manager API (BL242)
chunks.heading: Secret references in config
chunks.body:
## Secret references in config

Fields in `datawatch.yaml` can reference secrets:

```yaml
messaging:
  discord:
    token: "${secret:discord-token}"
  slack:
    token: "${secret:slack-token}"
```

Resolved at daemon startup and on hot-reload (`/api/reload`).

chunks.title: Secrets Manager API (BL242)
chunks.heading: Plugin env injection
chunks.body:
## Plugin env injection

Plugin manifests can declare env vars that are resolved from the secrets store at invoke time:

```yaml
# <data_dir>/plugins/my-plugin/manifest.yaml
name: my-plugin
entry: ./plugin.sh
hooks:
  - post_session_output
env:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: "${secret:github-token}"   # scope-checked against plugin:my-plugin
  API_BASE: "https://api.example.com"       # plain value, always injected
```

| `secret_delete` | Delete a secret |
| `secret_exists` | Check if a secret exists |
