chunks.heading: Judge routing policy and time limit (Unreleased)
chunks.body:
## Judge routing policy and time limit (Unreleased)

The judges (the Automaton guardrail, plan review and other autonomous judges) have their own role in the verifier routing policy, a backend list of their own (`autonomous.judge_policy`), a 30-minute time limit per run (`autonomous.judge_timeout_seconds`), one attempt per backend, warning alerts on each timeout and an error alert plus a `needs_review` hold when every backend has timed out. The how-to is `docs/howto/judge-policy.md`.

Every row below is **Validated: No**. No live run against a sandbox daemon has been made. The lifecycle rows run the whole judge flow on fakes: a real in-memory capacity ledger with one slot per backend, a fake judge session, a fake clock and a recording alert sink. The surface rows check that every operator surface carries the two settings with the same defaults and wording.

Test conditions for every row below: `go test -count=1` on the branch, with `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR`; the JavaScript rows with `node --test`. All rows passed on 2026-10-26.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Judge role defaults to the verifier routing policy: an empty `judge_policy` resolves to the verifier policy unchanged, a later verifier edit is followed, a non-empty list replaces only the backend list | **Yes** (`TestJudgeRoleUnsetResolvesToTheVerifierPolicy`, `TestJudgeRoleFollowsLaterEditsToTheVerifierPolicy`, `TestJudgeRoleSetOverridesTheVerifierBackendList` in `internal/autonomous/policy_role_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a verifier policy fixture | Live check: set `judge_policy` on a sandbox daemon, then read the judges' backend in an Automaton decision log. |
| Judge role selection honours each mode: `fixed`, `prefer-free`, `balance` and the presets, with the judge role named in the reason when nothing is eligible | **Yes** (`TestJudgeRoleSelectionHonoursEachMode`, `TestJudgeRoleWithNothingEligibleNamesTheJudge` in `internal/autonomous/policy_role_test.go`; `TestVerifierPolicySelect` in `internal/autonomous/verifier_policy_test.go`) | No | `go test` with fake load and admission | Live check: each mode on a real pool with a full local backend. |
| Judge and verifier picks are kept apart in the decision log and audit trail (`role=judge` in the note) | **Yes** (`TestJudgePolicyDecisionLogRecordsTheJudgeRole`, `TestVerifierPolicyDecisionLogRecordsTheVerifierRole` in `internal/autonomous/policy_role_test.go`; `TestJudgeChooserRecordsEveryPickToTheDecisionLog` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_route_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a temp store directory | Live check: one Automaton with both a verifier and a judge pick shows two separate decisions. |
| Judge chooser: the judge policy list replaces the verifier list, a pinned unit backend is the only entry, the balance mode reads load and not list order, a backend that does not admit is skipped, the unit backend is the fallback on the first attempt only | **Yes** (`TestJudgePolicyListReplacesVerifierBackendsForJudges` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_route_test.go`; `TestJudgeBackendChooserForPinsAndListOrder`, `TestJudgeVerifierChooserFollowsVerifierPolicy`, `TestJudgeVerifierChooserBalanceUsesLoadNotListOrder`, `TestJudgeVerifierChooserSkipsBackendsThatDoNotAdmit`, `TestJudgeVerifierChooserFallsBackToUnitBackendOnFirstAttemptOnly` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_attempts_test.go`; `TestJudgePinnedUnitBackendIsProbedBySelector` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lease_retry_test.go`; `TestPinRoutingUnpinnedFirstPick`, `TestPinRoutingUnknownCountSaysSizeRoutingSkipped`, `TestPinRoutingTaskOverrideStaysOnItsBackend`, `TestPinRoutingPRDOverrideToClaudeCodeIsNeverMoved`, `TestPinRoutingTimeoutFallback`, `TestPinRoutingJudgeSizeForMeasuresOnlyUnpinned` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_pin_routing_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a fake probe and load | Live check: a unit with a pinned guardrail backend never moves to another backend. |
| Judge pin versus default: an unpinned large diff tries `claude-code` first and records the size rule, an unpinned small diff keeps the default order, a task or PRD guardrail backend override stays pinned and is never moved or reordered, a judge that times out on its first backend moves to the next when unpinned and does not move when pinned, and the plan-review judge pins only when `autonomous.plan_review_backend` is set | **Yes** (`TestJudgeSizeRouteAboveThresholdPicksClaudeCodeFirst`, `TestJudgeSizeRouteAtAndBelowThresholdKeepsDefaultOrder`, `TestJudgeSizeRoutePinnedUnitBackendKeepsItsBehaviour`, `TestJudgeUnpinnedResolvedBackendDoesNotOverrideJudgePolicyOrder`, `TestJudgeSizeForSkipsMeasurementOnlyWhenPinned` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_size_route_wiring_test.go`; `TestPinRoutingUnpinnedFirstPick`, `TestPinRoutingTaskOverrideStaysOnItsBackend`, `TestPinRoutingPRDOverrideToClaudeCodeIsNeverMoved`, `TestPinRoutingTimeoutFallback` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_pin_routing_test.go`; `TestPlanReviewPinFlagFollowsTheConfiguredBackend` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_plan_review_test.go`; `TestGuardrailResolution_PinnedOnlyForTaskOrPRDOverride` in `internal/autonomous/guardrail_backend_resolution_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a fake probe, load and diff counter | Final gate: `go build ./...`, `go test ./... -count=1`, `make lint` and `gofmt -l` on the changed Go files all pass; no live daemon check was run. |
| Judge on a free Claude lane when local slots are full: the judge skips the full local backends and runs on the Claude backend that admits; the Claude session count only counts granted leases | **Yes** (`TestJudgeFallsBackToTheNextBackendWhenPreferredPoolIsFull`, `TestJudgeWaitsForFreeSlotBeforeTheJudgeRuns` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_route_test.go`; `TestJudgeClaudeWindowCountsOnlyGrantedLeases` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lease_retry_test.go`) | No | `go test` with an in-memory capacity ledger | Live check: fill the local slots on a sandbox daemon and confirm a judge runs on `claude-code` with the `prefer-free` reason in the log. |
| Time limit: default 30 minutes; `0` or negative means the default; the limit starts after the lease is granted, so the slot wait is not counted; a run over the limit returns a timeout result and releases the lease; a cancelled judge is not a timeout | **Yes** (`TestJudgeTimeLimitDefaultIsThirtyMinutes`, `TestJudgeTimerDoesNotCountTheWaitForACapacitySlot`, `TestJudgeRunUnderTheLimitIsUnaffected`, `TestJudgeRunOverTheLimitReturnsTimeoutResultAndReleasesLease`, `TestJudgeCancelledByItsCallerIsNotATimeout` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_timer_test.go`; `TestJudgeSessionTimeoutDefaultsToThirtyMinutes` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_attempts_test.go`; `TestNormalizeJudgeTimeoutSeconds_DefaultIsThirtyMinutes` in `internal/config/judge_policy_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a fake clock | Live check: a sandbox judge that sleeps past a short limit is recorded as timed out. |
| One attempt per backend: a timed-out backend is not tried again in the same call, a backend with no slot is passed over, the attempts never exceed the list length | **Yes** (`TestRunJudgeAttemptsTimeoutThenPasses`, `TestRunJudgeAttemptsNonTimeoutFailureIsFinal` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_attempts_test.go`; `TestJudgeMovesOnWhenItsLeaseWaitExpires` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lease_retry_test.go`; `TestJudgeSingleBackendPolicyGetsOneAttemptThenHolds` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_timeout_action_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a scripted attempt function | Live check: a three-backend policy with all three timing out shows three attempts in the hold. |
| Timed-out attempts survive a restart: the tried backends are excluded after a restart, and a call whose every backend already timed out holds without running the judge again | **Yes** (`TestJudgeTimeoutsSurviveRestartAndSkipTheTriedBackends`, `TestJudgeRestoredTimeoutsOnEveryBackendHoldWithoutRunning` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_timeout_action_test.go`; `TestJudgeTriesKeepTimedOutAttemptsPerJudgeCall`, `TestJudgeTriesSurviveDaemonRestart`, `TestClearJudgeTriesRemovesOnlyThatCallAndSkipsTheSaveWhenEmpty` in `internal/autonomous/judge_tries_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a temp store directory | Live check: restart the daemon during a judge run and confirm the timed-out backend is not tried again. |
| Warning alert on each timeout: titled `judge timed out for Automaton <id>`, names the Automaton, the backend, the time spent, the backends tried so far and the next backend or the end of the policy | **Yes** (`TestJudgeTimeoutWarningNamesPRDBackendsAndTimeSpent`, `TestJudgeTimeoutFirstBackendThenSuccessRaisesOneWarning` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_timeout_action_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a recording alert sink | Live check: the warning reaches the alert list and the configured notification channel. |
| Error alert and hold when every backend timed out: the Automaton is held in `needs_review` with a `judge-timeout` block verdict, one summary line per attempt, and an error alert naming the Automaton, the backends and the total time; nothing is approved or passed | **Yes** (`TestJudgeAllBackendsTimeOutHoldsWithSummaryOfEveryAttempt`, `TestJudgeHoldAlertNamesPRDBackendsAndTotalTime` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_timeout_action_test.go`; `TestRunPRDCompletionRulesReview_JudgeTimeoutIsBlockedWithHoldCategory`, `TestRulesReviewBlockStatusHoldsJudgeTimeoutAsNeedsReview`, `TestPRDHoldReasonHoldsJudgeTimeoutOnlyWhileNeedsReview` in `internal/autonomous/judge_hold_test.go`; `TestJudgeHoldOrBlockedHoldsOnlyAJudgeTimeout`, `TestJudgeHoldHeldFollowsAStoryOrTaskJudgeTimeout` in `internal/autonomous/judge_hold_units_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a recording alert sink | Live check: a sandbox Automaton whose judge times out on every backend shows `needs_review` and one error alert. |
| No slot on any backend and no timeout: the judge never ran, so an infrastructure verdict is returned and nothing is held; a mix of a timeout and a no-slot backend is held | **Yes** (`TestJudgeWithNoSlotOnTheLastBackendIsInfraNotHold`, `TestJudgeHoldsWhenATimeoutIsMixedWithNoSlot`, `TestJudgeCancelledWhileWaitingForASlotStopsWithoutNextBackend` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lease_retry_test.go`) | No | `go test` with an in-memory capacity ledger | Live check: a full pool on a sandbox daemon gives an infrastructure retry, not a hold. |
| Plan review judge: the review runs as a judge invocation, a timed-out judge gives a held verdict with one finding per attempt, a judge that could not run is a reviewer outage, the plan review takes the next backend when the preferred pool is full, and every backend timing out holds with an error alert | **Yes** (`TestPlanReviewRunsAsAJudgeInvocationForItsAutomaton`, `TestPlanReviewJudgeHoldIsAHeldVerdictWithEveryAttempt`, `TestPlanReviewJudgeThatCouldNotRunIsAReviewerOutage`, `TestPlanReviewTakesTheNextBackendWhenThePreferredPoolIsFull`, `TestPlanReviewIsHeldWithAnErrorAlertWhenEveryBackendTimesOut` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_plan_review_test.go`; `TestPlanReviewHeldVerdictBlocksApprovalInBlockModeUntilRerun`, `TestPRDHoldReasonHoldsHeldPlanReviewWhileNeedsReview` in `internal/autonomous/judge_hold_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a fake judge | Live check: a held plan review on a sandbox daemon refuses approval in `block` mode until the review is re-run. |
| Lifecycle: waits for a full pool and starts when a slot frees | **Yes** (`TestJudgeLifecycleWaitsForFullPoolAndStartsWhenSlotFrees` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lifecycle_test.go`) | No | `go test` with an in-memory capacity ledger, a fake judge session and a fake clock | Live check: fill a pool on a sandbox daemon, free a slot, and confirm the judge starts once. |
| Lifecycle: follows the policy fallback and records the decision | **Yes** (`TestJudgeLifecycleFollowsPolicyFallbackAndRecordsDecision` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lifecycle_test.go`) | No | As above | Live check: the decision log shows the backend the judge ran on and the reason. |
| Lifecycle: a timeout retries the next backend with one warning | **Yes** (`TestJudgeLifecycleTimeoutRetriesNextBackendWithWarning` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lifecycle_test.go`) | No | As above | Live check: a sandbox judge that times out once moves to the next backend and raises one warning. |
| Lifecycle: every backend timed out holds for review with an error alert | **Yes** (`TestJudgeLifecycleEveryBackendTimedOutHoldsForReviewWithErrorAlert` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lifecycle_test.go`) | No | As above | Live check: the hold reaches the operator's alert list as an error. |
| Lifecycle: a restart in the middle of a judge keeps one lease, one session and one attempt per backend | **Yes** (`TestJudgeLifecycleRestartMidJudgeKeepsOneLeaseOneSessionAndOneAttemptPerBackend` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_lifecycle_test.go`) | No | As above | Live check: restart the daemon mid-judge on a sandbox daemon and count the judge sessions. |
| Surface parity, config struct, REST, MCP schema, comm help and comm `config-set`: each surface names `judge_policy` and `judge_timeout_seconds`, the verifier-routing wording, and no stale wording about the old behaviour | **Yes** (`TestJudgeConfigSurfaceParity` in `internal/server/judge_config_parity_test.go`) | No | `go test`; the test reads the source files named on each surface | This is a needle check on the source of each surface, not a behavioural test. The MCP surface has no behavioural test for the judge keys yet. |
| Surface parity, defaults: the REST surface reports the empty list and 1800 seconds; every surface states the same default wording; the default is 30 minutes on every surface | **Yes** (`TestJudgeConfigDefaultsOnRESTSurface`, `TestJudgeConfigDefaultWordingOnEverySurface`, `TestJudgeConfigDefaultIsThirtyMinutesOnEverySurface` in `internal/server/judge_config_parity_test.go`) | No | `go test` | Live check: `GET /api/autonomous/config` on a sandbox daemon with no judge settings. |
| Surface parity, locale: the label and help keys for both settings are present and non-empty in all five locale bundles and are not copies of the English text | **Yes** (`TestJudgeConfigLocaleParity` in `internal/server/judge_config_parity_test.go`; `judge_policy and judge_timeout_seconds label and help keys are non-empty in all five locale bundles` in `internal/server/web/app-autonomous-settings-fields.test.js`) | No | `go test`; `node --test` | Live check: the Settings card shows the translated labels in each locale. |
| Surface parity, PWA: the autonomous settings card carries `autonomous.judge_policy` as a comma list and `autonomous.judge_timeout_seconds`, with label and help keys | **Yes** (`autonomous settings expose judge_policy and judge_timeout_seconds with label and help keys` in `internal/server/web/app-autonomous-settings-fields.test.js`) | No | `node --test` against the real settings field definitions | Live check: change both fields in the browser, save, and read them back. |
| Surface parity, CLI: `autonomous config-set --judge-policy` and `--judge-timeout-seconds` build the request body, a comma list is split, a negative timeout is refused | **Yes** (`TestJudgeConfigCLI_FlagsBuildBody` in `cmd/datawatch/judge_config_cli_test.go`) | No | `go test` | Live check: run the command against a sandbox daemon and read the settings back. |
| Surface parity, comm channel: `autonomous judge-policy` shows only the judge settings; `autonomous judge-policy-set` sets the list and the timeout; an empty list clears the list; bad input is refused without a request | **Yes** (`TestJudgePolicyCommShowsJudgeSettingsOnly`, `TestJudgePolicyCommSetsBackendsAndTimeout`, `TestJudgePolicyCommEmptyPolicyClearsTheList`, `TestJudgePolicyCommRejectsBadInputWithoutRequest` in `internal/router/judge_policy_comm_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a loopback server | Live check: send each verb from a chat channel on a sandbox daemon. |
| Config layer: the normalised judge list drops blank and duplicate entries and keeps order; an empty result is an empty list and not nil | **Yes** (`TestNormalizeJudgePolicy_TrimsDedupesAndKeepsOrder`, `TestNormalizeJudgePolicy_EmptyIsEmptyListNotNil` in `internal/config/judge_policy_test.go`) | No | `go test` | — |

Surface parity tests, by file: `internal/server/judge_config_parity_test.go` (five tests), `internal/router/judge_policy_comm_test.go` (four tests), `cmd/datawatch/judge_config_cli_test.go` (one test), `internal/server/web/app-autonomous-settings-fields.test.js` (two judge tests).

Lifecycle test names, by file (`cmd/datawatch`): `judge_lifecycle_test.go` (five tests, listed in the rows above), `judge_timeout_action_test.go` (`TestJudgeTimeoutWarningNamesPRDBackendsAndTimeSpent`, `TestJudgeSingleBackendPolicyGetsOneAttemptThenHolds`, `TestJudgeTimeoutFirstBackendThenSuccessRaisesOneWarning`, `TestJudgeAllBackendsTimeOutHoldsWithSummaryOfEveryAttempt`, `TestJudgeTimeoutsSurviveRestartAndSkipTheTriedBackends`, `TestJudgeRestoredTimeoutsOnEveryBackendHoldWithoutRunning`, `TestJudgeHoldAlertNamesPRDBackendsAndTotalTime`, `TestJudgeTryLogWriteFailureDoesNotStopTheJudge`), `judge_lease_retry_test.go` (`TestJudgeMovesOnWhenItsLeaseWaitExpires`, `TestJudgeWithNoSlotOnTheLastBackendIsInfraNotHold`, `TestJudgeHoldsWhenATimeoutIsMixedWithNoSlot`, `TestJudgeCancelledWhileWaitingForASlotStopsWithoutNextBackend`, `TestJudgeAskRunStopsAtTheTimeLimit`, `TestJudgeAskRunCancelledJudgeIsNotATimeout`), `judge_route_test.go` (`TestJudgeWaitsForFreeSlotBeforeTheJudgeRuns`, `TestJudgeLeaseIsReleasedWhenTheJudgeFails`, `TestJudgeLeaseIsReleasedOnSuccessAndOnCancel`, `TestJudgeBodyNeverRunsWhenTheLeaseIsNotGranted`), `judge_capacity_test.go` (the lease admission tests: `TestJudgeAdmitHoldsBackendAndNodePools`, `TestJudgeAdmitWaitsThenAcquiresWhenSlotFrees`, `TestJudgeAdmitReleasesOnPanic`, `TestJudgeTryAdmitProbesWithoutCommitting`).

## Task failure escalation policy: engine, interfaces and operator review (Unreleased)

A task that keeps failing moves up a ladder of workers, is held for operator review at a set failure count, and is then resolved by a retry (optionally with a changed spec, worker or file scope) or a cancel. The policy is set at three levels: task, Automaton and daemon default.

Every row below is **Validated: No**. None of these interfaces has had a live run against a sandbox daemon yet. The opt-in live smoke test is added by a separate task, and each Notes cell says what the live check must confirm.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Engine: policy model, step ladder, attempt records, retry prompt, hold at the failure count, operator retry and cancel, per-field override order | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/failure_escalation_*_test.go`, `internal/config/failure_escalation_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a temp store directory, an injected verifier and a recording alert sink | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: a real failing worker is held at the configured count, and retry and cancel act on it. |
| REST `GET /api/config` and `PUT /api/config` for `autonomous.failure_escalation.enabled`, `.max_failures`, `.steps` (compact text and JSON array; round trip to `config.yaml` and the live manager; a bad value is a 400 that names the key and changes nothing) | **Yes** (`internal/server/failure_escalation_config_surfaces_test.go`, `internal/config/failure_escalation_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a real manager and a temp config file | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: PUT a value, read it back with GET, then send a bad value and confirm the 400. |
| REST `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_failure_escalation` (Automaton and task override; `policy: null` clears; 400, 404, federation capability refusal, audit entry) | **Yes** (`internal/server/failure_escalation_rest_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a real manager seeded on disk and `httptest` | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: set, read and clear an override on an Automaton that holds a task. |
| REST `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/resolve_task_review` (retry with a note, retry with a changed spec, cancel; 409 when not held; 400, 404, capability refusal, method guard, audit entry) | **Yes** (`internal/server/failure_escalation_rest_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a real manager seeded on disk and `httptest` | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: retry and cancel a task held by a real failing worker. |
| MCP `autonomous_prd_set_failure_escalation` and `autonomous_prd_resolve_task_review` (proxy, body shape, clear sends a null policy, refusals, 409 and 404 pass-through); `config_set` accepts the escalation keys; `autonomous_status` describes `review_needed` | **Yes** (`internal/mcp/failure_escalation_tools_test.go`, `internal/mcp/failure_escalation_surfaces_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a loopback server | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: call both tools from an MCP client on a host session. |
| CLI `datawatch autonomous failure-escalation show`, `set`, `clear`, `global` and `resolve-review` (flag parsing, refusals before any request, body shape, help) | **Yes** (`cmd/datawatch/failure_escalation_cli_test.go`, `cmd/datawatch/failure_escalation_surfaces_test.go`, `cmd/datawatch/failure_escalation_config_test.go`) | No | `go test` with an `httptest` daemon double | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: run each subcommand against a sandbox daemon. |
| Comm channel verbs `autonomous set-failure-escalation` and `autonomous review-task` (word parsing, multi-word note, refusals, loopback request), `configure autonomous.failure_escalation.*` keys, help text | **Yes** (`internal/router/failure_escalation_comm_test.go`, `internal/router/failure_escalation_surfaces_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a loopback server | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: send each verb from a chat channel. |
| Web UI: Settings fields for the daemon default; Automaton and task override editors; held-task badge, attempts, report and the Retry, Edit spec and retry, Change worker, Narrow scope and Cancel task actions; held counts on Automaton headers, list rows and the Automation strip; locale keys in en, de, es, fr and ja | **Yes** (`internal/server/web/app-failure-escalation.test.js`, `internal/server/v5280_locales_test.go`) | No | `node --test` against the real `app.js` with a recording fetch; `go test` for the locale guard | No live run in a browser yet. Live check: change each setting, save and clear an override, and resolve a held task from the browser. |
| Status output: `autonomous status` JSON `review_needed` (omitted when nothing is held); CLI and comm status lines for held tasks; Automaton summary `review_needed`; task listing `escalation_failures`, `attempt_count`, `review_summary`; Automation status `review_needed_count` and `review_needed_task_ids` | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/failure_escalation_status_test.go`, `internal/autonomous/failure_escalation_views_test.go`, `internal/router/failure_escalation_surfaces_test.go`, `internal/mcp/failure_escalation_surfaces_test.go`) | No | `go test` | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: hold a task on a real run and read each view. |
| Alert: one error-level alert, titled "Automaton task needs review", when a task is held (one alert per hold, body names the Automaton, task, failed attempts, last worker and the ways to act) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/failure_escalation_hold_test.go`) | No | `go test` with a recording alert sink | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: the alert reaches the operator's alert list and the configured notification channel. |
| End-to-end flow on fakes: one Automaton with a dependent task; a two-step global ladder (local model, then stronger Claude); held after three failed attempts with one alert and the dependent never started; operator retry with a new worker and narrowed scope completes the Automaton. Also the cancel path and a task-level `max_failures` of 4 over the global 3 | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/failure_escalation_flow_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run TestFailureEscalation_FullFlow` with fake spawn, verifier, alert sink and attempt clock | No live run against a sandbox daemon yet. Live check: the same sequence on a sandbox daemon with the opt-in live smoke test (`failure_escalation_live_smoke_test.go`). |

- `failure_escalation_hold_test.go`: `TestFailureEscalation_HoldAtConfiguredCount`, `TestFailureEscalation_HoldRaisesOneAlert`, `TestFailureEscalation_HeldTaskBlocksDependentsNotSiblings`, `TestFailureEscalation_HeldTaskKeepsAutomatonOpen`, `TestFailureEscalation_BootReconcileLeavesHeldTask`, `TestFailureEscalation_DisabledStillFailsTask`, `TestFailureEscalation_TaskOverrideMaxFailures`, `TestFailureEscalation_HoldRecordsLearningOnce`, `TestFailureEscalation_HoldStatusCountedInSummary`, `TestFailureEscalation_ReviewSummaryListsEveryAttempt`
- `failure_escalation_review_test.go`: `TestFailureEscalation_OperatorRetry`, `TestFailureEscalation_OperatorChangeSpec`, `TestFailureEscalation_OperatorChangeWorker`, `TestFailureEscalation_OperatorNarrowScope`, `TestFailureEscalation_OperatorCancelRollsUp`, `TestFailureEscalation_ResolveNotHeldIsRejected`, `TestFailureEscalation_SetOverrideAutomatonAndTask`, `TestFailureEscalation_OverrideOrderEndToEnd`, `TestFailureEscalation_SetOverrideRespectsAcceptedStatuses`
- `failure_escalation_attempts_test.go`: `TestFailureEscalation_RetryPromptCarriesEarlierReports`, `TestFailureEscalation_AttemptRecordFields`, `TestFailureEscalation_PromptDisabledKeepsLegacyHint`, `TestFailureEscalation_AttemptChangedFiles`, `TestFailureEscalation_GitEnvDropsMultiplexerVars`, `TestFailureEscalation_OutcomeForError`

- `failure_escalation_test.go`: `TestFailureEscalation_Defaults`, `TestFailureEscalation_GlobalValuesApply`, `TestFailureEscalation_OverrideOrderPerField`, `TestFailureEscalation_Validation`, `TestFailureEscalation_ParseAndFormatSteps`, `TestFailureEscalation_ParseStepsErrors`, `TestFailureEscalation_JSONRoundTrip`, `TestFailureEscalation_OldStoredRecordsLoad`, `TestFailureEscalation_ReviewNeededIsNotTerminalOrFailure`

## LLM workload roles and session priority

Roles tag an LLM registry entry with the workloads it serves; priority orders a session in the capacity wait queue.
Operator guide: `docs/howto/llm-registry.md`. Each row below is Tested by unit tests only. Validated is left unset: no live run against a daemon has been done.

## Capacity rate ceilings and the admission Decision query

Rate-ceiling pools, the `Decision` result and the non-blocking admission query (`Ledger.Check`, `GET /api/capacity/admission`) are in the next patch above main. Operator guide: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md`. Every row is Tested by unit tests only, using an in-process ledger and `httptest` servers with fake clocks or short windows. Validated is No: no run against a live daemon with a real metered backend has been done, so a real ceiling being hit and the window freeing is owed.

## Automata tags: nested tag registry, per-Automaton assignment, browse and bulk tag

Tags are managed objects (`id`, `name`, `parent_id`, `color`, `description`) persisted to `tags.jsonl`; an
Automaton carries several (`tag_ids`). Deleting a tag with child tags is refused, deleting a tag still assigned
to Automata is refused with a count, and a move that would make a tag its own ancestor is refused. Operator
guide: `docs/howto/automata-tags.md`.

Both validation levels are listed. Each unit row is Tested; none is Validated: a live run against a sandbox
daemon, through each surface, is still owed, and the live rows below say exactly what that run must show.

chunks.body:
## Quality gate: shell-run command, invalid baselines, name-based regression, gate_disagreement

The gate's test command runs through a shell in the project directory, a baseline that cannot produce
usable results is recorded as an invalid gate (it only warns and never blocks), regressions are compared by
failing test name and confirmed by one re-run, and `autonomous.gate_disagreement` (`warn` or `block`)
decides what a verifier-passed task does when the gate confirms a regression. Operator guide:
`docs/operations.md` → "Quality gate".

Each row is unit-tested and none is Validated: a live daemon run with a real gate command, through each
surface, is still owed.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shell-run test command in the project directory | `TestRunTests_ShellCompounds`, `TestRunTests_MissingProjectDir`, `TestRunTests_Timeout`, `TestRunTests_GoOutputParsing`, `TestRunTests_NodeOutputParsing`, `TestRunTests_RealGoModule` | `go test ./internal/pipeline/ -count=1 -run 'TestRunTests'` | `RunTests` runs the command through `sh -c` in the project directory, so `a && b` works. A missing directory and a timeout are unusable runs. Go and node output are parsed into counts and failing test names. `TestRunTests_RealGoModule` builds and runs a real Go module with one passing and one failing test. | Unit + real subprocess | **Yes** (`internal/pipeline/quality_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |
| Baseline validity: valid versus invalid | `TestClassifyBaseline_ExitNonZeroNoTests`, `TestClassifyBaseline_ZeroTestsFound`, `TestClassifyBaseline_PackageSetupFailureOnlyIsInvalid` | `go test ./internal/pipeline/ -count=1 -run 'TestClassifyBaseline'` | A non-zero exit that names no failing test, a run with no tests found and a package-level setup failure are invalid. A run that finished with named failing tests is valid. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/pipeline/quality_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |
| Regression compared by failing test name | `TestCompare_NewFailingNameIsRegression`, `TestCompare_SameCountDifferentNamesIsRegression`, `TestCompare_FewerFailuresIsImproved`, `TestCompare_IdenticalIsStable`, `TestCompare_InvalidBaseline`, `TestCompare_InvalidCurrentRunIsNotRegression` | `go test ./internal/pipeline/ -count=1 -run 'TestCompare_'` | A new failing name is a regression even when the failure count is unchanged. An unusable baseline or current run is an invalid gate, never a regression. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/pipeline/quality_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |
| One confirming re-run names the failing tests | `TestEvaluateGate_ConfirmedRegressionNamesTests`, `TestEvaluateGate_FlakeNotReportedAsRegression`, `TestEvaluateGate_CleanRunDoesNotRerun`, `TestEvaluateGate_CompoundCommandRerunsWholeCommand`, `TestEvaluateGate_InvalidRunIsNotRerun`, `TestEvaluateGate_NodeFailureNameRegression`, `TestEvaluateGate_UnusableRerunIsInvalid` | `go test ./internal/pipeline/ -count=1 -run 'TestEvaluateGate'` | Only a name-based regression is re-run, once. Tests that fail again are listed; a failure that does not reproduce is reported as stable; an unusable re-run makes the gate invalid. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/pipeline/quality_reconfirm_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |
| Executor: invalid baseline marks the Automaton and never blocks | `TestGateValidity_SetPRDQualityGatesMarksInvalid`, `TestGateValidity_StatusCountsInvalidGate`, `TestGateValidity_SeamInvalidBaseline_CompletesWithWarning`, `TestGateValidity_RealRun_InvalidBaseline_Completes`, `TestGateValidity_RealRun_RegressionStillFailsTask` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestGateValidity'` | Validation at gate-set time and at start; `quality_gate_status: invalid` with the reason; the task completes with a warning. A regression from a valid baseline still fails the task when `block_on_regression` is on. | Unit + real command runs | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/gate_validity_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |
| Executor: `gate_disagreement` policy | `TestGateDisagreement_VerdictPassRegression_Warn`, `TestGateDisagreement_VerdictPassRegression_Block`, `TestGateDisagreement_InvalidGateNeverBlocks`, `TestGateDisagreement_SetConfigSanitizes`, `TestGateDisagreement_APISetConfigRejectsInvalid` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestGateDisagreement'` | `warn` records the disagreement and completes the task, `block` fails it with a `gate_disagreement: …` error, an invalid gate never blocks, and the setter rejects any other value. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/gate_disagreement_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |

The warn/block selector is in Settings and its label keys exist in all five locales. | Unit (node, browser-stub sandbox) | **Yes** (`internal/server/web/app-prd-gate-invalid.test.js`, `internal/server/web/app-autonomous-settings-fields.test.js`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |

chunks.heading: Phase 4 - model-tier defaults
chunks.body:
## Phase 4 - model-tier defaults

An Automation carries default model settings for the member Automata it runs. The
Automation tier sits between the Automaton and the global default for the execution
backend, model and effort and for the verification LLM, `verifier_source` gains
`automation`, task run records gain `executor_source`, and an optional planning pair
is used only when a member is decomposed. Two set operations, `set_llm` and
`set_verification_llm`, exist on the REST, MCP, CLI and comm surfaces. Design:
`docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (Phase 4).

Each test row is built and unit-tested, and none is Validated. Validated is filled in by
the operator's live run, with its date, per the rule at the top of this file. The live
row is opt-in and is the run still owed.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Verification LLM chain: the Automation tier and `verifier_source` = `automation` | `TestResolveVerificationLLMAutomationTier`, `TestResolveVerificationLLMAutomationLosesToMoreSpecificLevels`, `TestResolveVerificationLLMAutomationSameLevelModel`, `TestResolveVerificationLLMAutomationEffortChain`, `TestSelectVerifierLLMAutomationSourceBypassesPool` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestResolveVerificationLLMAutomation'` and `go test ./cmd/datawatch/ -count=1 -run 'TestSelectVerifierLLMAutomationSourceBypassesPool'` | The order is task, story, Automaton, Automation, global. With nothing set above it, the Automation's verification backend, model and effort win and the source is `automation`. A task, story or Automaton setting beats the Automation. Backend and model are taken from the same level, so an Automation model is never paired with another level's backend. Effort resolves on its own. A verification backend set at the Automation level bypasses the global verification pool, as the other per-unit levels do | Unit (resolver, selector) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/verification_llm_automation_test.go`, `cmd/datawatch/verification_llm_test.go`) | | No |  |
| Execution chain: the Automation tier for backend, model and effort | `TestResolveTaskBackendModelAutomationTier`, `TestResolveTaskBackendModelAutomationLosesToMoreSpecificLevels`, `TestResolveTaskBackendModelAutomationSameLevelModel`, `TestResolveTaskEffortAutomationTier` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestResolveTaskBackendModelAutomation\|TestResolveTaskEffortAutomationTier'` | The order is task, story, Automaton, Automation, global. The Automation's backend and model apply when no more specific level names a backend, and a more specific level always wins. Backend and model come from the same level. The effort chain has the same order and resolves independently of backend and model. An Automation with no effort leaves the effort empty | Unit (resolver) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/executor_source_test.go`) | | No |  |
| `executor_source` on task run records | `TestExecutorSourceValues`, `TestExecutorSourceRecordedOnTask`, `TestExecutorSourceJSONRoundTrip` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestExecutorSource'` | The values are `task`, `story`, `prd`, `automation` and `global`. A task of an Automation member that gets its backend from the Automation records `automation` and spawns with that backend and model. A standalone Automaton with no backend records `global` and spawns on the fallback backend. An Automaton-level backend records `prd`. The field survives a save and load and is omitted when empty | Unit (dispatch loop, fake spawn) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/executor_source_test.go`) | | No |  |
| Session status and PWA show `executor_source` | `TestSessionAutomatonExecutorSource` | `go test ./internal/server/ -count=1 -run 'TestSessionAutomatonExecutorSource'` | The Automaton block of the session status carries `executor_source` for a task that has one and leaves it out for a task that has none. The PWA shows it as an Executor line on the task and on the session status card (new locale key `status_executor_label`) | Unit (in-process HTTP, `httptest`) | **Yes** (`internal/server/executor_source_view_test.go`) | | No | The PWA rendering has no browser test in this row |
| Planning field does not affect execution or verification | `TestPlanningFieldDoesNotAffectExecution`, `TestResolveVerificationLLMPlanningFieldIgnored`, `TestAutomationPlanningLeavesRunAndVerifyDefaults` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestPlanningFieldDoesNotAffectExecution\|TestResolveVerificationLLMPlanningFieldIgnored\|TestAutomationPlanningLeavesRunAndVerifyDefaults'` | An Automation with only `planning_backend` and `planning_model` set leaves the execution backend, model and effort and the verification LLM exactly as they were, and the run and verify defaults do not change which LLM plans | Unit (resolver) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/executor_source_test.go`, `internal/autonomous/verification_llm_automation_test.go`, `internal/autonomous/automation_planning_test.go`) | | No |  |
| Planning used for decompose | `TestEffectivePlanningAutomationTier`, `TestEffectivePlanningUnsetUsesGlobal`, `TestDecomposeUsesAutomationPlanning` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestEffectivePlanning\|TestDecomposeUsesAutomationPlanning'` | A planning backend and model on the Automation are used when a member Automaton is decomposed. A backend alone never takes the global model, a model alone pairs with the global planning backend, and unset (or no Automation) uses the global planning backend and model. The Automaton's own decomposition settings still come first | Unit (resolver, decompose with a fake planner) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/automation_planning_test.go`) | | No |  |
| Automation fields and the member lookup | `TestAutomationPlanningFieldsRoundTrip`, `TestAutomationForPRDLookup` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationPlanningFieldsRoundTrip\|TestAutomationForPRDLookup'` | The planning, execution and verification fields survive create, update and reload, and an update can clear them. The lookup from a member Automaton to its Automation returns nothing for a standalone Automaton and a nil one | Unit (store round trip, Manager) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/automation_model_tier_test.go`) | | No |  |
| Manager setters: `SetAutomationLLM` and `SetAutomationVerificationLLM` | `TestSetAutomationLLM`, `TestSetAutomationVerificationLLM`, `TestSetAutomationLLMRejections`, `TestSetAutomationLLMPresenceSemantics`, `TestSetAutomationLLMDecisionAndAudit` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestSetAutomationLLM\|TestSetAutomationVerificationLLM'` | Each setter writes only its own fields and bumps the version once. A `nil` field is kept and an empty one is cleared. A `completed` or `cancelled` Automation is a 409 and nothing is written, a bad effort and a backend and model pair that do not fit are refused without writing, and a stale positive `expected_version` is a 409 while `0` skips the check. One decision and one audit record are written per call. Allowed while draft, active, paused or blocked | Unit (Manager) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/automation_set_llm_test.go`) | | No |  |
| REST `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_llm` and `/set_verification_llm` | `TestAutomationRESTSetLLM`, `TestAutomationRESTSetVerificationLLM`, `TestAutomationRESTSetLLMGuards` | `go test ./internal/server/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationRESTSet'` | Each returns 200 with the updated Automation and writes one audit entry. Omitted fields are kept and empty ones clear. No `expected_version` skips the check and a stale one is 409. A body with no setting field is 400 and names the allowed fields. A planning field on `set_verification_llm` is 400, and so is an unknown backend (an empty one clears and is not looked up). A malformed body is 400, an unknown Automation is 404, a GET is 405 and a caller without the write capability is 403 | Unit (in-process HTTP, `httptest`) | **Yes** (`internal/server/automation_set_llm_rest_test.go`) | | No |  |
| MCP `automation_set_llm` and `automation_set_verification_llm` | `TestAutomationMCPSetLLM`, `TestAutomationMCPSetVerificationLLM` | `go test ./internal/mcp/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationMCPSet'` | Only `automation_id` is required. Each tool proxies to its REST path with the keys the caller passed, and an empty string is forwarded so it clears. `expected_version` is forwarded only when positive. A call with no setting field is refused before any request is sent, and `automation_set_verification_llm` never forwards the planning arguments. A server conflict comes back as an error result | Unit (fake REST sink) | **Yes** (`internal/mcp/automation_set_llm_test.go`) | | No |  |
| Comm `automation set-llm` and `automation set-verification-llm` | `TestAutomationCommSetLLM`, `TestAutomationCommSetVerificationLLM` | `go test ./internal/router/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationCommSet'` | Each verb parses `key=value` pairs and posts them to the matching REST path. `model=` with an empty value clears. A missing ID, a missing pair, an unknown key, a token without `=` or (on `set-verification-llm`) a planning key replies with the usage line and sends nothing | Unit (comm router, fake daemon) | **Yes** (`internal/router/automation_set_llm_cmd_test.go`) | | No |  |
| CLI `datawatch automation set-llm` and `set-verification-llm` | `TestAutomationCLISetLLM`, `TestAutomationCLISetVerificationLLM` | `go test ./cmd/datawatch/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationCLISet'` | Both subcommands are registered. Only the flags given are sent, an empty value clears, and a call with no setting flag fails before any request. `--expected-version`, `--actor` and `--reason` are forwarded when given. `set-verification-llm` has no planning flags | Unit (CLI, fake REST sink) | **Yes** (`cmd/datawatch/automation_set_llm_cli_test.go`) | | No |  |
| Live: set the execution, planning and verification defaults on a sandbox Automation, run a member and read `executor_source` and `verifier_source` | `TestAutomationModelTierLiveSmoke` | Opt-in, against a sandbox daemon (TLS port 18443), never production. Skipped unless its environment variable names the sandbox daemon's base URL, following the control-operations live row above | Calls only the daemon's REST API: sets the defaults on a draft Automation, checks the fields and the 409 on a stale `expected_version`, then runs a member and checks that `executor_source` is `automation` and that a task-level setting still wins | Live (opt-in, sandbox daemon) | **No** (the test is not written in this build) | | **No** | Owed: the operator's live run, with date |

**Mobile-Parity: owed, not yet filed.** Issues are not filed from this
pipeline. File on `dmz006/datawatch-app` when the model-tier branch merges:

> `feat(automation): model-tier defaults and executor_source`
>
> Server added two operations on an Automation:
> `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_llm` (body `backend?`, `model?`, `effort?`,
> `planning_backend?`, `planning_model?`) and
> `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_verification_llm` (body `backend?`, `model?`,
> `effort?`). Both also take `expected_version?`, `actor?` and `reason?`. Fields
> are presence-aware: an omitted field is kept and an empty string clears it.
> `expected_version` is optional (omitted or `0` skips the check, a stale
> positive value is `409`). Allowed while the Automation is `draft`, `active`,
> `paused` or `blocked` (otherwise `409`); `400` for no setting field, a planning
> field on `set_verification_llm`, an unknown backend or a bad effort.
> New Automation fields on `/api/automations`: `backend`, `model`, `effort`
> (execution), `planning_backend`, `planning_model` (used only when decomposing
> a member), `verification_backend`, `verification_model`, `verification_effort`.
> Resolution order for the execution backend, model and effort and for the
> verification LLM: task, story, Automaton, Automation, global.
> The verifier source on a task's `verification` object gains the value
> `automation` (`task | story | prd | automation | global | pool`). Task run
> records gain `executor_source` (`task | story | prd | automation | global`),
> also present in the session status Automaton block.
> Acceptance: Android and iOS show `executor_source` beside the verifier source
> on a task and on the session status view, treat an unknown value as plain text,
> and, when they gain an Automation view, offer both set operations with an
> explicit clear action and surface the `409` and `400` messages. The PWA shows
> `executor_source` as an Executor line today and has no Automation view, so
> setting the defaults stays API-only until the PWA Automation view exists.
>
> Localization Rule: new key `status_executor_label`, English "Executor". The
> de, es, fr and ja bundles carry the English placeholder; please supply real
> translations in the app's own bundles.

---

## Automation view

The Automation view is the first sub-tab of the Automata tab in the PWA (the bottom
navigation has no Automation button), left of the Automata and Templates sub-tabs. It lists
Automations, draws each one as a pipeline strip, drives the control operations and has
a create and edit form. It is built in `internal/server/web` and covered by node tests;
there is no browser test in these rows. Design:
`docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (PWA).

Each test row below was run and passes, and none is Validated. Validated is filled in by
the operator's live run, with its date, per the rule at the top of this file. The live

Cancelled Automations stay hidden until the history toggle is on, search matches name or ID, and the cards are ordered by status then name. Names are escaped so hostile text cannot inject markup. If the Automaton title lookup fails the list still draws, with short member IDs | Unit (node, sandboxed DOM) | **Yes** (`internal/server/web/app-automation-list.test.js`, 19 passed) | Pass | No |  |

pipeline. File on `dmz006/datawatch-app` when the Automation sub-tab branch merges:

> `feat(automation): Automation sub-tab (list, pipeline strip, controls, create and edit)`
>
> The PWA gained an Automation view, the first sub-tab of the Automata tab (there is no Automation button in the main navigation). It uses these REST endpoints:
> `GET` and `POST /api/automations`; `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/automations/{id}`;
> and `POST /api/automations/{id}/{activate|pause|resume|cancel|skip_member|insert_member|remove_member|reorder_edges|approve_insert|set_llm|set_verification_llm}`.
> Member kinds are `prd` (an Automaton), `automation` (a nested Automation), `fork`
> and `join`. A join carries `on_branch_failure`, one of `all_must_succeed`
> (default), `any_one_is_enough` or `continue_anyway`.
> Cancel requires an explicit `cancel_in_flight` (`true` ends the member sessions
> that are running, `false` leaves them running). There is no default: the app
> must always ask. A `409` on any write means the Automation changed since it was
> loaded; show the server's message and offer a reload, do not retry. A `400`
> shows the server's message on the form.
> Strip rules: members draw as a chain joined by `on_complete` connectors; a fork
> draws its branches in parallel lanes and a join closes them and shows its rule;
> a nested Automation is an expandable level; members in the active positions are
> highlighted; an edge that was not taken is dashed.
> New locale keys: every key with the prefix `automation_`, plus `nav_automation`.
> The de, es, fr and ja bundles in the datawatch repository
> (`internal/server/web/locales/`) already carry translations the app can mirror.
> Acceptance: Android and iOS show the Automation list with status, progress,
> blocked reason and budget; show the pipeline strip with chain, fork lanes, join
> and expandable nested levels; offer pause, resume, cancel (with the explicit
> choice), skip, insert, remove, reorder and approve; offer create and edit with
> linear, fork, join and nested members, default models and a budget policy;
> handle `409` with a reload prompt; and treat an unknown status or member kind as
> plain text.

chunks.title: Testing Tracker
chunks.heading: Phase 3b — control operations
chunks.body:
## Phase 3b — control operations

Operator control of a running Automation: `pause`, `resume`, `cancel` (with a required
in-flight choice), `skip_member`, `insert_member` (with `agent_insert_policy` and the
one-urgent-at-a-time lane), `remove_member`, `reorder_edges` and `approve_insert`, on the
REST, MCP, CLI and comm surfaces, plus the `autonomous.automation.agent_insert_policy`
setting. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (the Phase 3b
sections).

Each test row is built and unit-tested, and none is Validated. Validated is filled in by
the operator's live run, with its date, per the rule at the top of this file. The live
row is opt-in and is the run still owed.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Manager control operations: pause, resume, cancel, skip, remove, reorder, version conflict, branch naming | `TestAutomationControlPause`, `TestAutomationControlResume`, `TestAutomationControlCancel`, `TestAutomationControlSkipEdge`, `TestAutomationControlRemove`, `TestAutomationControlReorder`, `TestAutomationControlVersionConflict`, `TestAutomationControlBranchNaming` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationControl'` | Pause keeps in-flight members running and starts nothing. Resume routes members that ended meanwhile and starts the next. Cancel with no in-flight choice is refused, with a message naming `cancel_in_flight=true` and `cancel_in_flight=false`. `true` ends the member sessions through the existing cancel path, `false` leaves running members alone. Skip follows `on_complete` (default), `on_blocked` or `on_failed`. Remove and reorder refuse members that have started. A stale `expected_version` is a 409. In a forked Automation with several active branches, an operation that acts on a position must name the active cursor, and the rejection lists the active branch member IDs | Unit (Manager, fake starter) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/automation_control_test.go`) | | No | The pattern also matches the insert tests below; run the pattern as one group |
| Insert lane: `insert_member`, `approve_insert`, `agent_insert_policy` and the urgent cap | `TestAutomationControlInsertNormalAppendsToEnd`, `TestAutomationControlInsertUrgentTakesFirstSlot`, `TestAutomationControlInsertAfterMember`, `TestAutomationControlInsertVersionConflict`, `TestAutomationControlInsertRejectsBadPRD`, `TestAutomationControlInsertAgentPolicy`, `TestAutomationControlInsertIntoActiveIsHeldWithReason`, `TestAutomationControlInsertRefusesTerminal`, `TestAutomationControlApprovePromotesNormalInsert`, `TestAutomationControlApproveUrgentTakesNextSlot`, `TestAutomationControlApproveDraftPending`, `TestAutomationControlApproveRejections` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationControlInsert\|TestAutomationControlApprove'` | A normal insert goes to the end of the chain (or after the named member). An urgent insert takes the next slot. An insert into a non-draft Automation needs a reason and is held as a `PendingInsert` until `approve_insert`. Under `agent_insert_policy` `allow` an agent insert into a draft lands at once, and under `require_operator` it is held. Only the operator may approve. A completed or cancelled Automation refuses an insert | Unit (Manager, fake starter) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/automation_insert_control_test.go`) | | No | |
| One urgent pending insert per Automation | `TestAutomationUrgentOneAtATime`, `TestAutomationUrgentOneAtATimeAfterApprove` | `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationUrgentOneAtATime'` | A second urgent `insert_member` while one is pending is a 409 naming the pending one. After the first is approved, another urgent insert is accepted | Unit (Manager, fake starter) | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/automation_insert_control_test.go`) | | No | |
| REST `POST /api/automations/{id}/{pause\|resume\|cancel\|skip_member\|insert_member\|remove_member\|reorder_edges\|approve_insert}` | `TestAutomationRESTControl`, `TestAutomationRESTCancel`, `TestAutomationRESTApprove` | `go test ./internal/server/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationREST(Control\|Cancel\|Approve)$'` | Each operation returns 200 with the updated Automation and writes one audit entry. A stale `expected_version` is 409. A `cancel` without `cancel_in_flight` (missing or `null`) is 400 and the message names `cancel_in_flight=true` and `cancel_in_flight=false`. `false` cancels the Automation. `true` is accepted by the handler, and the test's starter cannot end member sessions, so it is a 409 there. An `insert_member` without a reason is 400. A malformed body is 400, an unknown Automation is 404, and a GET or DELETE on a control path is 405. A cancelled Automation cannot be cancelled again (409). `approve_insert` of an unknown pending insert is 404, a stale version or a non-operator actor is 409, and the operator's approval promotes the pending insert | Unit (in-process HTTP, `httptest`) | **Yes** (`internal/server/automation_control_rest_test.go`) | | No | |
| MCP `automation_pause`, `automation_resume`, `automation_cancel`, `automation_skip_member`, `automation_insert_member`, `automation_remove_member`, `automation_reorder_edges`, `automation_approve_insert` | `TestAutomationMCPControl`, `TestAutomationMCPControlGuards`, `TestAutomationMCPCancel` | `go test ./internal/mcp/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationMCP(Control\|Cancel)'` | Each tool proxies to its REST path with the right body. `expected_version` and `automation_id` are required. `automation_cancel` without `cancel_in_flight` is refused before any request is sent, and both values are forwarded. `automation_insert_member` without a reason is refused before any request is sent | Unit (fake REST sink) | **Yes** (`internal/mcp/automation_control_test.go`) | | No | |
| Comm `automation pause\|resume\|cancel\|skip\|insert\|remove\|edges\|approve` | `TestAutomationCommControl` | `go test ./internal/router/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationCommControl'` | Each verb parses and posts to the matching REST path. `cancel` requires `in-flight=true` or `in-flight=false` and replies with usage otherwise. `insert` requires a reason | Unit (comm router, fake daemon) | **Yes** (`internal/router/automation_control_cmd_test.go`) | | No | |
| CLI `datawatch automation pause\|resume\|cancel\|skip\|insert\|remove\|edges\|approve` | `TestAutomationCLIControl` | `go test ./cmd/datawatch/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationCLIControl'` | Each subcommand sends the right REST request. `cancel` fails without `--cancel-in-flight <true\|false>`. `--expected-version` is forwarded when given | Unit (CLI, fake REST sink) | **Yes** (`cmd/datawatch/automation_control_cli_test.go`) | | No | |
| CLI controls with `--expected-version` omitted (insert, pause, resume, skip, remove, edges, approve, cancel and the settings commands): the current version is read first | `TestAutomationCLIDefaultVersionReadsCurrent` | `go test ./cmd/datawatch/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationCLIDefaultVersionReadsCurrent'` | Every control verb, with the flag omitted, first `GET`s the Automation and then `POST`s the control with `expected_version` read from that `GET`, in that order; each verb's body (member, member_id, on_complete, cancel_in_flight, reason) is unchanged | Unit (CLI, fake REST sink) | **Yes** (`cmd/datawatch/automation_default_version_cli_test.go`) | Pass | No | fake REST sink only; live behaviour of the built binary covered by story TS-837 (PASS 2026-10-29) |
| CLI controls, implicit version: a 409 race re-reads the version and retries once; if the retry is also refused the command gives up | `TestAutomationCLIDefaultVersionRetriesOnceOnRace`, `TestAutomationCLIDefaultVersionGivesUpAfterOneRetry` | `go test ./cmd/datawatch/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationCLIDefaultVersion'` | A control `POST` refused with a 409 version mismatch is retried exactly once after re-reading the version (two GETs, two POSTs), the second `POST` carrying the re-read version, and the command succeeds; when both `POST`s are refused the command fails with the daemon's 409 message after at most the one retry, never looping | Unit (CLI, fake REST sink) | **Yes** (`cmd/datawatch/automation_default_version_cli_test.go`) | Pass | No | fake REST sink only; live behaviour of the built binary covered by story TS-837 (PASS 2026-10-29) |
| CLI controls, explicit `--expected-version`: sent as given (even 0), no pre-read, and a stale one is still refused | `TestAutomationCLIExplicitStaleVersionStillRefused`, `TestAutomationCLIExplicitVersionIsSentUnchanged` | `go test ./cmd/datawatch/ -count=1 -run 'TestAutomationCLIExplicit'` | An explicit `--expected-version` is posted exactly as typed, with no `GET` in front and no retry on a 409; the daemon's `409: version mismatch` message surfaces verbatim as the command's error | Unit (CLI, fake REST sink) | **Yes** (`cmd/datawatch/automation_explicit_version_cli_test.go`) | Pass | No | fake REST sink only; live behaviour of the built binary covered by story TS-837 (PASS 2026-10-29) |
| Config `autonomous.automation.agent_insert_policy` | `TestConfigAutomationAgentInsertPolicyDefault`, `TestConfigAutomationAgentInsertPolicyLoadDefaultsToAllow`, `TestConfigAutomationAgentInsertPolicyRoundTrip`, `TestConfigAutomationAgentInsertPolicyValidator`, `TestConfigAutomationAgentInsertPolicyLoadRejectsBadValue` | `go test ./internal/config/ -count=1 -run 'TestConfigAutomationAgentInsertPolicy'` | The default and an empty value mean `allow`. `allow` and `require_operator` survive a save and load. Any other value is rejected | Unit (config) | **Yes** (`internal/config/config_agent_insert_policy_test.go`) | | No | |
| Live: pause, resume, cancel with `cancel_in_flight=false`, `insert_member` with the one-urgent cap, and `approve_insert` on a sandbox daemon | `TestAutomationControlLiveSmoke` | `DW_LIVE_AUTOMATION_CONTROL_SMOKE=https://127.0.0.1:18443 go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -timeout 10m -run 'TestAutomationControlLiveSmoke' -v` | Opt-in. Skipped unless `DW_LIVE_AUTOMATION_CONTROL_SMOKE` is set; the variable has no default and its value is the sandbox daemon's base URL, so the test cannot reach production by accident. It calls only the daemon's REST API. The `cancel_in_flight=true` path is not exercised live and is covered by the Manager tests | Live (opt-in, sandbox daemon, TLS port 18443) | **No** (written and opt-in, `internal/autonomous/automation_control_live_smoke_test.go`; not run in this build) | | **No** | Owed: the operator's live run, with date |

**Mobile-Parity: owed, not yet filed.** Issues are not filed from this
pipeline. File on `dmz006/datawatch-app` when the 3b branch merges:

> `feat(automation): control operations on a running Automation`
>
> Server added `POST /api/automations/{id}/{pause|resume|cancel|skip_member|insert_member|remove_member|reorder_edges|approve_insert}`
> (body `{expected_version, actor?, reason?}` plus the operation's own fields;
> stale `expected_version` = `409`). `cancel` requires `cancel_in_flight`
> (`true` ends the member sessions that are running, `false` leaves them
> running; a missing value = `400`). `insert_member` takes `member.prd_id`,
> `member.name?`, `urgent?`, `after?` and a required `reason`; an insert into a
> running Automation is held in `pending_inserts` until `approve_insert`. New
> config key `autonomous.automation.agent_insert_policy` (`allow` default,
> `require_operator`).
> Acceptance: Android and iOS offer pause, resume and cancel on an Automation,
> make the user pick `cancel_in_flight` explicitly with no default, show
> `pending_inserts`, and surface the `409` and `400` messages. The PWA has no
> Automation view in this phase, so these controls are API-only until Phase 6.

## Phase 3a — multi-cursor (fork/join + nested Automations)

surfaces that carry them. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md`
(the Phase 3a sections).

Each test row is built and unit-tested, and none is Validated. Validated is filled in by
the operator's live run, with its date, per the rule at the top of this file. The live
row at the end is the run still owed.

## Restart during launch: boot gate and start-confirm bound — unreleased

A worker whose first launch was held, so its pane holds only a bare shell, is no longer adopted at boot. A live session is adopted only once its agent has started, and an adopted claude-code session is held to the start-confirm bound. A launch still in flight at shutdown is drained within a fixed 15 s grace. Operator guide: `docs/operations.md` (Restart safety). The live check is the restart matrix row in the section below.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |

A bare shell with no output reads as not started, and an unknown session reads as not started. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/session/agent_started_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | No real pane was used. |
| Boot adoption gate | `TestBootAdoptionGate*` (4 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run '^TestBootAdoptionGate'`; fake session list and killer | A live session is adopted only when its agent has started. A live bare shell is ended through the killer and its task is reset to pending with the start-failure reason, with the retry count and start failures unchanged. A session with its agent running but no first turn is adopted, not killed. With no agent-started hook wired, a live session is adopted as before. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/boot_adoption_gate_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | |
| Adopted session is waited on under the start-confirm bound | `TestAdoptedSession*` (2 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run '^TestAdoptedSession'`; fake clock and panes | A healthy adopted session runs to completion under the bound. Without a pane hook the wait is unchanged. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/adopted_start_confirm_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | |
| Adopted start failure counts against the start budget | `TestAdoptedStartFailure*` (5 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run '^TestAdoptedStartFailure'`; fake clock and panes | A session that stays in `waiting_input` with no assistant turn past the limit is ended and counted as a start failure against the start retry budget. The silent window is measured from the task's launch time. A session that shows a first assistant turn, or leaves `waiting_input`, is never failed by the bound. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/adopted_start_confirm_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | |
| Launch registry: finish inside grace, roll back at the deadline, refuse starts while draining | `TestLaunchRegistry*` (4 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/session/ -count=1 -run '^TestLaunchRegistry'` | A launch that finishes inside the grace is not returned. The registry is empty after an error path. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/session/launch_registry_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | |

Each rolled-back session is logged. An empty drain writes nothing. | Unit | **Yes** (`cmd/datawatch/shutdown_launch_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | The grace is a fixed value, not a config key. |
| Restart-during-launch cases on fakes | `TestRestartLaunchCases` (5 subtests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run '^TestRestartLaunchCases$'`; fakes from the boot-resume and start-confirm tests | Five cases through the boot pass: a bare shell is ended and reset with the retry count unchanged; an agent with no first turn is failed fast by the bound; a healthy session is kept and never killed; a launch that finishes inside the shutdown grace is adopted by the next boot; a launch rolled back at the deadline is not adopted. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/restart_launch_cases_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | The shutdown grace outcome is modelled as the agent state the next boot sees. |

chunks.body:
## Daemon restart matrix: in-flight work across a restart

A sandbox harness, `scripts/restart-matrix.sh`, restarts a throwaway daemon with one unit of autonomous work in each of twelve states and records what became of it. Operator guide: `docs/operations.md` (Restart safety). Findings and the open choices: `docs/plans/restart-matrix-findings.md`. The unit rows cover the two defects the matrix found; the live rows are the matrix itself. Every live run used a fake backend for planner, worker, verifier and guardrail judge, on one machine, with one run per cell, so Validated is Partly, not Yes: no real model, no real terminal UI session, no systemd unit and no real service-manager kill was involved.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

chunks.title: Testing Tracker
chunks.heading: WS output-scope unsubscribe contract — test-only flake fixed (BL550)
chunks.body:
## WS output-scope unsubscribe contract — test-only flake fixed (BL550)

The unsubscribe contract: when a client sends `unsubscribe` for a session, its subscription for that session is removed, this client's screen-capture pipeline for that session is cancelled, and further output frames are stopped for that session only — the client keeps receiving frames for sessions it is still subscribed to, the other session's capture is not cancelled, and other clients on the hub are unaffected. Short and full session IDs refer to the same session both when unsubscribing and when matching delivery (`a1b2` ≡ `testhost-a1b2`), and unsubscribing an id the client never subscribed is a no-op. The Release-CI flake in `TestWSOutputScope_UnsubscribeStopsDeliveryAndCancelsCapture` (subtest `same_id`, failed in 0.01 s, passed locally) was a scheduling race in the test harness, not in the production path: `findHubClient` snapshotted the hub registry immediately while the hub applies client registration in its own Run goroutine, so the registry write could lag the frames the test had already observed. Fixed in the test file only (`internal/server/ws_output_scope_test.go`): `wsSubscribe` matches the initial `pane_capture` on the exact `session_id` (short/full forms equal) instead of substring-scanning the frame payload; `findHubClient` and the capture-cancel wait poll their real conditions under a deadline bounded by the shared frame timeout with every original assertion preserved at the deadline; and a `t.Cleanup` cancels any still-live capture and waits (bounded poll) until `Hub.ClientCount()` is back to zero so nothing leaks into the next subtest. No production behavior change; no non-test file touched. No live connection was exercised for this fix, so **Validated** stays **No**.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unsubscribe removes the subscription and stops further output frames for that session only — the other subscribed session keeps delivery | **Yes** (`TestWSOutputScope_UnsubscribeStopsDeliveryAndCancelsCapture`, subtests `same_id`, `short unsubscribes full`, `full unsubscribes short`, `internal/server/ws_output_scope_test.go`; no-op for an unknown id in `TestClientUnsubscribe_Direct`) | **No** | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/server/ -run WSOutputScope -count=50`; `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/server/ -count=10`; `GOMAXPROCS=2 go test ./internal/server/ -run WSOutputScope -cpu 1,2` | Test-only fix; the production `MsgUnsubscribe` / `client.unsubscribe` path is unchanged |
| Unsubscribe cancels this client's screen capture for that session and no other — a still-subscribed session's capture keeps running | **Yes** (same test: the real cancel is swapped for an observable one, asserts it fires after the unsubscribe acknowledgement and that the other session's cancel entry is still present; `TestClientUnsubscribe_Direct` pins the cancel-count contract on `client.unsubscribe`) | **No** | same as above | Capture goroutine teardown is now explicit in `t.Cleanup` (bounded poll on `Hub.ClientCount() == 0`) so a failed subtest cannot leak its capture goroutine into the next one |
| Short and full session IDs match when unsubscribing (and in delivery) | **Yes** (subtests `short unsubscribes full` and `full unsubscribes short`; id-matching pinned by `TestSessionIDsMatch`) | **No** | same as above | `wsSubscribe` now matches on the exact `session_id` instead of a payload substring that another session's pane text could satisfy |
| Other WS tests sharing the changed helpers audited for the same race | **Yes** and needed no change: `TestWSOutputScope_SubscribedModeFiltersTerminalFrames`, `TestWSOutputScope_ShortAndFullIDsMatch`, `TestWSOutputScope_ConfigDefaultSubscribedForNoHelloClient` (all use `wsSubscribe`); `TestWSOutputScope_MixedClients`, `TestWSOutputScope_AllModeGetsEverySession`, `TestWSOutputScope_HelloBadValueUnchanged`, `TestWSOutputScope_ConfigDefaultReadLive` (same hub/drain helpers) | **No** | same as above (all pass at `-count=50`; package at `-count=10`) | Audit result: no other test asserted on a hub-registry or capture-cancel state without a deadline-bounded wait |

chunks.heading: PRD worktree buildability — `EnsureWorktree` docs-index placeholder
chunks.body:
## PRD worktree buildability — `EnsureWorktree` docs-index placeholder

When the daemon creates or reuses a PRD's git worktree, `EnsureWorktree`
(`internal/autonomous/worktree.go`) calls the `prepareWorktree` helper
(`internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare.go`): in repos containing the
`internal/docsindex` package it ensures
`internal/docsindex/assets/docs-bm25-index.json` exists, writing the
same `{}` placeholder `make docs-index` writes, only when the file is
missing (an existing index is never touched), keeps the file
git-ignored (falling back to the worktree's own `info/exclude` if the
ignore rule is absent) and never stages or commits it. Before this,
packages importing `internal/docsindex` failed to build in a fresh
worktree with `pattern assets/docs-bm25-index.json: no matching files
found`, and the daemon reported an otherwise-fine task as failed with
"no new changes to verify".

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creates when missing — a new or reused worktree gets a `{}` placeholder at `internal/docsindex/assets/docs-bm25-index.json` when the file is absent (same content `make docs-index` seeds) | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_CreatesWhenMissing`, `TestEnsureDocsIndexPlaceholder_CreatesEmptyIndex`, `TestWorktreePrepare_ReuseRecreates` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Covers both fresh creation and recreation on a reused worktree |
| Leaves existing untouched — an existing (custom or fully generated) index is neither rewritten nor mtime-churned when the worktree is reused | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_LeavesExistingUntouched`, `TestEnsureDocsIndexPlaceholder_LeavesExistingFileUntouched` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Never clobbers a real generated index |
| Never staged / stays ignored — placeholder absent from `git status --porcelain` and the index; `git check-ignore -q` passes; exclude line appended to the worktree's `info/exclude` only when the repo `.gitignore` lacks the rule, idempotently (no duplicate on re-prepare) | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_NeverStaged`, `TestPrepareWorktree_GitIgnoredByRepoGitignore`, `TestPrepareWorktree_NonIgnoredRepoGetsExcludeLine`, `TestWorktreePrepare_ExcludeLineNotDuplicated`, `TestAppendGitExcludeLine_IdsAndNoDuplicate` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Prepares never run `git add` or any staging/commit |
| No-op for repos without `internal/docsindex` — no files, no directories, no `info/exclude` mutation in foreign checkouts | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_NoOpWithoutDocsIndex`, `TestEnsureDocsIndexPlaceholder_IgnoresForeignRepos`, `TestPrepareWorktree_RejectsUnknownRepos` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Preparation is non-fatal and must not touch other projects' trees |

chunks.heading: Plan review before approval + smoke/final-gate verifier split
chunks.body:
## Plan review before approval + smoke/final-gate verifier split

Pre-approval plan reviewer: after decompose, a configured LLM reviews the ORIGINAL spec against the plan (requirement coverage, task sizes, dependencies, non-trivial verification scripts, scope outside write_dirs) and records a `plan_review` verdict on the Automaton. Modes `autonomous.plan_review_mode` = `off` (default, no review, approval never affected) / `warn` (verdict recorded and visible, never blocks) / `block` (a `ok:false` verdict refuses approve until it is replaced). A reviewer outage is recorded (`reviewer_failed`) and never blocks in any mode. The plan's own smoke / final-gate verification task is judged by a separate LLM from `autonomous.smoke_verification_backend` / `autonomous.smoke_verification_model`; explicit per-task verifier overrides always win. Surfaces: REST `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/plan-review`, MCP `autonomous_prd_plan_review`, comm `autonomous plan-review <id>`, CLI `datawatch autonomous prd-plan-review <id>` (alias `plan-review`), PWA verdict panel + re-run button + settings fields (en/de/es/fr/ja).

chunks.heading: Tolerant `issues` parser for guardrail verdicts and per-task verification — v9.5.34
chunks.body:
## Tolerant `issues` parser for guardrail verdicts and per-task verification — v9.5.34

The guardrail judge and the per-task verifier used to have to return `issues` as an
array of JSON strings: a single object element — or a bare string/object where an
array was expected — failed the whole verdict/verification decode
(`json: cannot unmarshal object into GuardrailVerdict.issues.0 of type string`),
blocking the PRD even though the work was done. The tolerant decoder
(`internal/autonomous/tolerant_issues.go` — `parseIssues` + custom `UnmarshalJSON`
on `GuardrailVerdict` and `VerificationResult`) accepts all of those shapes and
renders issue objects into readable text, while every other field keeps strict
typing. See CHANGELOG v9.5.34.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tolerant `issues` decoding — string / object / mixed-array / bare-string / bare-object / bare-number / null shapes normalize to `[]string`; objects render `[severity] file:line: description / message` (deduped, stable order); malformed issues JSON still errors; all other fields (e.g. `"outcome": 5`) still fail strict unmarshal | **Yes** (`TestTolerantIssuesShapes`, `TestTolerantIssuesStrictOtherFields`, `TestIssuesRoundTrip`, `TestIncidentFixtureSizes` in `internal/autonomous/tolerant_issues_test.go`) | **No** (this session did not perform a live rejudge — set to **Yes** with the run date + host once one is actually observed, e.g. a PRD previously blocked by `json: cannot unmarshal object into GuardrailVerdict.issues.0 of type string` rejudged via `POST /api/autonomous/prds/<id>/rejudge`) | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Only `issues` is widened; the raw judge text is kept on the verdict in `raw_judge` (16 KiB), and the judge/verifier prompts now instruct "issues must be an array of plain strings, one sentence each, never objects" |

## PWA schedules-flood — `make test-e2e-pwa` (story `scripts/test-stories/pwa/schedule-flood.mjs`, TS-797 spec)

The PWA schedules-flood story: after a WS disconnect/reconnect burst with 20+
seeded sessions, the PWA's `GET /api/schedules` fetches stay coalesced (≤ 5,
independent of session count) and the browser never sees
`net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`. Run against **two origins**: (A) the
untrusted self-signed TLS origin, (B) a trusted TLS origin (service worker
controlled). `make test-e2e-pwa` is the local, non-docker route
(`scripts/e2e-pwa.sh`: isolated daemon + `npm ci` + `node schedule-flood.mjs`);
exit code = story's (0 pass / 1 fail / 2 skip).

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coalesced `/api/schedules` refreshes after WS reconnect — untrusted self-signed TLS origin (A) | No (fix lives in `internal/server/web/app.js` (`_loadSessionSchedules` coalescer); no `node --test` unit test for it) | **Yes** (2026-10-20, `make test-e2e-pwa`, `rc=0`) | Isolated daemon from `bin/datawatch` on fresh 127.0.0.1 ports (config from `testdata/datawatch.yaml`, self-generated TLS); 20 seeded shell sessions (always cleaned up — 20 disposed observed); Playwright + headless Chrome; evidence dir `/tmp/dw-e2e-pwa-04LWs3/evidence/schedule-flood` (removed post-success) | `PASS [A-untrusted-tls] /api/schedules=1 (limit 5) failed-events=0` — one fetch covered the reconnected detail view; zero `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`; `/api/sessions` + `/api/stats` 200 after the burst |
| Coalesced `/api/schedules` refreshes after WS reconnect — trusted TLS origin (B, service-worker controlled) | No (same as above) | **Yes** (2026-10-20, same run, scenario B self-generated: openssl throwaway CA + Node TLS proxy + Chrome `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list`) | Same harness; `TEST_TRUSTED_TLS` unset → auto-trusted origin; `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` asserted set before request counting | `PASS [B-trusted-tls] sw-controller=true /api/schedules=1 (limit 5)`; 4 `requestfailed` events were non-`ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` (expected offline-window/WS-reconnect closes), so the bounded-flood assertion held |
