chunks.heading: Baseline measurement — before-fix vs after-fix (connection-drop investigation, 2026-10-20)
chunks.body:
### Baseline measurement — before-fix vs after-fix (connection-drop investigation, 2026-10-20)

The story now also logs peak in-flight concurrency per phase — `load` = page load +
detail-view open; `reconnect` = the WS-disconnect → recover window — so before/after
comparisons diff on one line. Both runs 2026-10-20, 20 seeded sessions, scenario A
(untrusted-TLS origin; the daemon offers HTTP/1.1 only, so the browser's 6-concurrent
per-origin cap applies exactly as on the phone/cellular path). Two binaries with
different embedded `app.js` — no git stash: **before** = `app.js` as of `31d96b1e`
(parent of the fix commit, no `_loadSessionSchedules` coalescer), **after** = HEAD
(`8412e745` coalescer in place), both run via `bash scripts/e2e-pwa.sh schedule-flood`.

| origin | metric | before-fix (no coalescer) | after-fix (HEAD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (untrusted TLS) | total `/api/schedules` | **42** (page-load+detail=1, **reconnect-window=41**) | **1** (page-load only; reconnect-window=0) |
| A (untrusted TLS) | peak in-flight, all traffic, reconnect window | 8 | 0 |
| A (untrusted TLS) | peak in-flight `/api/schedules`, reconnect window | 4 | 0 |
| A (untrusted TLS) | story verdict | FAIL (`42 > limit 5`) | PASS, `failed-events=0` |

Evidence: `.scratch/evidence/README.md` (method + pointers), `.scratch/evidence/BASELINE-run-before.log` and `.scratch/evidence/run-after.log` (full run transcripts),
`.scratch/evidence-before/run-1/` (before-run screenshots + daemon log), binaries `.scratch/bin/datawatch-{before,after}`.

**Interpretation (CONFIRMED):** the pre-fix burst is ~41× the post-fix footprint, fired
in the reconnect window, proportional to session count (one un-coalesced fetch per
session update of the active detail view). 41+ requests against a 6-connection
per-origin pool starve the co-residents on that origin — `/api/sessions`, `/api/stats`,
and the WS upgrade handshake itself — which to an operator on cellular looks like the
device "dropped the connection." The flood does **not** by itself sever the WS
transport; it exhausts the shared HTTP pool. Other observed drop-path code — WS stale
watchdog (50 s stale threshold, 20 s ping tick, 50–70 s detection), reconnect backoff,
and the server's 30 s protocol-ping ticker (`internal/server/ws.go` `writePump`) — are
separate, legitimate disconnect/reconnect mechanisms, recorded for the record and not
fixed in this pass. See CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased].

## Autonomous completion-guardrail rejudgment — `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/rejudge` + MCP `autonomous_prd_rejudge`

New endpoint and MCP tool. Re-runs the PRD-completion "rules-review" guardrail for a `blocked` Automaton whose every task in every story is `completed`, without resetting or editing any task. The verdict is durably recorded on the Automaton's decision log (`guardrail_verdict` Decision + save, then a `guardrail_rejudge` Decision attributed to the acting operator) **before** any status change: `pass` clears the blocked reason and completes the Automaton; `block` keeps it `blocked` with the blocked reason set from the new verdict; no verdict (judge error or empty outcome) keeps it `blocked` with its previous reason and returns an error.

chunks.heading: Service worker activate guard — `shouldNavigateOnActivate` in `internal/server/web/sw.js`
chunks.body:
## Service worker activate guard — `shouldNavigateOnActivate` in `internal/server/web/sw.js`

On a real cache-name upgrade the new SW must force every controlled window to re-navigate so
installed PWA tabs drop the stale cached app.js. But `activate` also re-runs on a no-op
re-activation (browser re-activates the same SW on restart with no cache change) — the guard keeps
that path from needlessly churning open tabs: `clients.claim()` is still called, but the
`matchAll`/`navigate` loop is skipped when no stale cache key exists. The pure guard is unit-tested
and the `activate` listener is driven end-to-end with a stubbed `self` in `sw.test.js`; the
operator-visible double-load symptom on daemon restart was then verified live in headless Chrome
(CDP, `live-sw-check/` below).

| Test Condition | Unit | Live | Test ID / Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guard: no keys, or only the current key → navigate skipped; current + stale key(s) → navigate; non-array input tolerated | **Yes** | No | `shouldNavigateOnActivate: no keys at all is a no-op re-activation`, `...only the current cache present...`, `...current plus a stale key is a genuine upgrade`, `...multiple stale keys are a genuine upgrade`, `...non-array input is treated as no keys` in `internal/server/web/sw.test.js` | 5 pure-guard tests, `node --test` |
| `activate`: stale cache present → stale caches deleted, `claim()` once, every window navigated exactly once | **Yes** | No | `activate: stale cache present → stale deleted, claim called, every window navigated once` in `internal/server/web/sw.test.js` | Real `activate` listener, stubbed `self`/`caches`/`clients`; also `activate: one window navigate rejecting does not abort the others or the handler` |
| `activate`: no-op re-activation (only current cache, or no caches) → `claim()` still called, **no** navigate | **Yes** | No | `activate: only the current cache present (no-op) → claim called, no navigate`, `activate: no caches at all → claim called, no navigate` in `internal/server/web/sw.test.js` | `matchAll` skipped on the no-op path |
| Live: daemon-restart / reload under an already-activated current-version SW → exactly one document load, no spurious reload | No | **Yes** | `live-sw-check/`: `sw-live.mjs` (Phase B) + `RESULTS.md`; daemon `live-sw-check/config.yaml` (port 18491), log in `daemon-b.log` | Headless Chrome 155.0.8059.39 over CDP (puppeteer-core was absent); CDP `Page.loadEventFired`=1, `navigation entries`=[navigate], `reloadCount` 0, hook log empty. Phase A (fresh install) showed the one-time first-load SW-takeover reload that happens independently of the guard — not a guard-driven navigate |
| Live: genuine cache-name upgrade (new SW, stale cache present) → exactly one SW-driven reload, stale cache purged, new SW controls the page | No | **Yes** | `live-sw-check/RESULTS.md` (Phase C: `sw.js` `CACHE_NAME` bumped to `...-51-livecheck`, daemon rebuilt + restarted) | CDP `frameNavigated` once at +2.1s after the SW update burst (`reloadCount` 1); `caches` ended as [bumped key] only (stale deleted); page-script hook never hit — reload is the guard's `win.navigate`, not app JS. `sw.js` then reverted and rebuilt |

chunks.body:
## MCP error-mode parity with REST — BL463 (2026-10-20)

Follow-up to the findings in `docs/plans/2026-10-20-bl463-mcp-drop-findings.md`. Before
this change, many MCP handlers failed "soft": they returned
`mcpsdk.NewToolResultText("Error: ...")` with a nil Go error, so the result carried no
`isError` flag, no tool name, and (for REST-loopback proxies) no upstream HTTP status
or body — the same wire result a successful call would have, and `POST /api/mcp/call`
mirrored that (HTTP 200, `isError:false`) while direct REST returned 4xx/5xx. The
shared helpers in `internal/mcp/errors.go` (`toolError`, `toolErrorf`,
`toolHTTPError`) now return real IsError results named after the tool call,
and the `sx_parity.go` REST-loopback proxy helpers capture and carry the upstream
status + body (truncated at 2048 chars).

| Interface | Tested | Validated | Test File | Validation Steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toolError` flags `IsError` and names the operation | **Yes** | No | `TestToolError_FlagsIsErrorWithPrefix` in `internal/mcp/errors_test.go` | PASS |
| `toolErrorf` formats args into the message | **Yes** | No | `TestToolErrorf_FormatsArguments` in `internal/mcp/errors_test.go` | PASS |
| `toolHTTPError` carries the HTTP status + upstream body, degrades to the status text on an empty body, and bounds oversized bodies at 2048 bytes (maxToolErrorBody); the `sx_parity.go` loopback proxy helpers cap their error bodies the same way (boundedErrorBody) | **Yes** | No | `TestToolHTTPError_CarriesStatusAndBody`, `TestToolHTTPError_NoBody`, `TestToolHTTPError_TruncatesOversizedBody`, `TestBoundedErrorBody_TrimsAndCaps` in `internal/mcp/errors_test.go` | PASS |
| `channel_routing_config_set` validation failures return `IsError` results named after the tool | **Yes** | No | `TestBL331_ChannelRoutingConfigSet_InvalidJSON` / `_EmptyRulesJSON` in `internal/mcp/bl331_channel_routing_tools_test.go` (assert `res.IsError` + tool-name prefix) | PASS |
| Session-handler failure modes (`send_input`, `rename_session`, vision `image_path` read failure) return named IsError results | **Yes** | No | `TestBL91_SendInput_SessionNotFound`, `TestBL91_SendInput_MissingID`, `TestBL91_RenameSession_MissingArgs` (`internal/mcp/bl91_handler_test.go`); `TestBL368_VisionDescribe_FileNotFound_ReturnsError` (`internal/mcp/bl368_vision_describe_test.go`) | PASS — `go test ./internal/mcp/... -count=1`: 269 passed, 0 failed; `go test ./internal/server/... -count=1`: 1013 passed, 0 failed; `go build ./...` clean |
| Release-smoke §7r: **`get_my_scope` called by a live session** returns its own scope (positive: `session_id`/`full_id`/`mode`/`resolved_via` present and consistent; negative: unresolvable hint → `isError:true` + named body) | **Yes (script)** | **Yes** | `scripts/release-smoke-stdio-mcp.sh` probes 5–6, invoked by `scripts/release-smoke.sh` §7r (probe starts a fixture session when it owns the daemon) | PASS (2026-10-20) — live daemon run (fallback path) + sandbox run with `DW_SESSION_HINT=leaksess-abc` (`resolved_via=hint` asserted) |

chunks.body:
## Daemon restart safety (live, opt-in) — BL462

Live companion to the BL462 restart audit (`docs/plans/bl462-restart-audit-findings.md`).
It repeats the audit's sequence against a real daemon: start a long claude-code
task session, restart the daemon, and check that the tmux session survives,
the session record is not failed, and the session log keeps growing. The test
is skipped unless `DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1`, so `go test ./...` in CI skips it.

Run it on the daemon's host, against a sandbox daemon (never production), with
the same `TMUX_TMPDIR` as that daemon:

```sh
DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1 DW_BASE=https://127.0.0.1:18443 DW_BASE_TOKEN=... \
  DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD='<command that restarts the sandbox daemon>' \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 20m -run TestBL462_DaemonRestartSurvivesLive -v ./internal/session/
```

Leave `DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD` unset to restart through the operator path
(`systemctl --user restart datawatch`, falling back to `datawatch restart`).
Only do that from an operator shell where that unit is the daemon behind `DW_BASE`.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daemon restart with a live claude-code task session — tmux session survives, session record not `failed`/`killed`/spurious `complete`, session log grows after restart (re-pipe), task reaches a terminal state if it finishes within the wait | **Yes** (skip path only: `TestBL462_DaemonRestartSurvivesLive` in `internal/session/restart_safety_live_test.go`, run by `.datawatch/verify/bl462-s3-live-restart-test.sh`) | **No** (gated live run not performed; no sandbox daemon was started for it) | `go test` with `DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1` against a live daemon via `DW_BASE`/`DW_BASE_TOKEN`; restart is `systemctl --user restart datawatch` or the `datawatch restart` CLI, or `DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD` for a sandbox | Verifies what the audit verified by hand. Does not cover subprocess sessions (F4) or the capacity lease (F1); the audit's live run of those is in `docs/plans/bl462-restart-audit-findings.md` |

chunks.heading: Boot-resume adopts a live in-progress worker (deterministic + gated live)
chunks.body:
## Boot-resume adopts a live in-progress worker (deterministic + gated live)

Deterministic coverage for the adoption behavior — a daemon restart
resumes a run whose task was `in_progress` with a live worker session:
the live session is **adopted** (task stays `in_progress` on the same
session id, capacity lease re-adopted, **no duplicate spawn**, worker
finishes and the task verifies and completes), a dead session with a
completion marker in its output **goes straight to verification** (no
re-run of finished work), and a dead session without a marker **resets to
`pending`** (the only reset case). All sessions are fakes (map-backed
`alive` function, recording killer, fake output, spawn counter); every
wait is a bounded poll — no fixed sleeps; table-driven across the
`claude-code`, `opencode`, and `pi-prompt` backends; verified green with
`-race -count=3` (three races, no fixed sleeps). The pre-existing
`TestAdoptSessionDecision` (decision table for the same code) is
unchanged.

Gated live companion — one PRD with a long worker, restarted mid-worker
through the operator path (`systemctl --user` / `datawatch restart`) or
`DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD`; asserts the session id is unchanged after
restart, the session is not `killed`, no task is re-issued a new
session, and the task drives to verification/completion.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boot-resume: alive worker adopted — task stays `in_progress`, same session id, `AdoptedSession` set, capacity lease held, idempotent on a second boot | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_AliveAdopted` in `internal/autonomous/adopt_live_session_test.go`; `-race -count=3` | Fake sessions; no production state. Boot scan parked via `SetServerReadyCh` to keep the concurrent paths deterministic (same pattern as `TestRunDedupe`) |
| Boot-resume: dead worker without marker — task reset to `pending`, session id cleared, killer called for the exact session | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_DeadReset` | Table over dead-with-no-output / empty-session / never-started; no marker in the dead output in any case |
| Boot-resume: dead worker that finished during the down window — output carries `DATAWATCH_COMPLETE` → task goes to `verifying`, verifier runs once, **no spawn** | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_FinishedWhileDown` | Completing session is recorded as `complete` in the fake registry; the run finishes `completed` with verifyCount=1, spawnN=0 |
| Boot-resume: adopted task not re-spawned — executor run over an adopted `in_progress` task waits for the existing session (0 spawns), completes after fake completion; two concurrent `Run` calls start exactly one executor and the PRD stays `running` | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_NoDuplicateSpawn` | `apiFixture` + `countingSpawn`/`recordedKiller`; drainOnCleanup wired. Verified with `-race -count=3` (all green) |
| Restart while a worker PRD task is live — session id unchanged after restart, no second spawn (no task re-issued a session), worker not killed, task drives to verification/completion | **Yes** (skip path only) | **No** (gated live run not performed) | `TestDaemonRestartAdoptsLiveWorkerLive` in `internal/session/restart_adopt_live_test.go`; `DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1` + `DW_BASE` (+ optional `DW_BASE_TOKEN`, `DW_LIVE_RESTART_PROJECT_DIR`, `DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD`); run with `-timeout 25m`; cleanup kills only its own probe session via the API (no raw tmux kill) | PRD-level counterpart of `TestBL462_DaemonRestartSurvivesLive`: reuses `newBL462LiveClient`, `bl462RestartCommand`, `bl462PollUntil`, `bl462TmuxHasSession` from `restart_safety_live_test.go`. The restart subprocess env is sanitized by `bl462RestartEnv`: TMUX and TMUX_TMPDIR stripped, except the `datawatch restart` CLI fallback which keeps TMUX_TMPDIR (documented exception — the CLI re-execs the daemon in the ambient env and must keep the tmux socket dir) |

chunks.body:
## Restart no longer revives stale running Automata — new `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` limit — v9.5.32

At daemon restart, an Automaton left running is now gated: it resumes only if its newest activity is within `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` (default 3600) **and** its project directory still exists; `0` = never auto-resume, `-1` = no age limit (missing dirs still park). Parked Automata become `blocked` with a plain-English reason + operator alert, and each decision (resumed/parked, age, reason) is recorded in the startup log, the decision log, and the autonomous status `boot_resume` list.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boot resume gate (daemon startup path) — covers running and failed Automata (failed ones whose tasks were all killed by the restart); fresh Automaton resumes; stale (age > limit) parked; `0` parks even fresh; `-1` skips the age test but a missing project directory still parks; park ⇒ `blocked` + `BlockedReason` + operator alert; report records outcome/age/reason | **Yes** (13 tests, including the failed-Automaton path: `TestBootResumeGateFailedFreshRecovered`, `TestBootResumeGateFailedStaleParked`, `TestBootResumeGateCancelledUntouched`, `TestBootResumeGateFailedLimits`; `TestBootResumeGateFreshResumes`, `TestBootResumeGateZeroLimitParksFresh`, `TestBootResumeGateMinusOneSkipsStale`, `TestBootResumeGateStaleParked`, `TestBootResumeGateMissingDirParks`, `TestBootResumeGateDefaultConfig`, `TestBootResumeGateReport`, `TestBootResumeGateAlertOnPark`, `TestDecideBootResumeUnit` in `internal/autonomous/boot_resume_gate_test.go`; plus config-load tests in `internal/config/resume_max_age_test.go`) | **No** | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` and `go test ./internal/config/`; fake store + seeded PRDs aged via timestamps, temp dirs for the missing-directory case | `0` and `-1` are meaningful sentinels (round-trip preserved through config YAML); `DefaultConfig()` returns 3600; a parked Automaton is manually approvable — no silent re-run |
| REST config — `GET /api/config` reports `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` default 3600; `PUT /api/config` round-trips the key (0 and -1 preserved); `PUT /api/autonomous/config` persists it | **Yes** (3 tests: `TestResumeMaxAge_GetConfigDefaultIs3600`, `TestResumeMaxAge_PutConfigRoundTrip`, `TestResumeMaxAge_PutAutonomousConfigPersists` in `internal/server/resume_max_age_config_surfaces_test.go`) | **No** | `go test ./internal/server/`, real HTTP handler against in-memory config | Written values survive YAML round-trip, so an explicit 0/-1 is not clobbered back to the 3600 default on reload |
| MCP config — `autonomous_config_set` / `autonomous_config_get` accept and return `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds`, including the 0/-1 sentinels; tool docs mention the key | **Yes** (2 tests: `TestAutonomousConfigSet_ResumeMaxAgeSentinels`, `TestAutonomousConfigTools_DocumentResumeMaxAge` in `internal/mcp/resume_max_age_tools_test.go`) | **No** | `go test ./internal/mcp/`, fake autonomous manager | 0 and -1 pass through unchanged (not clamped to a positive value) |
| CLI help — `datawatch autonomous config-set --help` / `config-get --help` document `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` with the example `config-set '{"resume_max_age_seconds":1800}'` and the `0 = never resume, -1 = no age limit` semantics | **Yes** (2 tests: `TestAutonomousConfigSetHelp_MentionsResumeMaxAge`, `TestAutonomousConfigGetHelp_MentionsResumeMaxAge` in `cmd/datawatch/cli_autonomous_help_test.go`; sibling `max_engines_per_node` help tests in the same file) | **No** | `go test ./cmd/datawatch/`, help-string assertions | The key is the operator's primary knob for "how old is too old at restart" |
| Comm-channel `configure` — help text and the settings list both mention `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` (alongside `max_concurrent_tasks`), so a session can set it without leaving the channel | **Yes** (`TestHandleConfigure_HelpAndListMentionResumeMaxAge` in `internal/router/configure_help_test.go`; sibling `max_concurrent_tasks` mention test in the same file) | **No** | `go test ./internal/router/` | Help copy carries the same 0/-1 semantics as the CLI so the values read identically in both surfaces |
| Web settings field + locale bundles — Settings > General > Autonomous card exposes `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` as a min-less number (placeholder 3600) so 0 (never) and -1 (always) are settable, with the `settings_resume_max_age` label + `settings_resume_max_age_hint` translated in all five bundles (en/de/es/fr/ja); the hint explains the park/alert behavior | **Yes** (1 test: "autonomous settings expose resume_max_age_seconds as a min-less number with a label key" in `internal/server/web/app-autonomous-settings-fields.test.js`, which also asserts the en bundle defines `settings_resume_max_age`) | **No** | `node:test` (`node --test internal/server/web/`), loads `app.js` in a browser stub and reads `locales/en.json` | Field deliberately has **no** `min` bound — clamping would silently reject the 0/-1 sentinels; bundles: en/de/es/fr/ja json files |

## Per-tree write lock + same-tree admission + ci-watch own-commit pin — v9.4.0 / v9.5.0

The 2026-10-13 incident (three concurrent PRDs, one working tree) shipped two
cooperating fixes in the 9.4.0/9.5.0 development builds: the per-task tree
writer lock (BL428 Phase 2, `internal/autonomous/tree_lock.go`) and the
PRD-level same-tree admission gate (BL469, `internal/autonomous/tree_admission.go`),
plus the ci-watch own-commit pin (BL423, `internal/autonomous/ci_watch.go`).

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |

| Lock path — `.datawatch/tree.lock` under the canonical base for direct keys, under the worktree root for worktree keys, one shared file for base+worktree | **Yes** (`TestTreeLockPathMainCheckout`, `TestTreeLockPathWorktree`, `TestTreeLockPathSharedBaseOneFile`) | No | `go test`, path assertion on resolved keys | — |

| `refuse_dirty_tree_start` gate — dirty tree refused (names count + options); clean tree admitted; gate off allows dirty; missing tree skips the gate | **Yes** (`TestExecutorTreeLockDirtyTreeRefused`, `TestExecutorTreeLockCleanTreeAdmitted`, `TestExecutorTreeLockGateOffAllowsDirty`, `TestExecutorTreeLockMissingTreeSkips`) | No | `go test`, real `git status --porcelain` on seeded dirty/clean repos | PRD-level override `PRD.RefuseDirtyTreeStart *bool` wins over the daemon's global key when set |

| Incident-shape regression — three PRDs, one tree: one admitted, others refused at admission; no interleaved commits; no release-bump collision (each release task's version increment lands in its own commit, in order) | **Yes** (`TestSameTreeThreePRDsSerialize`, `TestSameTreeConcurrentReleaseBumpsDoNotCollide` in `internal/autonomous/same_tree_serialization_test.go`) | **Yes** | `go test`, real git repos, three concurrent `Manager.Run` callers (production kick shape), commit log + HEAD assertions; the release-bump test pins `9.1.2` (three sequential bumps from `9.1.0`) vs the incident's single-stale-read bump | Commenting out `admitTree` makes the first test red; commenting out `holdTree` makes the second red — both layers pinned |

## Automata lifecycle outbound webhook sink and peer forwarding — signed HTTPS delivery, allow-list and SSRF guard, bounded retry, federation peer forwarding with loop prevention, config keys and surfaces — Unreleased, shipped disabled (Phase 5 of plans/2026-10-13-prd-lifecycle-events.md)

Both sinks ship disabled (`autonomous.notify.webhook.enabled`, `autonomous.notify.forwarding.enabled` default `false`). Every row below is Tested=Yes from the Go or `node --test` suites named in it, and Validated=No until the live smoke run for that row is performed. Rows the smoke saw say which part under Notes.

**Run provenance (2026-10-25):** evidence is in `docs/testing/runs/lifecycle-webhook-smoke-2026-10-25/`. Both runs used a sandbox daemon built with `go build` from commit `f1d0ceaa` with a clean tree (0 uncommitted paths in both `environment.txt` and `smoke-run.txt`); the later commits change only this tracker and the evidence files, no daemon code. The sandbox has isolated data and home directories and free loopback ports, with a throwaway receiver on 127.0.0.1, on Linux with Go 1.27.2. Run 1, direct: `scripts/release-smoke-lifecycle-webhook.sh` in fresh-sandbox mode (`smoke-run.txt`, `environment.txt`, `forwarding-tests.txt`), all eight steps PASS. Run 2, through the story wrapper in `scripts/test-stories/`: sourced once the way the runner does, against a sandbox daemon started by hand from the same commit, existing-sandbox mode (`story-wrapper-run.txt`), all eight steps PASS and the story result is pass; that mode cannot read the daemon log, so the daemon-log secret scan is in run 1 only. The verification gate run on the final committed tree is saved as `verify-gate-run.txt` in the same directory.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outbound target guard — allow-list match (exact host or host:port, case-insensitive, no wildcards, empty list allows nothing), URL policy (https only, http only for an allow-listed host, no userinfo, no obfuscated IP spellings), address classes (loopback, link-local, private, Tailscale CGNAT refused unless allow-listed; cloud metadata refused even when allow-listed), dial-time IP re-check against DNS rebinding, redirects never followed, proxy environment ignored, response body capped | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/lifecycle_webhook_guard_test.go`) | No | `go test` with an injected resolver and `httptest` servers; no real DNS | **Observed 2026-10-25 (fresh sandbox):** an allow-listed receiver got the delivery; a host that is not on the list and the cloud metadata address were each refused with 400 at creation; with the list emptied a test-fire was refused and made zero requests at the receiver. **LIVE pending:** a private-address target refused at delivery time and audited as `refused`. Evidence: `smoke-run.txt`. |
| Request signer — `t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` = HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<raw body>`, constant-time verification, replay window in both directions, malformed and duplicate fields rejected, errors never echo the header, body or secret | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/lifecycle_webhook_sign_test.go`) | **Yes** (live-covered part only; the rest is unit-test only, see Notes) | `go test` with a fixed clock | **Validated 2026-10-25 (fresh sandbox, live part only):** the receiver snippet copied from the how-to (executed from the document text itself) accepted the signature of a real delivery, rejected the same request with one byte of the body changed, and rejected a wrong secret; the first delivery's signature also verified against the stored secret and the envelope parsed. **Unit-test only, not observed live:** the replay window in both directions, rejection of malformed and duplicate fields, the constant-time comparison, and the rule that errors never echo the header, body or secret. Evidence: `docs/testing/runs/lifecycle-webhook-smoke-2026-10-25/smoke-run.txt` (step 4) and `story-wrapper-run.txt` (same checks through the wrapper). |
| Webhook sender — 2xx delivered; 408, 429, 5xx and transport errors retried on the configured delay curve with jitter; `Retry-After` honoured on 429; 3xx and other 4xx permanent; over-size envelope loses `decision`/`verdict` then is refused if still too large; secret resolved on every delivery and never stored, logged or audited; one alert and one final audit record on a dropped delivery; context cancel stops retries | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/lifecycle_webhook_sink_test.go`) | No | `go test` with `httptest` receivers, injected clock, sleep and secret resolver. Live: sandbox daemon built from this tree, HTTPS on 127.0.0.1 on its own free ports, started for the run; the receiver is a Python `http.server` on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port | **Observed 2026-10-25 (fresh sandbox):** 2xx delivered (one signed POST, one delivery id); a receiver answering `500`, `500`, `200` got three attempts with one delivery id and gaps of 1.07s and 2.06s (backoff shortened to 1s, 2s for the run), audit `retry=2,delivered=1`; a stopped receiver got five attempts, audit `retry=4,failed=1` on the delivery and `failed=1` on the final-failure record, and one alert named the subscription and the five attempts; the secret value was absent from API responses, the audit file, the daemon log and every request the receiver captured. **LIVE pending:** `408`, `429` with `Retry-After`, the over-size envelope and context cancel against a live receiver (the run used `500`, one of the 5xx statuses). Validated stays No until those are observed. Evidence: `smoke-run.txt`. |

## Autonomous PRD Split Planning/Execution Backend (v8.20.0)

Added in v8.20.0. Separates the PRD planning backend (`decomposition_profile`, used by Decompose/DecomposeStreaming) from the task-execution backend (`backend`, used by autonomous task session spawning). Resolution order (v8.33.9 priority fix): `prd.DecompositionProfile` (per-PRD, wins) → `manager.cfg.PlanningBackend` (global fallback) → `"ollama"` default. Any registered LLM works for planning — opencode/claude-code spawn a full session with codebase tool access; ollama/openwebui run headless. CLI `prd-set-llm` gained `--decomposition-profile` flag in v8.33.9.

`POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_llm` — extended with `decomposition_profile` field (validated against inference registry). Available on all surfaces: REST, MCP (`autonomous_prd_set_llm`), CLI (`prd-set-llm --decomposition-profile`), PWA Settings modal, Android/iPhone (via REST).

## PWA Current-Status No-Change Contract (v8.19.8)

`GET /api/sessions/{id}/current-status` — changed in v8.19.8 from HTTP 204 (empty body) to HTTP 200 + JSON `{"no_change":true}` on the two no-op branches (no new output; thin delta). Root cause: RFC 7231 §3.3 forbids a body on 204; Go's `net/http` silently drops it; PWA's `r.json()` threw `Unexpected end of JSON input`. `apiFetch` also hardened to resolve 204/205 → null.

chunks.body:
## Multi-provider web search registry (BL391, v8.39.0)

Rewritten in v8.39.0 from the single-provider SearXNG-only design (v8.22.0/BL372).
`internal/websearch` now holds a provider-agnostic `Registry` (SearXNG + Brave
Search API, tried in priority order, extensible), an internal result cache, and
a SQLite usage-tracking store, shared in-process by REST/MCP/stats and by the
standalone `datawatch mcp-search` subprocess (`internal/mcp/search/`, injected
into opencode/goose sessions). The pre-BL391 rows below (`frameScanner`,
`searxngSearch()`, `TestHandleToolsCallNoURL`, etc.) described functions that
no longer exist after the rewrite — this section replaces them.

| Component | Unit tested | Live tested | Unit test coverage | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| PWA Dashboard "Search Usage" card (`_dashRenderWebSearchUsage`) | No | **Pending** | — | Live: Dashboard tab, new `websearch-usage` card in `DASH_CARD_DEFS` |
| PWA Monitor tab "Search Usage" stat card + history modal (`refreshWebSearchStatsCard`, `webSearchOpenHistoryView`) | No | **Pending** | — | Live: Monitor tab, replaces the old flat BL372 web-search tile |
| Config auto-migration — legacy `web_search.{provider,url,engine,num_results}` → synthesized `providers: [{name: "default", ...}]` | **Yes** | No | Covered by `internal/config` package tests (`applyDefaults` migration logic) | Preserves pre-BL391 `config.yaml` files without a manual edit |
| **End-to-end: real search through opencode + direct `mcp-search`, cache + usage verified live** | — | **Yes (2026-10-02, live on this host, v8.39.0)** | — | Operator-requested verification, done against the production daemon after rebuild+restart: (1) direct NDJSON `mcp-search` round-trip — identical repeated query recorded `cache_hit=0` then `cache_hit=1` in `websearch.db`, confirmed via `/api/websearch/stats` and `/api/websearch/history`; (2) `POST /api/websearch/providers/brave-fallback/test` — live Brave Search API call succeeded (3 real results); (3) `POST /api/websearch/providers/searxng-primary/test` — live SearXNG call succeeded; (4) a real opencode session (via `POST /api/sessions/start`) calling the actually-exposed `searxng_web_search` tool (see the injection-caveat row above) round-tripped through the same `Registry` → recorded to `websearch.db`. chunks.body:
## PWA WebSocket liveness watchdog (operator-reported 2026-10-06) — v8.61.2

Operator: "sent a command after being idle for a few minutes and had to exit the session and go back in for it to start moving again." Root cause: `ws.readyState` can stay `OPEN` after a NAT/proxy silently drops an idle TCP mapping — no `close`/`error` event ever fires (nothing on the wire tells the browser), so `scheduleReconnect()` — which only ran from those two event handlers — never triggered. The daemon's `MsgPing`→`pong` handler already existed (`internal/server/api.go`) but the PWA client never sent one.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_wsIsStale(lastActivityAt, now)` — pure staleness decision (no I/O) | **Yes** | No | 4 tests in `internal/server/web/app-ws-watchdog.test.js`: fresh activity not stale, exactly-at-threshold not yet stale (boundary is strict `>`), just-over-threshold is stale, minutes-of-silence (the reported scenario) is stale | Extracted from the `setInterval` callback specifically so it's testable — the stub browser environment this test suite uses no-ops `setInterval` entirely |
| `_wsSendPing()` — sends `{"type":"ping"}` only when `readyState === OPEN` | **Yes** | No | 2 tests: sends when OPEN, does nothing (and doesn't throw) when CONNECTING or `state.ws` is `null` | — |
| Full round trip: client ping → server pong → `wsLastActivityAt` refreshed | No | **Yes** | Playwright against a real daemon: captured actual WS frames over a real 20s `WS_PING_INTERVAL_MS` cycle — confirmed exactly one `{"type":"ping"}` sent and one `{"type":"pong"}` received | — |
| Watchdog forces a reconnect when activity truly stops (simulating a dead-but-still-OPEN socket) | No | **Yes** | Playwright: froze `state.wsLastActivityAt` via a property getter/setter that swallows all writes (a naive one-time backdate isn't a valid simulation — the daemon's 5s periodic `stats` broadcast would overwrite it before the watchdog's next tick, which is in fact why the first version of this live test gave a false negative and had to be corrected to actually block every frame, not just pings, from refreshing the clock). Confirmed: the stale connection closed and a fresh one opened within one `WS_PING_INTERVAL_MS` tick. | Live test script not retained (ad hoc verification, deleted after use per the project's temp-file convention) — the pure-function unit tests above pin the same decision logic permanently |

fixed by making the hook synchronous rather than left as a known-accepted risk | Full repo suite green | Found and fixed two real gaps mid-implementation, not just the planned feature: (1) a genuine `-race` data race from mutating the shared, unsynchronized `*PRD` pointer in a background goroutine after `Run()` had already returned — confirmed the same pattern is pre-existing elsewhere in this file and the project's CI doesn't gate on `-race`, but fixed this instance anyway since going synchronous was cheap and git push + `gh pr create` are fast bounded calls; (2) `git worktree remove` refuses to delete a worktree with uncommitted changes, which is the *expected* case whenever `session.auto_git_commit` is off (true on this very deployment) — fixed with `--force` on removal plus forcing `auto_git_commit:true` specifically for worktree-mode task sessions, so the branch isn't silently empty in the first place |
| BL407 Phase 3 — cluster-mode git: worker-side commit/push + completion callback (new `agents.PushOnCompletion` in `internal/agents/worker_clone.go`; `AgentResult.Branch`/`CommitSHA`; `runWorkerBootstrapTask` forces `auto_git_commit:true` + pushes on completion; `autonomousVerify` captures the reported branch/URL/provider/base-branch onto `prd.Git`; new `Manager.handleClusterCompletion` + shared `openCompletionPR` helper in `git_completion.go`; `handleWorktreeCompletion` gains a `ClusterProfile` guard) | **Yes** (2 new tests in `internal/agents/worker_clone_test.go`: no-op when never git-bootstrapped, a real bare-remote round trip — clone, commit, push, confirm the remote actually received it; 6 new tests in new `internal/autonomous/cluster_completion_test.go`: `handleClusterCompletion`'s branch/AutoPR/URL guards, successful PR-open from a reported branch, `OpenPR` failure records a Decision, and `handleWorktreeCompletion`'s new no-op for `ClusterProfile != ""`) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (3462+ passed), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec -severity high -confidence medium` zero new findings, `go test -race` on this phase's new tests clean, `gofmt` clean on every new/touched file (one genuine misalignment introduced by this phase's own edit to `cmd/datawatch/main.go`, fixed; everything else flagged confirmed pre-existing via `git stash` diffing) | Full repo suite green | No new operator-facing REST/MCP/CLI/comm/PWA surface — worker-to-parent plumbing only (`AgentResult.Branch`/`CommitSHA` ride the existing Phase 0 result-report callback), same as Phase 0; no Mobile-Parity issue needed. Known, accepted limitation carried forward to Phase 4: nothing here creates a *dedicated* branch for cluster-mode tasks the way Phase 1's `EnsureWorktree` does for worktree mode — a cluster worker pushes to whatever branch its Project Profile's `GitSpec` names, or that repo's default branch if unset, until Phase 4 extends `CloneOnBootstrap` with a create-new-branch mode |
| **B115** — e2e cookbook (`docs/testing/v9.0.0/cookbook.md`, TS-### stories) had zero coverage for any of the 21 releases between the v9.0.0 tag and v9.0.21 (confirmed via `git log --diff-filter=A -- scripts/test-stories/` and a full-text grep of all 692 story scripts for `BL406`/`BL407`/the v9.0.1-21 strings — zero matches) | **Yes** — 9 new real REST-driven e2e stories (TS-787–TS-795) backfilling BL406 Phases 0/1/2/3/5, v9.0.3's federation-aware PWA orphan card, v9.0.16's `notify_exclude`, and B113's scan-config round-trip; see `docs/testing/v9.0.0/cookbook.md`'s new "B115 backfill" section for the per-story mapping | **Yes** — all 9 run together against a real sandbox daemon (`bash scripts/run-tests.sh --stories=TS-787,TS-788,TS-789,TS-790,TS-791,TS-792,TS-793,TS-794,TS-795 --serial`): 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Two (TS-789, TS-793) needed `conflict:llm` after discovering live that a `draft`-status PRD rejects `add_story`/`add_task` — fixed by decomposing for real just to cross that gate, then asserting against our own controlled story/task text, not the LLM's output | 9/9 passed | Explicitly NOT backfilled (documented in the cookbook's own "Known gaps" table, not silently missing): BL406 Phase 4 (would file a real GitHub issue if run automatically), BL407 Phase 0/B114 (real cluster-dispatch terminal-state regression — needs a worker container image this harness doesn't have), BL407 Phases 1-3 (no REST/MCP/CLI/PWA exposure yet — that's this same plan's Phase 5), v9.0.7/v9.0.8 (would need to restart the shared sandbox daemon mid-suite), v9.0.10 (YAML-only, no REST surface), and the pure build/release/docs-only v9.0.x patches |
| BL407 Phase 4 — branch creation parity for cluster mode (`Manager.Run` assigns `prd.Git.Branch` for cluster-dispatched PRDs the same idempotent way Phase 1's `EnsureWorktree` does for worktree mode; new `SpawnRequest.Branch` threaded through `autonomousSpawn` as `agents.SpawnRequest.Branch`; `handleAgentBootstrap` now reads `agent.Branch` instead of silently dropping it via `proj.Git.Branch`; new `BootstrapGit.CreateBranch` — `CloneOnBootstrap` clones the default branch + `checkout -b` instead of `--branch <not-yet-existing>`; new `IsWorkspaceLockError` + extended `capacityRetrySpawn`) | **Yes** (2 new tests in `internal/server/agent_api_test.go`: explicit branch → `CreateBranch:true`, no explicit branch → unaffected `CreateBranch:false`; 1 new test in `internal/agents/worker_clone_test.go`: a real local-git round trip proving clone-default+checkout-b, then a simulated worker restart landing back on the same branch without erroring — caught and fixed a real bug live, `git pull --ff-only` hard-failing against a local-only branch with no upstream; 2 new tests in new `internal/autonomous/cluster_branch_test.go`: `Run()` assigns + threads the branch, idempotency across a simulated resume; 2 new tests in `internal/autonomous/capacity_test.go`: `TestCapacity_WorkspaceLockErrorIsWaitNotFailure`, `TestIsWorkspaceLockError`) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green, `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec -severity high -confidence medium` zero new findings on any touched file, `gofmt` clean on every new/touched file (6 files flagged were confirmed pre-existing cascading struct-literal drift via `git stash` diffing — identical flagged-file set before and after this phase's edits) | Full repo suite green | No new operator-facing REST/MCP/CLI/comm/PWA surface — `agents.SpawnRequest.Branch` already existed (F10 S7.3's workspace-lock field); this phase is the first caller to give it a real per-PRD value. Found and fixed a real concurrency bug this phase's own design would otherwise have introduced: concurrent tasks on one PRD now share one branch, which the pre-existing workspace lock would have rejected as a hard failure — fixed by making it retryable the same way a capacity-full wait already is, not by bypassing the lock. Known, accepted cosmetic quirk: a workspace-lock wait shows `waiting_capacity` the same as a real GPU-capacity wait, reusing the existing status/wait-reason surface rather than adding a new enum value |
| BL407 Phase 5 — config/parity surface (new `Manager.SetPRDGit` sets `PRD.Git.AutoPR`/`BaseBranch` unconditionally via `set_git` REST action/`autonomous_prd_set_git` MCP/`prd-set-git` CLI; new `autonomous.Config.DefaultAutoPR` applied once at `CreatePRD` time + YAML-facing mirror + daemon-startup bridge + `GET/PUT /api/config`/`/api/autonomous/config`/`autonomous_config_set` surface; PWA PRD Settings gains a Git section) | **Yes** (4 new tests in new `internal/autonomous/git_config_surface_test.go`: `SetPRDGit` sets + fully replaces both fields, not-found error, `DefaultAutoPR` applied at creation, no-default leaves `AutoPR` false) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (83 packages), `node --test internal/server/web/*.test.js` 182/182 green, `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec -severity high -confidence medium` zero new findings on any touched file, `gofmt` clean on every new/touched file (one genuine misalignment of my own in `internal/mcp/server.go`'s inline-comment column, fixed; everything else flagged confirmed pre-existing via `git stash` diffing) | Full repo suite green | Found and fixed live: the new MCP tool needed its own `federation.MCPToolCap` entry or `POST /api/mcp/call` 404s it as unknown despite being registered — caught by `TestEveryUnconditionallyRegisteredToolHasAnMCPToolCapEntry`; the `AutonomousAPI` interface's new method needed a trivial stub on the shared `fakeOrchAutonomous` test double (5 other fakes embed it, inherited for free); the new PWA Git-section hint text first said "PRD" and left "automaton" untranslated in 4 locale bundles, caught by `TestLocales_PRDNeverUserFacing`/`TestLocales_AutomatonNeverUntranslatedOrMistranslated` before shipping. Deliberately did NOT add comm-channel parity for `set_git` — that whole class of single-field PRD setters has never had comm-channel coverage in this codebase; adding it only here would invent new symmetry beyond what the plan asked to mirror. Mobile-Parity issue filed: `datawatch-app#249` |
| **B116** — `PUT /api/config`'s BL369 `autonomous.*` propagation (`internal/server/api.go`) marshaled the *entire* `s.cfg.Autonomous` struct and merged it onto the live `autonomous.Manager` config on every write, not just the touched key; four deliberately-no-`omitempty` bool fields (`AutoApproveChildren`, `PerStoryApproval`, `ContinueOnStoryFailure`, `InjectionGuard`/`BlockOnInjection`) are therefore always present in that marshal, so an unrelated write silently clobbered a live-only `true` default back to the YAML zero-value `false` (found live via `auto_approve_children`) | **Yes** (3 new tests in new `internal/server/autonomous_config_propagation_test.go`: only the touched top-level field is forwarded, a nested dot-path key like `default_quality_gates.enabled` forwards the whole parent object correctly, a patch with no `autonomous.*` key triggers zero propagation calls) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (69 packages), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec -severity high -confidence medium` zero new findings on the touched file (confirmed via `git stash` diffing), `gofmt` clean on the new test file (pre-existing drift on `api.go` confirmed via the same diffing) | Full repo suite green | Found live 2026-10-11 while setting `autonomous.worktree_base_repo` ahead of running BL404 as a real PRD; confirmed via the audit log that only the intended key was logged as changed while the live value visibly diverged. Fixed by scoping the propagated JSON to only the top-level field(s) this specific `PUT` touched, read from the already-type-converted config (not raw patch values, which may still be wire-format strings/CSV for array fields) |
| **B117** — `POST /api/autonomous/prds` hard-rejected a PRD with no `project_dir`/`project_profile` even when `autonomous.worktree_base_repo` is configured for exactly that case (BL407 Phase 1's worktree auto-assignment never got a chance to run at `Run()` time) | **Yes** (4 new tests in new `internal/server/autonomous_prd_create_worktree_test.go`: rejected when worktree mode isn't configured, allowed and `project_dir` passed through empty when it is, `cluster_profile` alone still rejected even with worktree mode configured, an explicit `project_dir` is unaffected) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (69 packages), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec -severity high -confidence medium` zero new findings near the touched lines, `gofmt` clean on the new test file (pre-existing drift on `autonomous.go` confirmed via `git stash` diffing) | Full repo suite green | Found live 2026-10-11 while creating BL404's PRD, the deliberate first real shakedown of worktree mode — confirmed the condition was unreachable through any surface (REST/MCP/CLI/comm/PWA all proxy through the one `POST /api/autonomous/prds` handler), not just an MCP-specific gap |
| **B118** — session-based decompose needs a real `project_dir` just like `Run()` does, but BL407 Phase 1's worktree auto-creation only fired at `Run()` time (after decompose) — a worktree-mode PRD could never successfully decompose; also added orphan-worktree cleanup on `Reject()`/`Archive()`, found missing in the same investigation (new `ensureWorktreeIfConfigured`/`cleanupOrphanedWorktree` shared helpers) | **Yes** (6 new tests in new `internal/autonomous/worktree_decompose_test.go`: `Decompose` creates a worktree, `DecomposeStreaming` too, `Run()` reuses the same worktree decompose created rather than making a second one, `Reject` cleans up a clean worktree, `Reject` leaves one with uncommitted content alone, `Archive` is the universal backstop for a cancelled PRD's worktree) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (69 packages), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec -severity high -confidence medium` zero new findings near touched lines, `gofmt` clean on every new/touched file (pre-existing drift on 4 files confirmed via `git stash` diffing) | Full repo suite green | Found live 2026-10-11 creating BL404's own PRD — the deliberate first real shakedown of worktree mode immediately surfaced this. Fixing it also closed a drifted-duplicate risk between `Decompose()`/`DecomposeStreaming()` already flagged as a prior bug source in their own code comments, by extracting one shared gate instead of hand-copying a third time |
| **B119** — `autonomous.execution_backend` (BL203's daemon-wide fallback execution backend) existed as a live `internal/autonomous.Config` field with zero config surface anywhere — not YAML, not `PUT /api/config`, not the daemon-startup bridge | **Yes** (1 new test in `internal/server/autonomous_config_patch_test.go`: `applyConfigPatch` round-trip) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green, `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec` zero new findings, `gofmt` clean | Full repo suite green | Found live 2026-10-11 while making Claude the daemon default backend for real PRD-driven development work — wired the same minimal 3-layer pattern as every other `autonomous.*` field this session; MCP-tool/PWA-specific surface deliberately deferred, same shape as BL404 itself |
| **B120** — B116's own scoped-propagation fix omitted an explicit clear-to-zero on a touched `autonomous.*` field (e.g. `planning_model: ""`) since a zero-valued omitempty field is absent from a normal struct marshal entirely, so the clear never reached the live manager | **Yes** (1 new test in `internal/server/autonomous_config_propagation_test.go`: an explicit clear-to-zero on a pre-populated field is forwarded as an explicit empty string) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (69 packages), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec` zero new findings near touched lines, `gofmt` clean on the new test code (pre-existing drift on `api.go` confirmed via `git stash` diffing) | Full repo suite green | Found live 2026-10-11 minutes after v9.0.26 shipped, while actually using the config surface just built to switch `autonomous.planning_backend` to `claude-code` — immediately exercising the new code surfaced the gap |
| **B121** — `autonomous.rules_file`/`context_file` (BL406) had full config read/write plumbing but zero consumers; the plan's own "decomposer/scanner both read it" claim was never implemented despite all 6 phases marked Done | **Yes** (6 new tests in new `internal/autonomous/rules_context_test.go`: empty project_dir, default filenames, missing optional context file, custom filenames, oversized-file cap, and an end-to-end Decompose() test proving AGENT.md content actually reaches the planning prompt) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (69 packages), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec` zero new findings, `gofmt` clean on new files (pre-existing drift on `manager.go` confirmed via `git stash` diffing) | Full repo suite green | Found live 2026-10-11 auditing BL404's real completed run after an operator challenge about whether AGENT.md/DATAWATCH-CONTEXT.md rules are actually enforced. Fixed the decomposer half immediately; the scanner half needs a genuinely new diff-aware rule type and is correctly deferred as **BL413** rather than improvised. Also independently demonstrated the *existing* scanner engine already works for structured checks with zero new code: configured a real `version-sync` consistency rule (`cmd/datawatch/main.go` vs `internal/server/api.go`) and proved it both passes clean against this repo and catches a deliberate mismatch, with no PRD involved |
| **B122** — B121's own large-prompt injection (~160KB) exposed a tmux send-keys timing race: a flat 10ms inter-chunk delay / 120ms trailing settle, never exercised beyond one chunk before today, corrupted the receiving TUI's input rendering (~13 unexpanded `[Pasted text #N]` placeholders) and the trailing Enter never registered | **Yes** (7 new tests in new `internal/session/tmux_large_payload_test.go`: settle scaling single-chunk-unchanged/scales-with-count/caps-at-max, an exact 4-chunk reproduction proving every chunk is sent then Enter, and exact-chunk-count parametrized cases at 2/5/13/20 chunks matching the real failure's scale) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (69 packages), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec` zero new findings, `gofmt` clean on new files (pre-existing drift on `tmux.go` confirmed via `git stash` diffing) | Full repo suite green | Found live within minutes of B121 shipping, kicking off BL403 Phase 1 as a real PRD — the first decompose call ever large enough to exercise this chunking path at more than 1-2 chunks. The stuck PRD was cancelled (`autonomous_prd_cancel`) and its orphaned tmux session cleaned up separately (`kill_session` — `Cancel()`'s own session-kill step reported 0 killed, since decompose sessions aren't tracked in the normal per-task session list; a smaller, separate gap not fixed in this pass) before restarting with the fix in place |
| **B121 revised** — v9.0.28's fix inlined full `AGENT.md`/`DATAWATCH-CONTEXT.md` content (~160KB) into the decompose prompt, which directly triggered B122's tmux chunked-paste corruption; B122's timing fix alone wasn't sufficient (confirmed live: a second, larger inlined prompt still corrupted claude-code's input at ~26 chunks) | **Yes** (rewrote `internal/autonomous/rules_context_test.go` for pointer-only behavior: tiny suffix even for a 200KB file, content never inlined, only mentions files that actually exist, end-to-end Decompose() test proving a 50KB seeded AGENT.md never appears verbatim in the prompt) | **Yes** — full `go test ./...` green (69 packages), `go vet ./...` clean, `gosec` zero new findings, `gofmt` clean on touched files | Full repo suite green | Found live within minutes of restarting BL403 Phase 1's decompose with B122's fix in place — the operator's own question ('do we need to directly inject... or just point to the files?') identified the root-cause fix directly. Also confirmed decompose already reuses the same one-shot session delivery path (`POST /api/sessions/start`, `one_shot: true`) every other one-shot task uses — not a bespoke code path, per Reuse-and-Expand |
| BL404 — imap_mcp messaging channel config parity (new `imap_mcp.*` applyConfigPatch cases mirroring the `ntfy.token` mask-preservation precedent; new `imap_mcp` section on `GET /api/config`; PWA Comms Settings card via the existing `BACKEND_FIELDS` renderer) | **Yes** (`internal/server/applyconfigpatch_imap_mcp_test.go`: all six keys, token preservation on `""`/`"***"`, skipped-key exclusion, `GET /api/config` masking; `internal/server/web/app-imap-mcp-settings.test.js`: `BACKEND_FIELDS` shape, both backend-list arrays) | **Yes** — real PRD-driven run through the new BL407 branch-per-PRD workflow (worktree-mode decompose + execution via claude-code, auto-PR on completion); independently re-verified in a fresh worktree from the pushed branch: `go build`/`go vet` clean, full `go test ./...` 69/69 packages, `node --test` 186/186 | Full repo suite green | First real shakedown of BL407's PRD-driven git workflow (Stage 2 of the v10.0.0 roadmap). Decompose needed BL407 Phase 1's worktree auto-creation extended to fire at decompose time too (found live, fixed as B118) and a creation-time validation gap fixed (B117) before the PRD could even be created. The per-task LLM verifier proved unreliable in both directions (an `ok:true` task's `issues` list contained 3 factually false complaints about content that was actually present and correct, confirmed by reading the real diff) — don't trust its `issues` text as a QA signal, only independent verification. PR: [#205](https://github.com/dmz006/datawatch/pull/205) |

chunks.body:
## Guardrail verdict decision log

Every guardrail verdict, judged or deterministic, is now recorded as a `guardrail_verdict`
Decision on the Automaton. A blocked Automaton also says why it is blocked. This is a
server-side change only; no client displays it yet.

Contract changes:

- `blocked_reason` (string, `omitempty`) on automaton objects (`PRD.BlockedReason`). It is set only
  while the automaton is blocked by a guardrail verdict. It is cleared when the automaton leaves a
  blocked status.
- `judge_session_id` (string, `omitempty`) on decision entries (`Decision`) and on guardrail verdicts
  (`GuardrailVerdict`). It names the session that ran the guardrail judge.
- `judge_output_path` (string, `omitempty`) on guardrail verdicts (`GuardrailVerdict`). It names the
  judge output file, which is kept until the verdict save succeeds.
- New decision kind `guardrail_verdict`, appended by `recordGuardrailVerdict` at the four guardrail
  sites: task-level, per-story, rules-review and ci-watch.

## Model/backend pairing — endpoint contract change

Changed endpoint contract. The PRD create, PRD LLM, story LLM, task LLM and
verification/guardrail set endpoints now return `400` with the mismatch text
when a model does not pair with its backend (a bare Claude alias on `pi` or
`pi-prompt`, or a provider-tagged model on `claude-code`). Before this change
they accepted the pair and the session later exited with no output. A PRD

## Reactive usage back-off — Phase 4 surfaces, admission gate and staleness guard — unreleased

A per-backend, in-memory flag (`internal/autonomous/backoff.go`) that holds autonomous dispatch to a rate-limited backend; set automatically on `StateRateLimited` and by operators, cleared at the parsed reset time or after `autonomous.backoff_max_wait_minutes`. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md`. Howto: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md` (`## Reactive usage backoff`). chunks.body:
## BL428 Phase 5 — per-LLM dollar-window budget (ceiling, ledger, admission gate, surfaces, peer opt-in) — unreleased

An LLM entry gains an optional `budget` (a dollar ceiling over a rolling `hours` window or a weekly `weekday` + `time` + `zone` window). A persisted spend ledger (`<data_dir>/autonomous/budget-ledger.jsonl`) is fed by a usage-event hook in the session cost path; when the window is full, autonomous admission for that LLM waits with the reason `budget window full: …` and resumes by itself when the window rolls over. Interactive session starts are never gated. `allocation_pct` is an opt-in, always-estimated share-of-allocation figure and never blocks. Peer spend counts only for peers named in `peer_window` (off by default) and fails open. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md` (Phase 5). Howto: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md` (`## Per-LLM dollar budget`). Live rows stay No until a sandbox daemon run.

| `allocation_pct` is estimated, informational and never blocks — `estimated: true`, `basis` text, nothing declared reports no figure | **Yes** (`TestBudgetAllocationPctEstimatedNeverBlocks` in `internal/autonomous/budget_test.go`) | **No** | Fake clock, allocation table | Admission never reads the figure |

chunks.body:
## BL431 Phase 5: Automation BudgetPolicy — unreleased

An Automation carries an optional `budget_policy` (dollar ceiling, window, pacing, on-breach rule, reset anchors, optional allocation estimate, optional opted-in peers), and a member may carry a narrower override plus an `estimated_cost_usd`. A pure evaluator (`AutomationBudget`, `internal/autonomous/automation_budget.go`) reads the shared cost rollup (`PRDCostUSD` / `AutomationSpendUSD`, built on the existing spend ledger — no second ledger). The coordinator checks it before it starts any member (advance, activation entry, fork) and the admit hook holds new member tasks at a dollar ceiling. On a breach the Automation pauses and resumes by itself at the window rollover only when the reset time is known, otherwise it goes to blocked and waits for the operator; an alert is raised either way. `allocation_pct` is an optional estimate and never gates. Another daemon's spend counts only for peers named in `peer_window`, without automatic confirmation. Surfaces: `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_budget`, MCP `automation_set_budget`, `datawatch automation set-budget`, comm `automation set-budget`; the computed `budget` view on `automation_get` / `automation_list` / `GET /api/automations/{id}` and on each `autonomous_status` Automation row; audit events `automation_set_budget`, `automation_budget_breach`, `automation_budget_resumed`. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (Phase 5). Howto: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md` (`## Automation spending limit`). All time-dependent tests use an injected clock.

**Live validation status: no live daemon smoke has been run for this phase.** Every Validated cell below is No and stays No until a sandbox daemon run exercises each row (set a small ceiling on an Automation, run members, and watch the pause, the automatic resume and the block). The unit tests drive a real `Manager`, `Coordinator` and httptest server with fake clocks, but not a running daemon with real sessions and real spend.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |

| Spend rollup across members — one shared per-Automaton cost (task, decompose and verifier sessions), limited to a window with `since`, summed over every member Automaton and recursively over nested Automations; lifetime falls back to session totals | **Yes** (`TestPRDCostUSDSumsTaskDecomposeAndVerifySessions`, `TestPRDCostUSDSinceExcludesEarlierSpend`, `TestAutomationSpendSumsMemberCostRecords`, `TestAutomationSpendLifetimeFallsBackToSessionTotals` in `internal/autonomous/automation_cost_test.go`) | **No** | Real `Manager` and spend ledger, fake clock | Peer spend is never part of this rollup. Live: run two members on a sandbox daemon and compare `spent_usd` with the sum of the sessions' costs |
| Ledger attributes spend to its session, so the rollup can find it | **Yes** (`TestRecordUsageSpendCarriesSessionID` in `cmd/datawatch/capacity_wiring_budget_test.go`) | **No** | Real budget ledger, fake usage event | The ledger entry carries `session_id` |

| Evaluator — dollar ceiling reached, below ceiling allows, no policy gives the zero verdict, tightest of Automation and member policy wins, a member override narrows the Automation policy | **Yes** (`TestBudgetEvalDollarCeilingReached`, `TestBudgetEvalBelowCeilingAllows`, `TestBudgetEvalNoPolicyZeroVerdict`, `TestBudgetEvalTightestWins`, `TestBudgetEvalMemberOverrideNarrowsAutomation` in `internal/autonomous/automation_budget_test.go`) | **No** | Fake spend entries, fake clock | A policy never widens the per-LLM ceiling |
| Evaluator — even pacing holds a start that is ahead of pace, no pacing spends to the ceiling; a member whose declared (or prior-spend) estimate would cross the ceiling is held; a window rollover clears the breach; the evaluator reads only the injected clock | **Yes** (`TestBudgetEvalPacingEvenHoldsStart`, `TestBudgetEvalPacingNoneSpendsToCeiling`, `TestBudgetEvalMemberEstimateWouldCrossCeiling`, `TestBudgetEvalNoEstimateStartsBelowCeiling`, `TestBudgetEvalWindowRolloverClearsBreach`, `TestBudgetEvalUsesInjectedClock`, `TestBudgetEvalResetAndPeerSeams` in `internal/autonomous/automation_budget_test.go`) | **No** | Fake clock across window edges | A pacing or estimate refusal is a hold, not a breach |

## Visibility, audit and parity close-out — unreleased

Waiting tasks gain a machine-readable wait cause, a plain-language reason, an optional reset time and a holder; running tasks gain their holdings; `GET /api/capacity` gains a `tasks` object (`waiting`, `running`) and `reset_known` on each back-off entry; the session status `automaton` block gains `wait_cause`, `wait_resets_at`, `holds` and `holds_note`. chunks.body:
## BL568 — Resource fingerprint exchange between federated peers (BL428 §3c/§4e) — not released

Two daemons that both opt the other in (the per-peer `fingerprint_sync` flag
on both sides) periodically exchange **hashes** of their shared-resource
fingerprints — compute-node identity from the node itself (GPU UUID, or cloud
instance ID) and the LLM-entry label (`billing_group`) that bills against one
account across peers. A hit becomes a **pending match record**; only when the
operator confirms it do the two daemons treat the resource as one shared pool,
and a confirmed shared compute node means the peer's admitted hold counts
against local admission capacity (peer outage fails open, logs once per
episode). Rejecting keeps (or makes) the resources separate. Raw values
(names, addresses, the billing-group label, tokens) never leave the daemon;
peer-token holders without the `federation:fingerprint` capability (only in
the full-control set) cannot read the exchange endpoint at all. Design doc:
[2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md](plans/2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md)
§"Resource fingerprint exchange (sections 3c and 4e) — shipped"; operator howto:
[federation-fingerprint.md](howto/federation-fingerprint.md).

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Node identity — stable per node across two addresses; different across two nodes; GPU UUID preferred with cloud instance ID fallback; a node with no source is skipped entirely; names and addresses are never inputs | **Yes** (`TestResolveSameNodeTwoAddresses`, `TestResolveDifferentNodesDiffer`, `TestResolvePrefersGPUUUID`, `TestResolveFallsBackToInstanceID`, `TestResolveNoSourceSkipped`, `TestResolveIgnoresNameAndAddress` in `internal/fingerprint/identity_test.go`) | **No** | Pure functions, faked hardware sources | The identity is the node's own value, never an operator-set name |
| Pair key + hashes — the key differs per peer credential; the hash is stable for the same input, different per peer pair (A↔B ≠ A↔C) and per kind (node vs billing group); bad input rejected | **Yes** (`TestPairKeyDiffersPerToken`, `TestHashStableForSameInput`, `TestHashDiffersPerPeerPair`, `TestHashDiffersPerKind`, `TestHashRejectsBadInput` in `internal/fingerprint/hash_test.go`) | **No** | Pure functions | Per-pair hashes are the only identities that leave the daemon — neither side can reverse one into the other's value |
| Node export — entry without identity skipped; `billing_group` hashed in place; no raw field ever in an export item | **Yes** (`TestExportSkipsNodesWithoutIdentity`, `TestExportBillingGroupHashed`, `TestExportItemsCarryNoRawValues` in `internal/fingerprint/export_test.go`) | **No** | Fixed node fixtures | The payload is hashes only |
| Reconciliation (sync side) — a peer that is not opted in is skipped (never contacted); a node match creates a **pending** record and nothing is auto-confirmed; no match, no record; a rejected stays rejected on re-observe; a billing group also makes a match; peer errors fail soft, logged once per episode; the default interval is slow (10 minutes); sync never confirms | **Yes** (`TestSyncSkipsPeerNotOptedIn`, `TestSyncCreatesPendingNodeMatch`, `TestSyncNoMatchNoRecord`, `TestSyncRejectedStaysRejected`, `TestSyncBillingGroupMatch`, `TestSyncPeerErrorFailsSoftLoggedOnce`, `TestSyncIntervalDefaultIsSlow`, `TestSyncNeverConfirms` in `internal/fingerprint/sync_test.go`) | **No** | Fake peer HTTP server, fake clock | The operator decides |
| Match store — create pending; confirm; reject; a rejected stays rejected (a later confirm is refused); observe is idempotent (same match, no duplicate); records persist across reload; unknown id is an error; `shared_with` lists confirmed peers only; the on-decision callback fires | **Yes** (`TestMatchStoreCreatesPending`, `TestMatchStoreConfirm`, `TestMatchStoreReject`, `TestMatchStoreRejectedStaysRejected`, `TestMatchStoreObserveIsIdempotent`, `TestMatchStorePersistsAcrossReload`, `TestMatchStoreUnknownIDErrors`, `TestMatchStoreSharedWithOnlyConfirmed`, `TestMatchStoreOnDecisionFires` in `internal/fingerprint/matches_test.go`) | **No** | In-memory + persistence reload | A confirmed shared node starts counting the peer against local capacity; a reject undoes it |
| Peer gate (admission) — a confirmed shared node adds the peer's hold to the local admission; a peer failure fails open (local spend decides) and logs once per episode; combined held at the limit blocks; **pending** matches never count; peers not opted in never count | **Yes** (`TestPeerGateUnreachableFailsOpen`, `TestPeerGateLogsOncePerEpisode`, `TestPeerGateBlocksWhenCombinedHeldReachesLimit`, `TestPeerGateIgnoresPendingMatch`, `TestPeerGateIgnoresPeerNotOptedIn` in `internal/fingerprint/gate_test.go`) | **No** | Fake peer, real capacity math | A peer outage never stalls local work |
| Responder REST endpoint `GET /api/federation/fingerprints` — capability **and** opt-in required; an admin token without the capability is rejected; the response is per-pair **hashes only**; keying differs per caller | **Yes** (`TestFingerprintEndpointNeedsCapability`, `TestFingerprintEndpointOptInRequired`, `TestFingerprintEndpointAdminTokenRejected`, `TestFingerprintEndpointOnlyHashes`, `TestFingerprintEndpointKeyedPerCaller` in `internal/server/federation_fingerprints_test.go`) | **No** | httptest server | Peer-token holders without the capability cannot even see the endpoint |
| Match routes — `GET /api/federation/fingerprint-matches` (list, `?state=` filter), `POST …/{id}/confirm`, `POST …/{id}/reject`; unknown id 404s; all require the capability | **Yes** (`TestFingerprintMatchesListFilters`, `TestFingerprintMatchConfirm`, `TestFingerprintMatchReject`, `TestFingerprintMatchUnknownID404`, `TestFingerprintMatchesNeedCapability` in `internal/server/federation_fingerprint_matches_test.go`) | **No** | httptest server, real match store | The decision echoes back the updated record |
| Capability model — `federation:fingerprint` is granted only with the full-control set, nowhere else | **Yes** (`TestCapFederationFingerprintOnlyInFullControl` in `internal/federation/capabilities_test.go`) | **No** | Table-driven | The per-peer opt-in rides on top of this |
| MCP tools — `federation_fingerprint_matches` (list, optional `state`), `federation_fingerprint_confirm`, `federation_fingerprint_reject`; capability entries registered on all three | **Yes** (`TestMCPFingerprintList`, `TestMCPFingerprintConfirmReject`, `TestMCPFingerprintToolsHaveCapabilities` in `internal/mcp/federation_fingerprint_test.go`) | **No** | MCP request capture, loopback REST | — |
| CLI — `datawatch federation fingerprint list [--state]`, `… confirm <id>`, `… reject <id>`; `--fingerprint-sync` on `federation peer add|update`; `--billing-group` on `llm add|update` | **Yes** (`TestCLIFingerprintList`, `TestCLIFingerprintConfirmReject` in `cmd/datawatch/cli_fingerprint_test.go`; `TestCLIFederationPeerFingerprintSyncFlag`, `TestCLILLMBillingGroupFlag` in `cmd/datawatch/cli_fingerprint_args_test.go`) | **No** | Command wiring, fake daemon | — |
| Wiring in the daemon — idle by default (no peers, no opt-in); the capacity gate composes the peer gate (local + peer held); a peer error fails open; confirm/reject each write exactly one audit record | **Yes** (`TestFingerprintWiringIdleWithoutOptIn`, `TestCapacityGateComposesPeerGate`, `TestCapacityGateFailsOpenOnPeerError`, `TestFingerprintWiringAuditsDecisions` in `cmd/datawatch/fingerprint_wiring_test.go`) | **No** | Fake peer, recording audit seam | `fingerprint_match_decision` audit events; a pending match is inert until confirmed |
| Comm verbs — `federation peer fingerprint <name> on|off` and `llm … billing_group=<label>` round-trip over loopback; `federation fingerprint list [state]`, `confirm <id>`, `reject <id>`; unknown id or bad input gets a usage reply, no request sent | **Yes** (`TestRouterFederationPeerFingerprintSync`, `TestRouterLLMBillingGroupKey` in `internal/router/fingerprint_args_test.go`; `TestRouterFingerprintList`, `TestRouterFingerprintConfirmReject`, `TestRouterFingerprintUnknownID` in `internal/router/fingerprint_cmd_test.go`) | **No** | Fake loopback server | — |
| PWA — settings markup + functions wired; the pending panel renders each match (kind, local + peer resource, both actions); localized empty state; confirmed matches render collapsed and keep a reject action; a decision posts to the per-match route and the panel reloads; editing a peer is a PUT with `fingerprint_sync` always explicit; adding a peer is a POST with `fingerprint_sync` only when opted in; the toggle pre-fills from the record and defaults off; the LLM form carries a billing-group field that round-trips; all new i18n keys exist in every locale bundle | **Yes** (10 cases in `internal/server/web/app-fingerprint.test.js`) | **No** | jsdom against the built `app.js` | The five locale bundles still carry English placeholders until the translation pass |
| Live two-daemon smoke for this feature | **No** | **No** | — | Not run. Needed: two sandbox daemons behind two addresses of one node (or both labelling one LLM entry with a shared `billing_group`), opt-in on both sides, one pending match, a confirm, then a capacity hold under combined load, and one peer-outage episode (log once, admission unaffected) |

## Readable holder names — capacity endpoint contract — unreleased

`GET /api/capacity` resolves raw holder ids into operator-readable names and adds them **beside** the unchanged raw id fields: `holder_names` on `node:` pools (parallel to the untouched `holders`/`holder`), `holder_name` on each lease and waiting entry, and `readable`/`short_id` beside `task_id` on `tasks.waiting`/`tasks.running` (`readable_reason` next to `reason` for waiting tasks that name holders). The name object carries `id`, `kind`, `task_title`, `prd_id`, `prd_title`, `short_id` and `readable`; the never-truncated long form `full` appears only with `?long=1`. A resolved holder without a title falls back to the raw id in the API and to the localized `(untitled <short id>)` label in the PWA. The session status `automaton` block gains `wait_reason_readable` beside `wait_reason`; the CLI/comm formatter prefers the readable line and falls back to the raw id for older bodies. The `capacity_name_untitled` and `capacity_name_prd` keys exist in all five locale bundles (`en.json`, `de.json`, `es.json`, `fr.json`, `ja.json`) with real translations. The Unit column is Yes for every row below; every Live row stays No until a sandbox daemon click-through of the capacity card.

## Session store and PRD store

One record per session (`sessions.d/`) and per PRD (`autonomous/prds/`), a coalescing background writer, an archive file and a per-field size cap. Operator guide: `docs/operations.md` (Session and PRD storage layout). Plan and numbers: `docs/plans/2026-10-23-session-store-write-amplification.md`.

Unit results, 2026-10-23: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestStore' ./internal/session/` and `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestPRDStore' ./internal/autonomous/` pass with no race reports. The full `go test -race ./internal/autonomous/` passes (27 s). The full `go test -race ./internal/session/` fails 11 tests (`TestOneShot*`, `TestRestart*`, `TestResumeMonitorsAdopts_*`) on data races between the screen-capture goroutine (`manager.go`) and test code reading the session pointer from `store.Get` without a lock; the same tests fail the same way on `main` (checked with `git archive main`), so they are not caused by the store change and are left for a separate fix.

Live validation, 2026-10-23: a daemon built from this branch ran with a throwaway data directory and config, port 18081, no TLS, `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR`, never the production daemon. The data directory started with an old `sessions.json` of four sessions (two finished 30 days ago, two recent). First start: `sessions.json.pre-records.bak` and `sessions.d/LAYOUT` appeared, `sessions.json` was removed, the two old finished sessions moved to `sessions-archive.jsonl`, `GET /api/sessions?view=summary` returned the two recent ones, `?history=1` returned all four, and `GET /api/sessions/<archived id>` returned the archived session. A new shell session created a third record within the flush interval. Creating a PRD with a 90 KB spec wrote `autonomous/prds/<id>.json` and one side file, and `GET` returned the PRD. SIGTERM stop and restart kept every record.

## PRD commit scope: staging bounded to declared write dirs

Changed behavior: a PRD task session's auto-commit stages only the files under the PRD's declared write dirs (the spawn request's write scope, forwarded into the session's `WriteScope`); a worktree-mode PRD's scope is its own worktree; and a direct-mode PRD with no declared write dirs gets no git activity at all (new `prdAutoCommits` gate in `internal/autonomous/executor.go`), so it does not auto-commit the whole project directory. ## Worker idle nudge work-child guard and adopted sessions — unreleased

Operator notes: `cmd/datawatch/session_idle_probe.go` (work-child walk and own-server matching), `internal/autonomous/worker_nudge.go` and `worker_nudge_step.go` (the one nudge decision shared by the fresh and adopted waits), and `internal/autonomous/adopt_wait.go` (adopted-session wait). ## Post-turn nudge for idle claude-code workers — unreleased

Operator notes: `cmd/datawatch/post_turn_nudge.go` (the post-turn wait's nudge unit: the backend family is read on every tick until the session is visible; wait-start and family-resolved lines; the one-time window warning), `cmd/datawatch/worker_nudge_hooks.go` (the hooks shared by the fresh and adopted waits), `cmd/datawatch/end_attribution.go` (idle-detector end reason with the session's nudge history), `internal/autonomous/worker_nudge.go` (idle clock runs from the start of the idle run; the log-file age no longer shortens it), `internal/autonomous/worker_nudge_step.go` (answered and stall log lines, `NudgeStallError`, the stall retry reason) and `internal/session/completion_summary.go` (template placeholders are not completions). Changed behavior: the nudge applies to every claude-code worker in the post-turn wait whatever the task status shows, and a session that is not visible when the wait starts is nudged from its first visible tick. `GET /api/config` returns the effective nudge and stall windows as read-only keys. ## Live held-task review — unreleased

Operator notes: `internal/autonomous/review_wake.go` (the per-Automaton wake channel and its pending flag), `internal/autonomous/api.go` (`ResolveTaskReview` signals a live executor instead of waiting for it, and the run goroutine takes a decision that arrived at exit), and `internal/autonomous/executor.go` (the re-scan in the one-task-at-a-time walk and in the concurrent coordinator). Contract change on REST `resolve_task_review`, MCP `autonomous_prd_resolve_task_review` and CLI `datawatch autonomous resolve-review`: the 400 "executor is still finishing; try again shortly" answer no longer occurs while the Automaton is running, and there is no five second wait. The comm channel command `autonomous review-task` posts to the same REST route and changes in the same way; it has no test of its own for this change. All Go tests below were run and pass. No live connection test was run, so every row stays Validated: No. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-25-live-held-task-review.md`.

## Session tags (own tags, inherited tags, tags route) — unreleased
